text: I stayed here for a weekend and I do not think I would stay here again. The positives this hotel has going for it are its location ( a couple of blocks away from the wonderful Reading Central Terminal, Independence hall, and shopping) and the rooms are nicely appointed. The rooms look recently redone with flat screen televisions and attractive marble bathrooms. Also, each room has a Keureg coffeemaker with delicious complimentary coffee as well as an empty refrigerator. That should make for a nice stay however, the negatives are as follows: 1) There are no king-sized beds in the hotel although there is certainly room for them. No big deal but would be nice. 2) I requested a wake up call and it was never made- this is totally unacceptable. 3) My room was not made up even though I was out of it at 9:00am. At 5:30 pm, the housekeeper finally knocked on my door and asked if I just wanted towels which made me think she wanted to avoid cleaning the room, but I told her, no I want the room cleaned which was eventually done. I found this very unprofessional. 4) This hotel is pet friendly and although they confine pets to one floor I witnessed a dog defecate in the lobby, not far from their fish restaurant. That was pretty gross. 5) The comforter on the bed was entirely too warm for summer, and the extra blanket in the room was a twin, only useful for one person. 6) There was no iron in the room which is often useful for travelers. I don't know if I was there on a very busy weekend or what, but despite the nice room and good location, the above problems make it doubtful I would return to this hotel.
label: NEG

text: I've reviewed Geno's - http://www.yelp.com/biz/genos-steaks-philadelphia#hrid:_NrO8jJP-vCBEtuehOxWtA I've reviewed Pat's - http://www.yelp.com/biz/pats-king-of-steaks-philadelphia-2#hrid:eVAW9xtyPJofcgd33XrsFA And while both of these icons of Philly cheesesteak goodness were nice - Jim's won the competition for me by a landslide!!! We were in the Philly area for an off site training, when my coworker casually mentions that he's craving cheesesteak. And as he's never been to Philly (?!?), he's never been to Pat's nor Geno's. With the hunt afoot, and I whisked him away for a taste test of Geno's (2 stars) and Pat's (3 stars). By this point, we've each had 2 cheesesteak in about 15 minutes. My coworker was pretty satisfied that he's had the "Philly cheesesteak experience" at this point, and from the sounds of his burps, pretty full to boot. But me, well I've been to Philly many many times, and neither Geno's nor Pat's really hit the spot for me. So, with a bit of whining, and some sad puppy dog eyes (and the promise to fix the SQL bug that he's been working on), I convince him to come with me to a THIRD cheesesteak joint - Jim's. Please keep in mind that this is our THIRD cheesesteak in about 30 minutes at this point. THIRD. So I hope you understand what high praise it is, when I say that my coworker not only wolfed down his Jim's cheesesteak - but whimpered for more (we ended up ordering another cheesesteak from Jim's and split it). Yes, we each ate 3 1/2 cheesesteaks, with the final 1 1/2 from Jim's. Yes, it's *that* good. What makes Jim's better then Geno's or Pat's? Some may say the toppings, others may point to the warmed bread. Me? I say it's love. As any good glutton knows, the difference between two practically identical dishes (or in this case, 3), isn't the ingredients - after all, a cheesesteak is constrained by the bun, cheese and meat - but of the love that goes into making it. Jim's? They load theirs up with an extra helping of love on each cheesesteak. Yes, I love that they are indoors (I hate the cold), and yes, I love that they have more toppings then just "wit" (I like mine with peppers and mushrooms as well as onions). But it's in the love that they put into the execution. Upon ordering, the cheesesteak-master lathers the bun with cheese, then HOLDS the bun, over the meat, letting the steam from the hot grill and the cooking meat to meld and blend with the cheese. Then he deftly tops with whatever you desire, before briskly wrapping it up. Delicious. The bread was so soft and warm. I got the cheesewiz (again), and it was so thick and creamy and perfectly held the finely chopped meat together. My coworker, again, got the provolone (our scoring model you understand), and the cheese was soft and gooey and stringy - like a perfect cheesesteak should. Of the three that we tried that night, it should come as no surprise that Jim's was BY FAR our favorite. High marks all around in all categories - service, options, quality of bun, meltiness of cheese, and the effort that went into the deliciously chopped meat.
label: POS

text: So I've waited to write this review because it pains me to give a bad review to service places, but it's easier to get over a bad meal at a restaurant than it is to get over a disappointing hair experience. When I booked the appointment online I said I needed my greys covered. When I was in the chair I pointed them out again. When I left they were still there. I called two days later after contemplating writing a scalding review on Yelp, but figured that wouldn't really help my hair situation, nor would it get me my money's worth. I think I spoke with Savannah the salon owner and she told me to come back and they'd fix the problem by using another formula and/or applying heat to set the color (like most places do). I almost considered buying a box of color and doing the roots missed myself. She told me that she didn't suggest I do that, so I made an appt to come back after a trip I planned. My hair was supposed to be perfect for my trip and it wasn't. So, I went back yesterday and Dara covered the stubborn grey hair by applying a stronger formula to my roots, no heat. text: First off, Cosi should thank Yelp for not allowing us Yelpers to give ZERO stars and Maria L for really liking her Mint Mocha. text: I am writing to describe the abysmal experience we had at this restaurant last night. We went BTB because we had experienced good food, good servive and a pleasant atmosphere in the past. The waitress when she arrived, was polite and helpful. Even so, it took quite a while for the food to arrive. When it arrived, it was not to the quality that we were used to. Then the live music started. At 8pm. Somehow the hostess had seated us in front of the speakers. It was horribly loud. I live in New York City which is loud, and I had to cover my ears. We asked if there was a quieter part of the restaurant, and they looked at us like we were nuts. Finally we left. I paid for the meal, mostly because I just wanted to get out of there, but it was the biggest waste of money ever. I am now going to post on every restaurant review web site I can find, about this awful, painful experience. Julie Van Dore

text: "Oh, how the mighty have fallen" ...and it's so, so sad. A tiny part of my soul has died while shedding Broccoli Cheddar flavored tears. Alas, all good things must come to an end. Dammit. Let me just put this as succinctly as possible: Omar is L-A-Z-Y. He's the reason we'll not be back (as long as he, or others like him- are employed there). My boyfriend ordered my soup and asked that white bread be put in the bag to accompany my soup. Mind you, we ask the SAME thing every time we come in and there has never been an issue. You can get bread or crackers with the soup. I pick bread. White bread. Easy enough? You'd think so because the bag that they put the bread slices in is CLEAR plastic. Meaning each slice of bread is easily visible. On one occasion there was no white bread in there, and one of the girls so lovingly sliced some up for me really quick. How nice those days were. I will cherish them in my heart despite my growing bitterness and resentment. Anyhow, this Omar person, when asked to put in the white bread, tells my boyfriend that he CAN'T because the bread is MIXED. *pause for effect* Let me repeat "He CAN'T because the bread is MIXED". Yea. Wow. Duhhh. Hey, Omar- you don't need to have Superman X-ray powers to find slices of white bread in a huge CLEAR plastic bag! How hard is it to NOT select a piece of wheat bread, or dutch crust or some funky garlic smelling bread and pick up the piece of white bread next to it? How did you even get a job, if you're that damn inept?! Why can I pick my own bread for my sandwich and not my soup? Why am I forced to eat whatever scraps of bread you deem worthy? Why do I have to pay for bread I don't like and won't eat because you're lazy?! So my boyfriend, being the nice guy that he is- just takes the bag of bread he's given. Actually, I think his acquiesence is probably due to the fact that he has a bad temper and it's easier to just shut up sometimes than argue with an idiot. So yea. He goes to pay for the soup and discovers Omar (duh duh duh) only marked that he had one soup. Not that free soup is a bad thing, but it's generally accepted that 'honesty is the best policy' - so he points out the error and pays for his food. (As I'm sure the owner of the Deli would have wanted him too) I can't take it personal though, according to the ladies at the register Omar had managed to muck up a bunch of orders before ours. Surprise, surpise there is zero white bread in the bag. Instead we have a large pile of the funky smelling garlic bread. Oh my, isn't that nice? I guess my palate isn't delicate enough to appreciate garlic bread with Broccoli Cheddar soup. Ooops, I meant Broccoli Water. My soup was not soup. It was cream colored runny liquid and had huge chunks of broccoli floating in it. Although I am happy to report that after much digging I did manage to find one small chunk of cheese. I got a vague sense of deja vu as it reminded me of combing through a box of Cracker Jacks, looking for the 'prize'. Both of these ended the same way, with me standing there looking dejected and thinking "this is it?". I was so disapointed. But I resisted the urge to hurl my broccoli water across the room, but only because I knew I'd be the one cleaning it up. Thanks a lot Omar, you destroyed my faith in Deli Towne and it's ability to consistently provide the level of service and yummy-ness required. It's too much of a risk going all the way there after being let down by your laziness and 'can't do' attitude. "Make a fool of you once, shame on them. Make a fool of you twice, shame on me". Now I have to find another place to get my soup (and white bread). Dammit.
label: NEG

I wouldn't go here alone, even during the day, and I sure as hell wouldn't come here at night, even with company. So that's par for the course. (Also, I digress: if you're the grungy or dreadlocked type of hipster, or just down with a more street crowd, you might not get the sort of looks I did. It's not like I walked out here decked out like a prepster, but I definitely got extra flack for being a whitey-white girl being where she shouldn't be.) The cafe itself is also very, very dingy. Paint peeling, rickety furniture, cracks in the flooring, more than a handful of free-roaming flies, etc. It was, I suppose, a little more "earthy" and a little less "homey" than I expected, in that regard. A glance behind the coffee bar at least told me that hygiene was definitely being maintained back there--can't speak for back in the kitchen, which is behind a solid door in the back. The lady behind the counter was very nice and spoke very limited English, which is usually, to me, a sign of good things to come. I have a good bit of travel under my belt and language barriers don't phase me. My beau and I got iced coffee, which was ok (I still like Almaz's better) and ordered a hummus platter to start, as well as yebeg tibs (spicy) and kitfo (medium rare). The hummus platter was generous, with decent hummus (probably not home-made), tons of extremely tasty green olives, and store-bought thick multigrain pita. Not exhilirating, but alright. The meat dishes came served together on a large platter, on top of injera, with a tiny portion of collard greens, a mild crumbled white cheese (think Feta in looks but cottage cheese in terms of taste), and yellow lentils--these added sides were no more than maybe 3 Tbsp each, though the tibs and kitfo portions were almost too generous. There was also an extra plate of injera on the side--definitely more than plenty, so don't even think about ordering extra. ;) All the sides were delicious, so I was sad the portions were so small. I did enjoy my partner's tibs, though I found it a little underwhelming and very greasy. My kitfo was floating in chili oil and, while tasty, had come raw rather than medium rare. (I loves me some still-mooing cow, but I also like to trust a place and don't generally get raw red meat items on a first visit, unless highly recommended.) That was fine, but how they managed to make raw ground beef heavy rather than light/refreshing, I don't know. My favorite part was the injera. I found it a little less sourdough-y/tangy than Almaz's (not better or worse, just different) but the texture was perfect. We dropped just under $50 with tip for those two iced coffees (which neither of us finished: rare for two ex-baristas), the appetizer, and two mains. It was too much, in my opinion, for the quality of food. Worst part, I had to stop by the pharmacy on the way home for a bunch of antacids because the kitfo just started riling my stomach up. I don't know if it was a freshness issue (it tasted fine--but was very highly spiced, so I might have been off on that count) or just all the chili oil everything was floating in. It took a half pack of extra-strength Rolaids before I felt alright, and it took me out of commission for the rest of the day. The service was friendly and not pushy; the atmosphere was laid-back. But the location was extremely iffy, and nothing about the experience makes me want to make another trip back to see if it was the kitfo's fault or my stomach's. Sorry Kaffa; I'll be sticking to Almaz from now on.

Russel, the hotel shift manager, was fabulous and assured us that our money would be refunded and that he had made a reservation for us... at a QUALITY INN. um, really?! The great thing was that Russel bought our room for us, but it was still a giant let down as something similar had happened to us the year before at another hotel. I asked someone later if it would make a difference to book the reservation through the hotel rather than through an online site and my suspicion was confirmed. Hotels always overbook in order to assure a full house and they rely on cancellations. Online booking sites are the lowest priority for keeping reservations because they don't pay the hotel until 30 days later, but they hotel gets paid no matter what. My friends were late, so I spent the time reading the reviews and awards hanging on the wall and perusing the menu. By the time they showed up, I had decided our menu: dumplings in spicy sauce, golden eggplant coins, mapo tofu, 3 pepper chicken and two other dishes they could choose to include the spice-intolerant. They chose Triple Delight with Spicy sauce and a chicken noodle dish. The spice-intolerant who chose the noodles said they were bland. Well, duh. The Triple Delight was chosen because the friend enjoys that dish and uses it as a comparison. He said it does not compare to his favorite place, but it was well-made and he enjoyed it. Those two dishes, along with the eggplants, served as our non-spicy complements. The eggplant coins were delicious! Probably our second favorite, after the dumplings in spicy sauce. However, the sauce with the golden coins was uninteresting, and we used the remaining dumpling sauce with it. That spicy dumpling sauce is amazing. I would drink it like a milkshake. The mapotofu was tongue-tingling numb, like a good szechuan peppercorn dish! I enjoyed it, but my friends who had never had the peppercorn before had mixed reviews about the sensation. And one friend who had peppercorn before said he felt it was too strong of a sensation compared to his previous experience. Nevertheless, I enjoyed it, including the silky texture of the tofu and the fine mince of the meat. It seems to me that most folks get take-out (both from reviews and my experience seeing a lot of delivery orders prepared). I would go back for when I want that peppercorn experience, especially for the dumplings. Though, I think Dim Sum Garden will remain our go-to Chinatown joint. Oh P.S. It is BYO, so bring either a white wine or cold beer to counter the spice!

text: We chose Kota for our 'regular-dinner-get togethers' last Saturday night with friends. It is one of many 'to-try' choices in my Yelp bookmarks. For a party of 8, there was no trouble getting a table as the Fox was vacant this weekend. I am sure this is a much different venue with the pre-show crowds. Nevertheless, love the location of this place and the real city-feel you get in Grand Center. Suffice it to say, having lived in the city for many years, Grand Center really has come to life. The service was aces, with a very attentive hostess, bartender and server. Again, it was a slower night. The waitress even walked us to the table pointing carefully to the short set of stairs. The decor is tasteful with carefully selected art and a huge row of colored glass and low lighting to add ambiance. Very comfortable space. Trying to describe 'New American' style of cuisine invites some laughter, but indeed it's interpretation can vary depending on the chef. Someone in our party got excited for the cajun dishes offered, another the variety of vegetarian choices. Presentation was good. We started with the calamari, ahi tuna tostadas and stuffed mushrooms for the table. Our entire group seemed pleased. The tostadas have been reviewed before, and they are that good - not the best by any means - but served on a plantain chip gave this app a good flavor. For the main course, I ordered the Voodoo Shrimp Pasta (hickory fired shrimp with squid ink fettuccini in jalapeno cream sauce, with roasted corn and poblano peppers). And it appeared every one asks the server what 'squid ink' fettuccini is; simply by the look on her face when we did the same. For the record, it is just dark-colored noodles. The flavors were great. The cream sauce brought out the bite and made the shrimp rather tasty and juicy. Good dish. We had a duck connoisseur of sorts on-hand and commented on trying that the coconut curry duck linguini was very lacking. It was the only dish that offered us an option of leftovers. The jambalaya - made with mussels - was said to be very good. Before I forget, Koda offers Delirium Tremens on tap here which is an excellent Belgian pale ale if you like yours strong. Because of it's proximity to the Fox, I am sure the mood of the restaurant changes between casual and semi-formal, depending on the night. My recommendation, to soak in the surroundings and your meal, go when there is not a show. But alas, it fits the bill for a perfect dining option where you can where your jeans and yet eat a refined, creative menu.

Using an automated grinder, the various toppings are brought together perfect, and not uneven --- as is the case in the coldstones where the server's disinterest or lack of attention to detail can detract from the quality of the ice cream that is supposed to be custom blended. Scoop De Ville has such a warm, fun feel to it that you just enjoy being in the place. None of the contrived "sing every few minutes with no enthusiasm or soul" that you see in some of the Coldstone outlets (Times Square, anyone?). From the fuzzy, hand drawn menus to the cheerful and helpful staff...this is exactly what creates a wonderful dessert experience. Even though Scoop De Ville has been around 20 years, the family that runs it has been in business in Philadelphia since 1850 producing candies and chocolates. They just moved from their 90 year old location to a nearby, roomier location --- but the quality, the ambience is all there. Be prepared to be absolutely delighted!

text: Heading to the Reno area to visit friends for the weekend, but we needed somewhere to eat Friday night (7-30-10). So, I did some research (yelping) and came across ZoZo's which I noticed had a solid 4 star rating with 30+ reviews. I told the wife about the place since she's the picky one and even though she wanted to go to Johnny's Ristorante to eat, I convinced her to take a chance and give my fellow yelper's the benefit of the doubt. The gamble paid off. We found a new place to dine in Reno. ZoZo's sits in a strip mall at the corners of Moana Ln & Lakeside Dr. Basically, it's in a "if you blink, you'll miss it" spot, so keep your eyes open. Parking is ample and abundant and well lit at night. The area surrounding the restaurant isn't so great, so I suggest driving and not walking around the area alone. Upon entering ZoZo's, you'll find it reminiscent of the old 70's style pizza joints. It's dark, but cozy. It's dimly lit by candles and has the red pleater seats that squeak when you sit down. In other words, a fun and nostalgic place (at least for me). I made reservations for 7:00 pm and we arrived a few moments early. As we walked in, we were immediately greeted by the owner Judy who seated us right away. Our waiter (Pepe) came over within a few moments to take our drink orders and he explained the specials on the menu. We selected a Chianti wine and we went with Pepe 's recommendations for our appetizer, dinners and desert. Prior to any food hitting our table, a loaf of fresh garlic bread was given to us to munch on. The goodness of the bread has been beaten up already, so I'll skip the details and move on. Our Appetizer: Quail cooked to perfection placed upon a bed of artichokes, onions and spinach. Our Salad: Was a basic green salad with croutons, cherry tomato's and a house "creamy italian" dressing. Our Dinners: The wife selected the New York Steak topped with Gorgonzola cheese accompanied by Asparagus and Mashed Potato's. I went with the Cioppino on a bed of Linguine pasta. Our Desert: Only Tiramisu would do. As some of you already know, I rate the totality of the restaurant when I dine out. Nothings left out or missed. Everything from the bathrooms cleanliness to the wait staffs attention to detail, it's all fair game. So as far as ZoZo's overall rating goes, this place is a solid 4 star with a 5 star potential. I enjoyed watching the owner Judy take the time to conversant with all the patrons in the establishment as they dined (which is rare nowadays) and I really enjoyed our waiter Pepe's kind and friendly attitude. Pepe is a true gentleman as defined by Webster himself. The food was "out of sight" and the ambiance of the establishment can be described in one simple word; "nostalgic." Now for the cons of my review: 1. ZoZo's is NOT open for lunch on the weekend. 2. The mens restroom was a bit unkept. 3. I had my heart set on an espresso after dinner, but their machine wasn't working. Overall, ZoZo's is still a solid 4 stars restaurant.

text: New Orleans Birthday Trip = Music in the French Quarter So this here, this back in an ally, is the House of Blues. It's dark and it's ominous and it really feels like it should and would be an great place to grab a drink and listen to some music. It may not be the first, but it's the best because it's basically awesome. Venue: HoB is a real music venue, that's what it's built for. It's a stage, with a lighting truss and music set up, two floors and a balcony, and every spot is within spitting distance of the stage. Both floors have their own bars, and while the space may get crowded, just remember there are 799 other people here just attempting to enjoy the music, so don't be an ass and share the space. It's dark inside the hall, with various mood lighting in blues and purples, and be careful where you put your foot down, because there might just be a step or two there. Largely, the entire venue is deceiving. There are upstairs, downstairs, private rooms, music halls, parishes and patios. You could throw whatever the hell kinda party you wanted down in NOLA at the House of Blues and probably never run out of space. Downside of HoB nowadays it it's national chaindom. Back when NOLA's HoB was the second in charge and still a novelty, there was nothing better. But now they seem to be everywhere, even at Disney, and they're owned by Live Nation--the authenticity has been lost a bit. Still, in certain glimmers of chords and powerful vocals, you can find it: that true music hall feel, so go for the history too, but always for the music. Music: The entertainment at HoB run the gamut. They'll have everything from The Naked Brothers Band a la Nickelodeon to David Cook to burlesque shows and real soul music. Take a pick, but always go, even if just for the opening act like we did. That's right, we went to House of Blues for an opening act: acoustic Vertical Horizon, or the frontman at least. It was awesome, and spontaneous and well worth it, because the venue is welcoming and acoustically primed. There's food too, but we skipped out after VH was done (and yes I knew every song). I here the brunch is pretty good though, so if you're in town for a while, try both.

text: Life is too short to not enjoy it to the fullest. These days I've been just trying to keep my mind clear and my heart open. I need times like these to keep me grounded so that I don't get overstressed by life. I needed a day like this so that I'm balanced and I can reset, recharge the batteries. There were already about 6 people waiting for the restaurant to open. A good sign... This restaurant was pumped up all week by a friend of mine and it delivered. The place is easily missed. It is located on a small avenue and is small itself. There is nothing special about the exterior or the interior but that never distracts me from the quality of food. The order included yellow tail sashimi, albacore sashimi, spicy tuna roll, and yellow tail tuna collar dinner. Don't forget the cold sake which contributed to my headache and subsequent dehydration. The tuna collar dinner included a sweet and sour cucumber salad, miso salad, and one piece of mochi ice cream. The yellow tail sashimi was excellent quality. It was very fresh, tender, and flavorful. The albacore lightly grilled in the outside so it had light chewy texture but ultra tender in the inside, this too melted in your mouth. I had to try the yellow tail collar to compare to Teru sushi. The collar here was larger because it includes a section of the body behind the collar. It looked beautiful on my plate. It looked like it was baked not grilled. The outside was almost crispy and the meat cooked well. It was a tad dryer than expected but tasted good. The skin was much different being baked not grilled. I like the grilled skin much better and skipped some parts of the skin. The plate includes ponzu sauce which was sour and tasted great with the tuna. All in all the night was filled with laughter and stories. Shared moments that became stories. Great food, great company, great atmosphere, great service, and cool patrons. When we left the restaurant, it was completely full and there were at least another 8 people waiting to eat here. Have you ever had a day where you just didn't want to end? text: I took a date here on a Saturday night. It was the day of a big college football game in the Dome so parking in Quarter was even more atrocious than normal. Now as a bit of backstory, when I was in highschool I worked with my grandfather on our cattle farm in Missouri. when I was leaving for New Orleans he told me that while they may be some of the best cooks there, if he remembers correctly they couldn't cook a steak to save their lives since there aren't much cattle farming opportunities on the swampland. Now, years later, his words ring truer than ever. While the service was acceptable, the food was sub-par, especially for the high price. The SS&LH is more of a gross parody of New Orleans food than an actual restaurant. The reason I frequented the joint was a deal I got through Groupon, so at least I had an excuse; I'm not sure about the other 4 people who were at the other tables. The atmosphere was dingy, the live musician was a mediocre flutist playing over some backing tracks, the whole thing was New Orleans gone wrong. For one, I am pretty sure my side of sauteed mushrooms were microwaved before they brought them out. Correct me if I am wrong, but I am pretty sure after a light treatment of butter in a frying pan it isn't proper to place the mushrooms in a bowl or water. I may have been born at night, but it wasn't last night; these mushrooms were nuked. The drink prices were ridiculous as well. $4.50 for Turbodog??? I can pick up a 6-pack at Win-Dixie for seven dollars after their markup. I know the quarter is expensive, but this may be criminal. To be frank, there is no reason to come to this restaurant, and tourists and locals alike should stay away. If you are really jonesing for a steak, just go to Applebee's. You will get better food, or at least comparable, for cheaper, plus you don't have to park in the quarter. You are in New Orleans, there is no excuse to go to an overpriced mediocre restaurant.

text: Edmonton's downtown pyramid on Churchill Square is City Hall. It houses our local government offices, on the second floor they hold council meetings at least once weekly - check the website for specifics. It's a beautiful building inside and out. The decor changes often as new events or festivals take place in the city. The main foyer is often used for award ceremonies, local events and festival activities. There are lots of historical photos - of previous mayors and old local government buildings. There's more to this place than the counter where you go to pay your city parking tickets! In the front, facing the square, is a large fountain in the summer which is converted into a skating rink in the winter. You can hear the bells of the clock chime in a sort of creepily beautiful way bouncing off the tall buildings of the city's core. The underground parking at City Hall is meters, so bring your change. I'll give you some inside advice that I picked up working downtown in the past - after 6pm, the cost is only $0.50/hr, from 6am-6pm during the week, the rate is $1.50/hr. Weekends are also $0.50/hr. They may have changed things but the meters used to be free on Sundays and Holidays. Still, it's connected via the LRT pedway to the Winspear Centre, Edmonton City Centre shopping, The Stanley Milner Library, The Citadel, The Westin, and many other locations. Check out the pedway maps. It's great in the winter to park in one spot and not have to go outside! It's also a LOT cheaper than any other underground parking in the area.

text: On the recommendation of a friend, our party of 4 decided to try this hole-in-the-wall restaurant last night. To say the least, it was a big disappointment. The first disappointment was I wanted to sit at the round table that sat 6. The host said, "That table seats 6, you sit here at this table." Which also sat 6. Ridiculous. Moreover, they never had a party come in "large" enough to sit at that round table. On to the food... Everything from the samosas to the garlic naan to 3 out of 4 of our entrees needed salt -- not a ton of salt, but enough that it was just annoying because we were constantly having to reach for it. However, much to our surprise, the appetizer sampler was decent. The chicken tikka wasn't dried out as it is at many restaurants. It needed just a touch of salt, but it was good. The seekh kebab was decent, but I think a little more spice would've put it where I really like it plus just a tad more salt. The 2 shrimp were OK too. I will say, however, that the grilled onions they served with it were absolutely superb. Not overly cooked with just enough bite and a wonderful flavor. One in our party was an Indian food virgin, so we suggested what 2 of us were getting: Chicken Makhani. Another disappointment. It seemed as tho there was a flavor component missing. It did need just a touch of salt, but not enough that we felt we needed to add salt like the other food. The newbie and I ordered it medium spicy, and the third ordered spicy. Our friend who loves spicy REALLY had some spice. She enjoyed it, but it was the spiciest she's ever had "spicy" from an Indian restaurant -- not a complaint in her book. The medium was good too. There was quite a bit of heat to the dish, but not so much that I was rushing for the raita. The level of heat all around was good. The fourth in our party order the Lamb Roti Kebab. He was pleased with the dish, and I had to take a bite since he was pleased. It was decent. I think the flavor components were there, and I was fine with the salt level -- of course, lamb altogether adds another level to the dish. Anyway, the majority of us agree that we won't be returning to this restaurant. It just isn't worth it. Indian Palace a couple miles away on N. Maryland Ave is SOOOO much better with comparable prices -- and I mean SOOOOO much better.

text: First, this review is based on an experience three years ago when my mom got married here. I know that they must have chosen this venue based on price alone as they were on a tight budget (and shouldn't have been getting married in the first place--different story for another day). The day before their wedding (June 30th, 2006) was a wet one in Tucson. Everyone in the wedding party went here to rehearse and it was an okay place. It wasn't like the fancy wedding places I would have chosen, but it was my mom's taste as she was having a hill billy -- er, I mean, "cowboy" themed -- wedding. It was Southwestern-y feeling, for sure. Her minister didn't even rehearse as the ground was too wet to practice on. No one working there insisted that we go ahead with a rehearsal to make the wedding went off without a hitch (ha! Irony). Instead, they kept to themselves until the "rehearsal" was over with. The next day, the storms came even harder just before the ceremony. No one working there offered to dry off the seats for the guests; we had the ushers do it. No indoor options were arranged or even avaliable for that matter. My mom had her joke of a wedding, cowboy hats on all the men and all. We all went inside where the reception was to be held. It was pretty basic. If they had done something to the chairs, it would have made a spectacular change and even looked a little classier. Instead, we were all seated on plain metal folding chairs -- fitting, I suppose, for the Cowboy wedding. The people who catered the wedding (Golden Corral, of all places!) weren't worth making note of, but I'm going to. They served up the food, but for the bridal party, well my sister the other bridesmaid, they said she only had the option of ____ instead of the white meat chicken she was pointing to. Had I known this took place, I would have reminded them that my mom was the one paying them to stand there and be rude (and everything else as her husband is a cheap bastard), so they could at least be nice enough to the bride's daughters. People enjoyed the open bar and a lot of drunks took it upon themselves to act stupid. The entire time I was wondering where the hell the people running this place were to put a limit on the number of drinks people could get, or to at least lasso the drunks still parading about the dancefloor picking up the flower girl and tossing her around. She giggled the whole time, but I'm sure she'll have strange flashbacks later in life. Anyways, this place is okay if you don't have the funds to have a big fancy wedding (or don't want one, for that matter). However, it's not somewhere I would choose to marry.

text: I live here for a damn good reason. I came to Philadelphia for college because I didn't think I could afford to go to New York. Despite our second-rate opinions of each other then, I now refuse to move to New York (despite working there) because I love Philadelphia so much. Albeit smaller, Philadelphia has the diversity that gentrification ruined in most major cities. It's the only place that I can think of where I can have conversations with people of all groups in my day, and pay it no mind. We have affordable living, a wealth of culture, and as Yelp clearly shows, some of the finest eats, drinks, and shopping on the planet. The best thing of all is that the 215 refuses to be jaded. We're just as smart as New Yorkers, just as cosmopolitan (dear god, I'm never using that word again), and we're still faced with reality every day. Brotherly love seems cliche, but if you do the math and the history, this place was designed on those principles, and despite our litter, deer carcases (which, if you were in the city, those were people... or you didn't get off the turnpike), and any other blemishes, we still keep it TRILL... and for you squares out there, that's truly-real. Recently asked if I'll ever leave Philly, until I get a job I can't refuse in NYC or I move to Tucson, Arizona with the woman of my dreams... I just might not. text: New Deck Tavern is a charming Irish Pub tucked away on Sansom Street. The atmosphere both inside and out really succeeds in creating a warm intimate atmosphere, with a bit of an old world charm. It's actually a big bar, and can draw a big crowd, but it is partitioned such that it seems cozy and inviting somehow. Additionally, there is outdoor dining as there is all along Sansom on the 3400 block, and it's quite nice as well when the weather is decent. The food is decent, but not particularly memorable. I usually have a sandwich or a burger. The highlight is probably the fries, as they are actually quite good. The hamburgers leave a bit to be desired though. Anytime I order a burger and the waiter doesn't follow up with "how would you like that cooked?", it sets off red flags in my head. You're pretty much stuck with medium-well. That said, the prices are very reasonable. Expect to pay about eight to ten dollars for an overall very satisfying meal. The drink menu is basically the same as the food. There are a decent number of taps, but if you're a beer lover like me you may get bored quickly. They had Yards and Dogfish head on tap, but beyond that you're stuck with the big name mass-distributed kind(Guinness on down to the Budweisers of the world). They certainly have a nicely stocked bar, and I have no right to complain, but I just feel they could have aimed a little higher. Perhaps New Deck is a victim of its own success. The food doesn't need to be any better than it is because the place gets totally packed on the weekends. If you want a table on a Friday night, you're going to have to wait. The staff is attentive though, and once seated you shouldn't have to wait long for your food. So overall, the New Deck Tavern has some minor faults, perhaps mere quirks if you will, but it has a charming atmosphere and is a nice place to grab a bite or just hang out with friends.

text: --Lack of consistency in both food and service-- I moved here several months ago and was stoked to hear about a vegan diner in Reno. The first time I dined, the place was adequate enough for three stars, but today I returned and the service and food were abysmal. I ordered the falafel sam'ich, one of many overly self-conscious, self-aware items on their quixotic menu, and my friend tried the nachos. The nachos were passable but obscenely overpriced. My falafel was a downright disaster. To start, the sunflower wheat bread was hard and crumbly, about an hour away from stale. The falafel was overcooked, hard, and dry. As you can imagine, lifting this awkwardly prepared sam'ich to my face was a task even the most dexterous human would struggle with; I should know, I'm ambidextrous. Soon, I was reduced to forking my meal, which had been reduced to a pale imitation of anything resembling a sandwich. The only good thing was that they forgot to charge me for the avocado, which happened to be good, though with the gross lack of oversight in preparing my stale $8 stinker, I'm surprised it wasn't overripe and sullen with stench. Ordinarily I would bring this to a restaurateur's attention, but that would have made my fragile, crumbly mess of a sandwich even less of a bargain at $9. Now, before you assume I'm a cynical food snob who ought be nice to this locally owned restaurant, consider the fact that it utterly screams pretense about its supposed 'vegan cred'. As a vegetarian, I find this a tad obnoxious. Why should a veggie restaurant have to try so hard? I get it: you're hip, you hire hipsters, and the background music is even hipper. How about spending less time on the decor and more time on the food? How about dropping the price a couple bucks on each item? I've had better vegetarian food at traditional non-veggie restaurants. The Western Village has an excellent veggie burger for $5 with fries. Aside from beverages or appetizers, there's nothing on the Pneumatic Diner's menu for $5. Having espoused my true feelings for the Pneumatic Diner, allow me to hurl one last curve ball to further flummox my dear reader. Even with all my gripes, I still enjoy the ambition of any entrepreneur who recognizes the need to provide an alternative to a typical meat-laden menu. Kudos to the owners for their daring attempt; though they fail so spectacularly in execution, their aspiration is spot on..

text: I want to like this place, I really do, but I have just about given up on Bala. Like others have said in their review, it is a great building. You can tell it used to be a great theater before its re-purposing into a cinema. There is staircases on each side that lead up to a balcony (you can't sit up there) and the ornamentation in the theater really is beautiful- the main theater with the chandelier has metal work all around it with an Egyptian theme. This place has good bones- that's about it. I have had several strange experiences at Bala that have made me want to rarely return. First, they used to offer a $5 matinee special for all films before 4. Great! Except no films would play before 4- all films started 4:30 at the earliest. If you don't want to offer a matinee, don't put it up there on your website. Now that they have raised their prices (which I will get to) to $8 bucks a ticket, they have some matinees. Who I believe to be the manager, Frank, is one of the worst customer service experiences a patron can have. He is rude when you ask him a question and has yelled in front of us (the paying customer) to his employees. Maybe it is time to find a new career? That being said, all of the other employees I have encountered have been nothing but professional and courteous at all times. On two separate occasions, the heat in certain theaters was not working. I understand that these things do happen from time to time, but when it happens twice, you should either close the theater all together until repairs can be made, or offer some sort of discount to another film in a theater that has working heat. Finally, the prices have jumped- a lot. The tickets used to be $7 for a show- which I felt was reasonable for what you were getting- the building has nice bones, but it simply cannot compete with newer theaters in terms of comfort and amenities- therefore, I always thought that Bala was priced accordingly. During my most recent visit, however, I found that a ticket had jumped to $10 dollars- comparable to the bigger theaters nearby. This is just ridiculous. If I am going to spend $10 on a movie, I am going to go to a theater where I know I will get good service and have heat- two things Bala cannot always provide. While I want to support local business as much as possible, I won't support a bad business. For the same money I can go to KOP and see a film. If you are looking for a theater that serves a similar niche as Bala without the inconsistency and jacked up pricing, go to Bryn Mawr Film Institute- you will not be dissapointed.

text: We were here last Sunday, May 24. The only three reasons why we came in here was 1) Joe's Crab Shack, the closer we walked towards it, seemed like less and less of a good idea and this is right next door, 2) it smelled really good, and 3) seemed like a micro or in-house brewery is always a cool idea. I just don't know anymore. We really started this dining experience with hope in our hearts. The design of the building is cold-yet-impressive. The graphics on the logo reminded me of the Soviet Union. Different. Industrial-looking to the max. Not tacky, like next door at Joe's. I liked the way you walk past the big tanks where they brew. You knew they were not there for show. This restaurant is also on the banks of the Christina River, which is very calm and nice to look out at. However, we did not sit outside, because there were the ever-present bratty kids whose parents are unable to control them. As I mentioned, it started out on a hopeful note. Our server's name was Don and he was very earnest in selling that beer. I decided to try a taste of three different kinds, the Ironbound Ale, the Vienna Red, and the Raspberry Wheat. He brought them in three very small juice-sized tasting glasses, and only a sip of each. That was fine, like a little "flight" of beers. I did not like the Ironbound - it was bitter to me. The Vienna Red was slightly better, but not with food. The Raspberry Wheat was good (well, the best out of all three, and I did want a beer), and I felt it would go with what i was ordering, which it did. I also asked for a glass of ice water, and it tasted terrible. We had just come from Delaware Park, and their drinking water was bad-tasting, as well. What's with the drinking water in Wilmington, is it all this bad? And I'm originally from Philly... After the beer-tasting, the service went downhill from there. I don't know, our server may have received bad news between the time we ordered and the time we received our food. He was struggling with the next table, reading their orders back wrong, etc. He seemed so flustered all of a sudden. They weren't THAT busy. We ordered the seafood bisque, and it never arrived. What is up with that? He realized this as soon as he walked up with our entrees. He actually ASKED if we wanted it taken off the check. Come on, now! No, leave it on? We want to pay for the food we never received?!? Please. How do you forget someone's soup? How do you OFFER to take it off the check? Oh, I forgot the famous, "Do you still want it?" No, man! You eat it before the entree, not with! Entrees...my boyfriend ordered a catfish dish which appeared to have some sort of remoulade on top of it. I don't think this is on the online menu, and I, like Aimee C. below my review, was unimpressed with the overall experience, and didn't pick up a menu to take home. I usually do that...if I like the place and if it was a good overall dining experience. For the life of me, I can't remember what his side dish was. I know he'd remember, but right now I don't care enough to get that information for you readers. I normally take pictures of my food, but the light was not good enough for my camera phone, and as I said, we did not eat outside. My entree was that House Smoked BBQ Pork sandwich. The flavor was good, and I'm sure that was the smell that I was sniffing outside. It was definitely smoked, and that makes a big difference to me when I'm eating anything BBQ. But that's where the goodness stopped. This thing was pretty dry. Overly smoked? I don't know what that sauce was but I dipped my fries (which were good, I must say, and fresh-cut, but a very chintzy serving) in it, and I'm 99% sure it was malt vinegar. I like that, and use it at home. But I wonder if this was supposed to be some sort of Eastern North Carolina BBQ sauce. So, nice touch if it was for the fries (which now I'm thinking it wasn't, and I don't like Eastern NC BBQ vinegar taste), but it doesn't make up for a dry sandwich, forgotten bisque, and wait! I'm not quite done! We get the check and this little "flight" of three beers was on it! .50 for each one! Listen, if this Don had MENTIONED that there was a charge, or if I had SEEN that on the menu, I wouldn't complain, but there was absolutely no evidence prior to that of charging for these tastes. We weren't going to raise a stink for $1.50, but you know what? You tip for service, and with each error, your tip goes down a notch. That's how it is. Mention if there's a charge...for ANYTHING, OK, Don? It might make a difference in your tip. The food wasn't horrible, but it wasn't that wonderful at all, and the service was so hopeful at first, as I mentioned (maybe twice I mentioned it), and became so disappointing, that we will not be back, even though they have opened or will be opening one in our area, in Maple Shade, NJ. Not enough to get me to want to go. I'm just tired of any sort of chain, no matter how small or local it is...

text: I was eager to try the newly opened Bibou and went to dinner there tonight with three friends. The old Pif space has been lovingly redone, with dark wainscoting contrasting nicely with the elegantly set tables. Charlotte Calmels is the perfect hostess: the welcome is warm and charming, and everything is done to make you comfortable at one of the very closely spaced tables. The menu is short but diverse, with some dishes hinting at the Burgundian origin of the chef (snail ragout with fava beans). We tried the soup of the day, made with corn and lump crab meat, its velvety creaminess nicely contrasted with tasty kernels of roasted corn, the foie gras, unctuously rich as expected on a port and cassis reduction, and the beautifully textured rillettes terrine. For our main dishes, we had the deftly prepared duck breast special, the richly tasting hangar steak (both meats perfectly cooked rare to medium rare), a moistly sweet halibut on basmati rice with ramps, incredibly light and deeply flavored, and the breaded veal scaloppini, correctly done but my least favored dish of our order. The desserts, as well as the cheese plate, need some tweaking. The $12 cheese plate came with three small pieces of good but hardly exceptional cheeses, a few grapes and some salad greens - serviceable but not up to the high standards of the first two courses. Similarly, the desserts are all good - a nicely caramelized apple Tarte Tatin with chocolaty ice cream, a "chocolate millefeuille" that brought miniscule layers of creamy chocolate on crisp puff pastry - but they too are not in the class of the appetizers and main courses. The price/quality ratio is excellent, most appetizers are under ten dollars (the exception, of course, is the foie gras) and the most expensive main courses are in the mid twenties. You can end the meal with a rich French Press coffee and a couple tiny madeleines (the latter compliments of the house). Lovely! The service is professional and diners can have a quick conversation with chef Pierre Calmels when he briefly leaves his kitchen. It is simply marvelous to go out in South Philadelphia and sit in a restaurant with such amazingly sophisticated food at such affordable prices. Word has already gotten around, the restaurant was full at all times with content diners, enjoying the good luck of having a place like Bijou join the list of fine Philadelphia BYOBs. My rating is 4.5 - when the cheese platter gets better, it will be a 5 star place!

text: For quite a while now, I've been pondering what exactly to say about The Drunken Fish based on the one time I visited the Central West End location. I had veritable writer's block insofar as any substantive, noteworthy observations were concerned. In retrospect, my mental jogging-in-place makes perfect sense, because this restaurant is nothing if not insubstantial. The decor and overall ambiance - if you can even call it that - are more in line with a vapid Wash Ave. club than with anywhere I would want to be caught eating, dead or alive. If the restaurant name wasn't a tip-off, The Drunken Fish basically imports the most boilerplate aspects of Vegas and Ibiza culture and distills them to appeal to self-consciously hip Midwestern college students whose experience with these locations is limited to feature shows they watched on E! I digress, though - good food/service can always mitigate if not supersede lack of ambiance. In light of that, it's doubly disappointing that the actual substance here does nothing to loosen the perpetual eye roll that embodies my attitude towards this place. The staff is functional, but not particularly friendly or efficient. As for the sushi, it's not the worst I've had in St. Louis, but it's the kind of sushi made for people who eat sushi just so they can be seen eating sushi. I can't speak for all of the rolls, but the California and spicy tuna rolls tasted somewhere between "sloppy" and "bland", with none of the smooth, clean sophistication of similar rolls at superior restaurants. Supposedly the happy hour here is legendary but really, too much of a mediocre thing is just that. It's like oil to water anyway, because I don't even drink. I honestly don't understand how this place makes a killing when the much better Chi is mere blocks away. Then again, Chi has been trying really, really hard to emulate The Drunken Fish nowadays. Let's just hope they limit the hero worship to the decor.
label: NEG

text: We try to keep our red meat consumption down to once or twice a month, but when the mood strikes - Zinburger is the best burger in Tucson! Our game plan is to arrive by 5 and grab a table on the patio. We enjoy our first bottle of Hey Mambo with an order of sweet potato chips. The appetizers are also half off during happy hour. The yogurt dip which comes with the sweet potato chips is a nice flavor complement to the sweetness of the chips. By the time 5:45 rolls around, we're ready to order burgers and that second bottle of wine (after all, how many places can you get 2 decent bottles of red for the price of 1!) My favorite toppings are the braised onion and Maytag blue cheese; my husband goes for the Manchego, avocado and sometimes a third topping of maple bacon (always with a little mustard on the side). text: Yeah yeah let's all make fun of Whole Foods by calling it "Whole Paycheck . . .". Okay, finished? The employees don't get paid enough to care about their jobs and the other customers are sometimes very scary (I won't delve too deeply into personal accounts, but I was semi-stalked there once by a random fellow customer and I truly RAN into the restroom). Sure John Mackey, CEO of Walmart, is a verifiable nutjob, but there really isn't too much else in terms of vegan-friendly, organic, environmentallly conscious grocers in New Orleans (grrr!), so Whole Foods is my heavenly haven. The employees are mostly super duper helpful and friendly. Sometimes too friendly . . . but very well informed about their products and if not, they can always direct you to someone who is. As far as Whole Foods as a whole (hah, I made funny!) goes, this one has a little less selection in terms of vegan products (but more than the larger Veteran's location), but there's plenty more regional-themed products to satisfy the locals. They have excellent quality control for their produce, meats (I am told) and they even take great care to not stock the damaged boxes and cans (for the most part). Some of my favorite ares are the bulk section (buy in bulk and it will be comparable to Wamart prices!), the salad bar (love that tofu), and the wine area is pretty darn decent. Also it's kind of not-so-nice that the products at this Whole Foods are noticeably pricier here than they are in Austin or Houston but okay, I'm over it. Also a minor point, but in case anyone is curious - I only buy my cat's food here. I don't like feeding her Purina and all that other awful stuff, but I can't afford Pet Promise, so she's stuck with the 365 brand of dry and cat food. She's not a finicky eater, but she was a bit snotty about the dry food at first - now she loves it. And it is completely cheap and a billion times better than Iams and all that mess. Just a FYI! Oh and Whole Foods publishes a "The Whole Deal" coupon, recipe, etc. booklet every month or two and the coupons sometime coincide nicely with the weekly deals. Check it out!

text: I recently had a craving for an oyster po-boy. I went to Fiorella's, but alas, no oysters. Before absolutely confirming this, the waitress turned around and asked one of the owners sitting at the table directly behind her. The owner apologized to me and explained it had been hard finding decent oysters, so she wasn't serving them that day. Thrown off course for a moment, I finally decided on the shrimp poboy as a substitute. I was glad I chose shrimp over italian sausage. The breading was perfect(!) and just a little spicy. The shrimp were sliced sideways and piled high atop the pillowy toasted french toast. The fries were great as well, and this is coming from a "I only eat onion rings" kinda gal. My mom had red beans and rice...but then of course, it was Monday. Since she stole a few shrimp from my plate without asking, I got a few forkfuls of her meal. It was tasty! Not exactly perfect, like 'insert favorite relative's name here' (in my case, my grandfather) used to make, but pretty tasty. On my next visit, I look forward to the illusive oyster poboy and I think I need to try their eggplant chips. Oh, and if I hadn't been so dead-set on getting a poboy, I would have tried their fried chicken. It looked awesome, and judging from the breading on the shrimp, must be divine. My only complaint was that since it was so close to a few cheesy frozen-daiquiris-in-plastic-foot-tall-neon-green-alien-cup establishments, there were a few fratties that walked in, then back out again. Not Fiorella's fault, that would be all of the silly frat boys.
label: POS

text: ERRR did I really just find frozen veggies mix in my burrito.... and a slice of Kraft cheese (unmelted). WHERE THE HECK IS MEXICAN FOOD in Philly??! I'd rather go to Qdoba than this wannabe. At least you know it's not meant to be authentic there.... Oh how I miss California!! :(
label: NEG

text: I guess I've been on a bit of a Brazilian steakhouse kick lately.. After going to Chima and Fogo I would say that Picanha is right up there - but it's much different. Unlike Chima and Fogo where you pay a flat rate, at Picanha you pay by weight. So you go up to the counter and tell the griller man what you want and they give it to you. The meat was delicious and tender, and had almost the same selection that the big boy steakhouses had. My only advice would be to get all the meat you want in one shot. I went up a second time to get just one more piece of chicken and a small piece of steak and it was an additional $4. They weigh the food with the plate, which is very heavy. I think when I went up for seconds I got overcharged. Otherwise I was very happy with my experience! Can't wait to go back!
label: POS

text: Very nice place to dine at. Every dish I ate there so far ended up being absolutly delicious. The staff is friendly and the owner puts in an effort to check on his guests. Some of the portions could be a little bigger, other then that two thumbs up. Recommendations: Appetizers: Fried Goat Cheese with a cherry glaze (phenomenal) Entrees: Fetuccini Portofino (Salmon / asparagus etc.) Filet Mignion New York Stip Rack of Lamb Desserts: Chocolate Mousse Cake Tiramisu Each dish was absolutely amazing!!!

text: Ok breakfast place. Our server was very nice, but the another one did nothing but bitch about another waitress that works there. Bitch in a very loud voice, relentlessly through our entire meal. If you stop in, sit as far away from the restrooms as possible. There's about 5 feet between the toilet and the closest table. text: Just because this place is better than the campus bookstore doesn't make it good. It's return prices are almost as bad, and its "buyer beware" attitude is off-putting. I feel like I'm at a carnival being grifted by carnies whenever I go to this place. Trust me, instead of having to walk anywhere for the express purpose of being ripped off, just go online and buy the books for half the price.

text: Wonderful place! Very clean, great toys, friendly staff who know their products and are willing to provide you advice if needed regarding your choice of pet food. We wandered into this place after reading reviews, a bit pricey on some of the toys and products, the price provided for the dog food is really cheap for the quality of food you will feed your precious pup. Have you ever gone through bags and bags of dog food only to use a scoop of it and the rest goes to waist because your dog is so fu@*n picky?? Welcome to my frustration with my pup.. The workers here gave us a quite a few samples of their line of healthy dog food. I tried one already and she did not like it, however I am happy to have had it as a sample only.. I will try the rest and hopefully find one that she likes.

text: Endless amounts of perfectly prepared and cooked meat served to you table side. Do you really need me to write anything else here? Oh yea, massive salad bar with amazing sides and fixings. Do you really need me to write anything else here? Oh yea, fried pallenta, fried plantans and mashed potatoe sides placed on your table throughout the meal. Do you REALLY need me to write anything else here?

text: I went to eat here with my boss on a business trip. Surprisingly, I had never been to a hibachi restaurant before. This place flat out sucks. Since we were seated at the grill by ourselves, they switched out the chef for a newbie that was slow and didn't know how to do anything. He also didn't understand English. We ordered the filet mignon and lobster and he cooked it way over well done. We kept telling him to stop, but it wasn't until someone else walked by and explained to him that we wanted medium rare. He started grilling again and we had to tell him to stop AGAIN. Anyway, he didn't know what he was doing, and I thought it was messed up that they swapped the chefs when they saw us come in. The grill next to us was full and they had the chef cook everything right, quickly, with some entertainment value. The only decent thing about the meal was the rasberry salad dressing, otherwise the rest of the food didn't taste very good. Yuck. The end.

text: I went to this salon thinking that I could get a nice short haircut. I wear my hair short but have not been able to find anyone that consisitently gives a good cut. I asked the receptionist for someone that specialized in short hair and she recommended Cate and I made an appt. I explained to her that I wanted it shorter on the sides and longer on top and to keep my bangs long. She gave me the worst haircut I have ever received in my life! The top is so short and choppy, I look like Fonzie. I have never cried over a haircut before, but this one made me cry. I am embarassed to leave the house. I would not recommend this salon to anyone and certainly not recommend Cate. I am not a very picky person when it comes to haircuts but this is horrible.
label: NEG

text: I'm probably the only person here who wasn't satisfied when I purchased a loaf of bread here. I remember coming here in a rush to pick up a loaf of bread for a little gathering I was supposed to attend. It's a good thing I ended up bailing on this open event. When I got home, and tried the multigrain loaf I had purchased, it was a disaster. I found the texture too dry, and almost impossible to break. Not to mention how difficult it was to chew it comfortably. My teeth were sore after a few pieces! I also found the bread lacked in flavor. My mom makes bread from scratch often, and I've been to quite a number of bakeries in my lifetime. Sorry, this place just doesn't do it for me. I kind of want to say it's pricey, but since it's an independent bakery, and they make everything themselves, I don't totally object. $4.25 for a baguette is a lot though...Even in France they don't charge so much. In summary, I wouldn't run to purchase here again.
label: NEG

text: Ian R., the author of the first Main Street Liquors review, certainly has a point. Main Street is a bit seedy, and most of their products are a bit overpriced. Like a lot of liquor stores up and down Gallatin Pike, Main Street does their best to just barely abide by the absurd state laws regarding selling liquor and beer in the same business. Main street has a little beer/convenience market right next door (in the same building), and they probably make up for the extra rent they have to pay by gouging prices on liquor. Main Street is a prime spot, if you're a street-wandering whino who doesn't know what typical liquor prices are to begin with. It's pretty far down on Gallatin, where things start to get exceptionally shady. Their selection is a bit limited, and there are plenty of other liquor stores to choose from north of Main Street. I'd recommend hitting one of those.
label: NEG

text: This place is a dump and need to be renovated... AGAIN... If you enjoy eating in the same room that your food is cooked (before the smoking ban, this was a bigger issue) this is the place for you... Not well lit and food is average at best...

text: I can't believe I've been coming here for two years. Hmm I guess its about time to take an inventory. Lets see... Beer selection is still unreal... Check Ghent Mussels still Rock... Check The Steak Frites Salad is still effing amazing... Check Yup, Still 5 big ones. Wouldnt see it any other way. text: This is 2nd Avenue's answer for beer selection. They offer more varieties on draft than any other establishment in the area (but not as many as Flying Saucer). This is more of a dive-y type bar than others around and is mostly populated by preppy looking college aged patrons. The bar is actually located in the basement of the building it is in, hence the name. It's on the very edge of the 2nd Avenue strip, so its a little quieter than a lot of its neighbors, but that doesn't mean that it doesn't get insanely packed. If you can go there during a quieter time, they have fooseball tables you can play as well as various bar type video games. It looks like a whole and the people can get pretty obnoxious at times. I've found that they have probably the worst staff at any bar I've been to in Nashville. The waitresses/bartenders tend to be pretty bitchy and unhelpful. I guess if I had to put up with drunk frat boys all the time I'd be that way too, but you get the impression that they hate everyone. They serve food here, but I've never tried it and don't actually know anyone who goes there that has. But it's nice to know if you happen to get hungry while you're there. Their happy hour is from 2-7 during the week and they have specials that vary daily. Sundays would be the best day to go as they have 2 for 1s and half price on all pitchers, but it gets pretty packed.
label: NEG

text: As a resident of South City, an Uncle Bill's visit is a must at some point. My brother and both of our significant others decided to try it out after a Blues game one night a couple of months ago. The first thing I noticed was the cloud of smoke that enveloped our party as I opened the door. Normally, that would be enough for me to turn around, but I wanted to give Uncle Bills a chance. When we were seated, I asked to be seated in the non-smoking section. I was notified rather bluntly that the booth was in fact in the non-smoking section, even though we were 5 feet away from a woman lighting up. At this point, we all reeked anyway so we decided to order. The silverware was dirty and our waitress had a few teeth missing. I decided to chalk this up as one of those "adventures" that we could remember for a while. The food was okay, nothing out of the ordinary. I was concerned about the cleanliness of the staff and the building itself. I don't think I'll be going here again unless I've had a few drinks.

text: -PINBALL ALERT!- Overall I could give here 3 stars, but I'm curving to 4 because when it comes to Timeless old school video arcades in Philadelphia this is the only one that really still exists (and it's kind of sad to say it). For a fairly small arcade it has a fairly balanced offering of games to enjoy. They have new school games like DDR alongside old school games like Mrs. Pacman, 3D fighters like Soul Caliber alongside quirky Japanese 2D fighters (and plenty of sharks that are waiting to school noobs in VS mode for each), and a couple of shooting and racing games. They even have a pool hall towards the back and and plenty of games where you can win tickets for prizes. But most importantly they have Pinball! they only have newer one's like Family Guy, Pirates Of The Caribbean and The Simpsons (at least since I last checked). But they were all pretty well maintained at least. While it might be filled with plenty of tweenagers on certain occasions, I'll take an old school spot over somewhere like Dave & Busters any day of the week!

We ordered dim sum as an appetizer, which took awhile to get served but was very delicious! The mini roll was especially crunchy and tasty. The receptionist was very friendly. She offered to check our coats, and actually put it on me when I was leaving the restaurant :) A good way to end the night!

I walked near the counter with the second half of my sandwich, and I did not even have to ask--despite the line, my server held out his hand and wrapped the half for me to take home. Overall, an excellent Sunday lunch and my go-to spot for a deli fix.
