text: After a huge disappointment at the nearby Yo My Goodness, my sweet tooth was still looking to be satisfied. Sweetie's was close by, and I've had it on my bookmarks for quite some time, so me and Andy stopped in. The place is quaint and cute, and reminds me of a 50's candy shop. Lots of jars of loose candy, etc. There was also a display of (REALLY small) cookies and ice cream. The ice cream didn't look to be that special. Neither did the (homemade?) cookies. I didn't want a snocone or an ice cream float (yes, they also offer those things!) So I went with a prepackaged cookie from "The Very Best Cookies". The cookie was pretty decent. So why only one star? The service SUCKED. The woman working the counter was snippy and rude, and practically hovered over us as we browsed around the store. I honestly would have liked to look around more, but her stares made things way too uncomfortable. I paid for my cookie and left. I see no reason to come back to this store. The candy offered wasn't unique; it was stuff I could easily buy at any grocery store. The ice cream didn't look special, nor did the cookies. And the service sucked. Two huge disappointments in the span of 20 minutes. I think that's a personal best for me.
label: NEG

text: I had heard tons of word-of-mouth reviews raving about this place, so when I finally made my way there I desperately wanted it to live up to the hype. I am always looking for a little gem around here, something new in the least, and but sadly this won't be my new "it" place. The atmosphere is very nice, if not surprising for its concrete strip-mall exterior. The martinis were good. We ordered an all-sushi dinner, and while it was tasty, I never hate sushi. It wasn't anything that interesting. And it was frustrating that the sushi entrees didn't come with miso or a salad with ginger dressing, which has always been standard in my experience. Overall, you can get much better sushi by traveling north a bit to Princeton and going to Ajihei. The atmosphere suffers, but the fresh fish is outstanding.
label: NEG

text: Contrary to popular belief, I don't hate all chain restaurants. I'd just rather support local joints. Sure I hate SOME chain places, like Applebees or Taco Bell, but that's more on account of their food being absolutely disgusting rather than a wholesale opposition to chains themselves. Take for instance....The Olive Garden. I don't hate the olive garden, but I just don't prefer it. Some members of my family LOVE the garden and request it for their birthday all the time. So I go. The food is uniform and somewhat bland, smothered in canned-tasting sauce, and the atmosphere is so patronizing it's almost kitsch (wow, it's like I'm eating at a REAL Italian restaurant!). But the prices are reasonable, the food is filling, and it doesn't make me sick (most of the time). So whatever, it's all good. Why did I waste all that time talking? Well, imagine if The Olive Garden stripped away all the decor, turned down the lights, put candles on the table, raised the prices by 50%, kept the same somewhat bland food, and offered the same level of service. Welcome to Paul Mineo's Trattoria! We arrived around 8:15 on a Saturday night. We made reservations, but quickly realized they were completely unnecessary, since we were one of 3 PARTIES IN THE ENTIRE RESTAURANT. A Saturday night. At 8:15. At an Italian joint. Bad sign #1. The owner greets us and says we should love the food, the cooks are from Sicily. Hmm...whenever someone feels the need to call something like that out, I know it's time to be skeptical. So whatever. We sit down and look at the menu. Their website has the menu online but conveniently leaves out the prices. When I look at their menu, I notice 2 things: #1: There is no dish on their menu under $18. Even the linguine alfredo (without chicken of course) #2: Their menu seems to be a fancied-up version of the olive garden. And when I say "fancied-up", I mean in font and language used, not as in the actual menu items, featuring such staples as "famous lasagna" and the same boring canneloni and chicken parmesan that every other boring italian restaurant has. Except here it was $20 instead of $15. Let me take the opportunity to say once again, I don't mind paying good money for good food. If you're being adventurous and creative and really putting an effort into making a dish, and pull it off, I'll pay through the nose for a meal. A great meal is worth paying a lot of money for. I'm just concerned with value here. Don't throw some pasta, bland sauce, and frozen vegetables on a plate and tell me I'm getting a value for $20. I'm not. So the food comes and we eat. It's alright. Big portions, not-so-great taste, but filling enough so no one really complains. I start to wonder if these "sicilian chefs" took cooking lessons at Macaroni Grill or Bravo. I'm also noticing that we're the only party left in the dining room and the waitstaff is essentially swooping out from under us to take our plates away. I look at my watch. It's 9:30. On a Saturday night. The place is dead quiet apart from the random and cheesy musical selections piped in (I felt like I was at an 80's prom). We wanted to split checks, and the waiter informs us that it will result in an automatic 20% gratuity added. Seriously? Is this really necessary? I'm not a bad tipper, but an automatic healthy gratuity added simply for splitting checks goes past annoying and becomes ridiculous. Do you really think a party of 2 is going to gyp you in a tip, buddy? I wasn't before, but maybe I will now. So we were finishing up, done paying the bill, just making small talk, when our waiter approaches us and tells us they're closing early since they're so dead and they'd appreciate it if we left. I look at my watch. It's 9:45. They're supposed to close at 10:00. You couldn't have waited an extra 5 minutes for us to wrap things up? We're essentially being rushed out the door because the waiter wants to get out of there. What is this, McDonald's? At least at Olive Garden I know they'll stay open until we're finished! This is about the 3rd or 4th different Italian restaurant that this space at Westport has occupied that I remember. As far as I'm concerned, it's all the same place with different names. Same menu, same chefs, hell I don't know, maybe same servers. Until they change things up and take this place more seriously (instead of trying to be an upscale chain joint), I expect yet another name change selling the same lazy italian standbys.
label: NEG

text: We hired them to move a small retail store from Boston to Miami. They said they would give us 24 hours notice before the goods arrived. I received a phone call at around 8:30 am that they are here in Miami and are ready to drop off the shipment. So much for the 24 hours notice. While making small talk I was asking if they were going to do anything in Miami or head straight back and the driver said "that depends on how much I tip him" From bad to worse, the driver disappeared before the first boxes could be unloaded and never showed up until it was ready to go. The 2nd guy only brought in a couple of small things and sat in the back of the truck most of the time. The 3rd guy was great, he worked hard to make me work as little as possible in helping him move some of the heavier items and make sure we were satisfied. I would give him 5 stars and the other 2 0 stars. I can't say how things were on packing end in Boston, but I couldn't recommend using Isaac's in the future.
label: NEG

text: This place was quite a treat. I had the opportunity to come here Sunday of Labor Day weekend. There wasn't much of a wait, which is a shame because while you wait you can view the garden and nursery or sit inside and sip on a pellegrino. We sat in the garden in one of maybe three tables. Expect a slow meal if you sit here and note there is only breakfast served on weekends. The food is as fresh as it gets and very flavorful. I wanted everything on the menu-- even the granola (which I refuse to order in a restaurant, on hungover mornings). The staff was very attentive and friendly. This place is a solid place for guests and the rents-- and very reasonably priced for what you get! I desparately wish there was something like this in San Fran!
label: POS

text: Great customer service! The food was ok and as the ratings said I've had better.
label: NEG

text: Since moving to the greater Philly area seven years ago WMMR has been number one on my radio dial. Well not exactly "dial", but number one button sounds kinda dumb. I first started listening when Casey was an intern and P and S were putting him through his paces during the "month of stunts". Then came a black period in which I had to move out of the area for a year to complete an internship. Since this was in the olden days before iPods and such I could only catch about 5 minutes of static filled signal of P and S in during my drive to work in the morning. I still found this five minutes of the P and S show funny, even through the static. Something people, who are critical of WMMR, should realize is how lucky we are to have a dedicated rock station in our market. Drive out of the WMMR listening range and I wish you luck finding rock station with the history and integrity of WMMR. Particularly if you head into rural PA where you will be forced to listen to pop rock stations, classic rock, or purchase radio. I'll be kind with my critique of DJs at other stations who cause me to scratch my head wondering how they actually got a job as a DJ. We are seriously spoiled by have such a great rock station in our area. My only two criticisms One is they tend to play a relatively small rotation of songs. Though this is countered by "Jackson's iPod" and "everything A-Z" weeks. Other critique. There are times were I get a tad annoyed by P and S because they will kill a clip or sound bite to death. That is it though. As far as the other DJ, Pierre Robert is awesome. Who else loves Philly as much as he does or knows the history of rock and roll in philly more? I'm also a huge fan of Matt Cord and Jackson. MMR Rocks!
label: POS

text: If you like Brazilian barbecue, you MUST get in your car or take a looong bus ride to this place. Every single this is delicious. You can choose to either pay by weight per plate or $21 dollars for all you can eat. I would suggest going when you want a bigger meal and just getting the all you can eat option, since paying by plate only ends up being a few dollars cheaper. It's great being able to sample a little of everything. The skirt steak is my favorite and is absolutely amazing. There aren't any signs or descriptions on the salad bar, so you kind of just have to grab what looks good to you. That's part of the downside to the restaurant - there is little guidance on how to operate the place from the staff. It's BYOB and the crazy amount of meat consumption goes along well with a bottle of red wine.
label: POS

Not sure how that happened, but they were a bit slower than normal because of it, but at least they noticed us. Food here isn't anything remarkable, but the TBM and wasabi roast beef sandwiches are usually acceptable. Chai Tea Latte is decent, although the House Coffee has no refills.

text: I eat at natural cafe once a week there are 3 locations in santa barbara 1 downtown, and 2 in goleta the downtown one is the most convenient because its on state street and you can sit outside. there are so many options, even if you aren't a vegetarian. i recommend the sauteed tofu, the Caesar Salad (its vegan), the tempeh, the hummus and any of the vegetarian entress including the tacos and the yogi special. -the items that aren't typically found in "healthy" restaurants like nachos are great in my opinion but they aren't going to be your guilty pleasure items as if you went to a mexican restaurant.

text: First, for the money, the location and the service, you can't beat this place. In fact, I recommended that 2 different people stay here when asked about my trip to New Orleans. Beyond just the service, the cool hotel and the location the POOL ON THE ROOF IS ONE OF THE BEST POOLS I HAVE EVER BEEN TO. After drinking and staying out late, there's nothing like going up to the roof, having room service delivered and laying on plush chairs overlooking the city. Five stars: - top notch service and incredibly nice staff - nice old hotel, with very cool chandeliers and marble - Great location (2 blocks from bourbon street, but completely out of the hustle bustle) also very close to charles street trolley - ROOF POOL Two stars: - Older and shows in areas - Rooms are nice, but not top notch Average: Four Stars
label: POS

text: There's lots of love for Honey's but not from me. Everyone raves about the brunch, but I wasn't too hungry so just went with coffee and a bowl of veggie chili. Well, it was called veggie chili, but it was not very chili like. It was bland and completely dry, like it came from a bean dip that was sitting out for hours under a hot lamp, with a huge glob of sour cream on top. Their menu is huge, and perhaps that's a problem. Items that probably aren't ordered as much also don't get much attention. Service was ok, but my coffee cup sat empty for a while. The coffee was nothing to write home about. Also, any non-fast food style restaurant that only takes cash automatically loses a point from me. If I go back, I'll try some pancakes and maybe have a better review. If you find yourself at Honey's stay away from the veggie chili.
label: NEG

text: Two words: Greasy Beans. Ok, more than two words. This place is literally two blocks away from my house. Why, WHY can't it be good? I just don't like this place. Just go to Juanito's or any other stand, and it will be just as good, if not better, and cheaper.

Brunch is offered pretty much all day, and the menu has fresh ideas and a rotating daily special. I've had polenta cakes, eggplant towers, a delicious re-take on huevos rancheros, a simple bagel with lox, and amazing homemade cookies. The selection is always diverse and while sometimes a little pricey (any coffee beverage + food will run you around $10 - 20), the results are always worth it. The baristas are very talented as well, often winning local awards for their beverages. The place is always jammed and the internet is always slow, and I'm docking them a star because they took out a lot of their electrical outlets over the past year to discourage lengthy sit-ins by students or wi-fi addicts. It's in a perfect neighborhood--one of midtown's only neighborhood districts, so people watching is great and you are always sure to see someone you know enjoying a mocha or yazoo beer. And you can't beat this place in the summer time, it just feels so alive! All in all, my favorite cafe in Nashville.

What did they charge? 390! I said, "What about the $360?" They said it was 360 before tax. A total lie! I protested, but they wouldn't budge. I was already late for work (since this was getting to be 10am) so I then asked about the warranty. They said 90 days labor!! I said "What happened to lifetime??" They conversed and said "Ok, 1 year labor." Wow. What a bunch of liars and con artists. I will never go back here again and I agree with the first review of this place. What a bunch of crooks.

text: Started an account so I can yelp this place into the ground.... One of the worst dining experiences I've had eating out. Refer to amee m's review; I was there so I can vouch for the experience. There were 6-7 parties ahead of us written on the list (not physically waiting) when we got there, and it was written that they would "come back" though we honestly saw several empty tables. We were told the wait was still 45-50 minutes. Later I realized that the maitre'd must have turned them away because they were short help with the kitchen and waiting staff. The maitre'd had to clear and set the table for us herself and service from the waiter was very, very slow. It seemed like forever between the appetizers and the main course, which was odd, since we saw the chef out in the dining room, not to chat with diners, but to shoot the bull with some of the servers. Keep in mind, this is Fri night, the night of the week where they might expect at least a few diners?? But I guess when your food standards are so low, it doesn't really matter how much time you spend in the kitchen. The chicken tortilla soup was an overly salty concoction. We contemplated pouring some water into the soup to make it edible. Sirloin steaks were made of leftover jerky meat, and I suggested to my companion that the restaurant spring for some Safeway Rancher's Reserve next time for a more tender cut... The buns on both burgers we ordered came well done (top and bottom). This was a first, as I thought they only prepared the meat that way if you asked for it. (I looked to the table across from us, and they were blessed with similarly charred buns...) We scraped the cancerous parts off the buns and the rest of the burger was mediocre, so I was told. Back to the drawing board, boys... Now onto the dessert, something that should be a cakewalk (pardon the pun)? My cheesecake came out partially liquefied in the middle and tasted like it looked, pasty and raw. It was left untouched after a taste and I wondered how any self-respecting chef would let that monstrosity leave the kitchen. My companion had a raspberry chimichanga that she said was good, though I didn't see her finish it.. When the waiter asked us at the end how the meal was, I mentioned the charred buns and was immediately rebuffed. "We told the chef, but he likes it that way. What are you going to do?" Indeed... Onto the positives: The bread that came out before our meal was decent, nicely warmed, though some of the end bits were rock-like. The artichoke dip appetizer was also a hit, which made the rest of the meal all the more disappointing. And lest you think they got it entirely right, it only came with three toasted baguette slices... for a whole bowl of dip. We walked out vowing we would get revenge on Circus Circus via the craps tables. PS: Waiter had never heard of a Malibu and Coke... subtract another star. text: Terrible. There really isn't any other way for me to describe this shop. I stared at a blank space for a few moments wrestling with a less abrasive way to put it, but there really isn't one. I actually don't know where to start, but i'll try... A recent Via-ctim showed me their unfortunate purchase-- a terribly heavy bike-boom era Raleigh (step-through) with chipped paint, a torn saddle (typical couch-cushion), rust pretty much everywhere you can imagine, old cottered cranks and a browning chain (it'd been cleaned and lubed, but that's really it). She's 5'0" even; the bike is roughly 52cm, maybe larger. The saddle was SLAMMED to the frame in a half-hearted attempt to accommodate her height, but even still her arms were stretched way out and she had to lean forward to reach the brakes. All for-- get ready-- $200. It's likely that the bicycle garnered this price a few decades ago when it was brand new and unridden. Today, i'd say it would be fair to ask maybe $50-$70 if it were in exceptionally good condition. This one was certainly not. I don't know of a single bike shop in philadelphia (other than Via, of course) who'd be OK with selling someone a bicycle in such disrepair with this poor a fit. Shame on you, Via... Another example can be found from a Yelper on this very page: "He then even asked his repair guy to get me a quote if I were to swap out the flatbars for dropbars. When that came out to $225, I decided I might just want to get a new bike altogether." $225 to swap out a set of bars. I can't vouch for this reviewer's story, but i'm certainly not surprised. There was another instance where I went in to purchase a chain ring with a slightly less-than-ubiquitous BCD for a home repair i wanted to make at the last minute. Despite being familiar with their practices, i figured-- being pretty experienced with bicycle maintenance-- that an in person visit would be fine. Guess again. When i asked the price for the part once it was in my hand, i felt a little uncomfortable with what i heard. Knowing that the price was way over what it was worth (the ring's teeth were well worn), i asked the person i spoke to if he could give me a more reasonable price (and explaned why). When he went to grab the owner, i was given a relatively firm answer ("no"). As i put the ring down, i noticed it wobbled from side to side-- it wasn't flat, but BOWED. When i pointed this out, the owner grinned and asked if i wanted it for a bit cheaper. Needless to say, i walked out immediately. The unfortunate thing about Via-- well, the MOST unfortunate; there are definitely many-- is the fact that newer riders feel they're getting a good deal. They see a working bicycle and a price slightly cheaper than they find at shops who aren't in the business of deceiving their customers and think they've found a shop that cares. What they don't realize, though, is that they've actually bought something worth so little that other bike shops (second hand or otherwise) would never sell this sort of thing to an unsuspecting customer. If you go through the reviews, you'll notice a certain trend: New, inexperienced or unsure consumers stopping in for a first bicycle or a tube change under a five star rating, followed by a one or two star rating from someone who went in for something a bit more substantial. That's the thing with Via-- if you need an innertube or know little about bicycles, everything will seem kinda neat. The creaky wooden floors, the dusty old bicycles with character, the hustle and bustle, the almost-rude staff... this can all seem a bit romantic to someone who recently moved to the city and wants to buy a first bike, or simply someone who never rode before and decided to start. But under the hood, this is by and large a horrible bicycle shop packed with what i can only guess are cheap bulk lots of old worthless bicycles bought for pennies and sold after VERY minimal work for dollars. Stay FAR away. If you want a fair price on a bicycle you can afford or want something with the character of an older 70s or 80s build, visit the Bike Church (google philadelphia bike church). You'll get a far better bike for much closer to what it's worth without any of the BS. PS-- sorry this review got a little wordy. I initially logged in to type a few sentences, but every time i think about another person who went in there and got ripped off, it really starts to make me realize what a crap business Via is.

When I arrived at 8:00a, they were just opening up their clean, organized shop, putting out the flags, and getting ready for business. By the early afternoon, the owner of the shop called and clearly explained the problems before going ahead with any work, and even offered to take my van to get emissions retested for me for free - definitely shows that they are confident in their work. Had I gone to a local gas station, I'm guessing they would have played with the timing and idle speed and gotten it to barely pass emissions. At EAT, they did a very careful diagnosis (including compression testing) and helped my van run better and pass with flying colors. While the price was more than I wanted to pay (isn't is always?), I think it's always a good deal in auto service when your car is cared for by people who are experience, skilled, and careful in auto repair. Can I say....yum Yum YUm YUM!!!! Everything was very well executed and the crab cakes werent falling apart. They were that perfect combo of sticky enough to stay together but loose enough to come right apart where you can taste the chunks of crab... (mouth is watering reliving this delight!). PS: Twenty Manning gives your table awesome warm bread to share, don't over load because the meals are filling, but I recommend trying at least a small piece. For my main course, I had the Seared Candied Scallops, (clearly I was on scallop overload that night). I'm a fan of seafood and these scallops were seared to perfection, a golden crust outlining each piece and as sides came roasted pumpkin and sauteed spinach. I am a huge pumpkin lover and this was a great healthy alternative to roasted potatoes. One of my colleagues ordered the and another the salmon, everyone was raving. It was thrilling to have food that both tasted good and was good for you. Afterwards we were able to lounge around, have a few drinks and soak up the trendy dim lit atmo... would we go there again? The potatoes, of course, were instant. No butter, no gravy. Just plain bad. Now, I'll critique the apps last, as they really were just an afterthought. text: The Mercy Lounge is the favorit-est of my favorite venues in Nashville. Almost all of the bands I like, local and touring, play here at least once when they come through town. It's a smaller, intimate type venue where you can get right up in a performer's face if you want or you can chill out off to the side at a table. It's what I'd picture my own club to be if I was lucky and financially secure enough to have one. Their main bar is long and decorated with vintage pin-up girl characters which helps lend to its rock-n-roll attitude. One of the best things about the Mercy Lounge is it's variety of shows that come there. I think it's one of the few, if not the only, venues in town which are not type-casted to a specific genre or music. Their calendar hosts bands from all ranges of the music spectrum and some weeks I can find myself there almost every night. They have a full bar with a decent selection of beer on draft, you can get local brew Yazoo here which is alright by me. Their drink pricing is pretty standard for a venue but they offer drink specials sometimes on nights they do events with local bands. Every Monday night they have 8 off 8th which is a hosting of various local musicians and bands that rotates from week to week. It's always free and it's a good place to be to cure the Mondays. They have a couple of pool tables and some booths in the back room which is a fun place to hang out in-between sets or during an opening band you're not interested in. They have a limited menu, which I have yet to try, but it looks like you're run of the mill 'i've drank a little too much and need to munch on something to clear my head' kind of bar food. Not overtly disgusting but nothing really to excite me into trying the fare. Their door man is touted as the best in Nashville and the bartenders are nice, but usually busy. The parking lot is limited so come early if you don't want to pay, otherwise the independent lot next door can range anywhere from $5 to $15 depending on the expected turn out and how evil the people that own it feel like being. Another thing to note is that the Mercy Lounge tends to sell out easily, especially for bigger name bands. It's best not to wait on buying tickets to shows here or you might find yourself standing in the parking lot hoping someone has a mercy ticket they'll throw your way. Also its located in the middle of an industrial district next to the railroad tracks, so there isn't really anything within walking distance. So if you feel like continuing your evening somewhere else after a show at the Mercy Lounge I suggest you keep your alcohol intake down to a beer or two.

text: (This is for the Hillsborough location.) I'm from California which features an embarassment of good, cheap Vietnamese restaurants. Chauvinistically, I wasn't expecting much from this place, but I went anyway, desperate for some of that delicate Vietnamese flavor I love so well. I shouldn't have worried. The food was very good. We began with the Chao Tom Nuong, which is the do-it-yourself spring roll with ground shrimp pattie ($11.95). The price may be somewhat high but the platter was absolutely tremendous, and they boil the rice-paper wrappers for you instead of leaving it up to you, unlike other places.The plate came with the shrimp, pickled radish and carrot, mint leaves, cucumber, and a big pile of vermicilli noodles with friedd garlic on top - delicious.The shrimp pattie was delicious with a taste somewhat indicative of dim-sum, and the vegetables accompanying were very fresh. However, they didn't give us any cilantro! We moved on to our lunch choices. I ordered the Bun Muc Nuong ($7.50) which is Grilled Squid over vermicelli noodles, although I added a portion of grilled shrimp for a few bucks extra. The seafood was tasty and had a good charred taste, although the squid got just a little bit too soft. The bowl provided a generous portion of vegetables along with the noodles - in fact, it was definitely the biggest vermicelli noodle bowl I'd ever seen. (Portions are always bigger in the South...even in Vietnamese restaurants.) I poured a big bowl of fish sauce over it and went to town. Delicious, fresh, and marginally healthy. My grandmother had the Bun Cari Ga or Curry Chicken Soup ($6.50) which came in a tremendous bowl, along with fresh vegetables (cilantro, mint, bean sprouts, jalepeno) for garnish. It had a rich coconut milk flavor and was full of chicken, carrot, eggplant, and potato, along with the standard rice noodles. It was very tasty, but so gigantic that she could barely finish a third of it. (I sense a VERY cheap way to eat for at least two days.) The restaurant is set in what was an old steakhouse space and it looks it - very big and not too bright inside. Seating is at booths, and wooden chopsticks are provided to you without asking. Our server was quick and efficient - food came out at a steady clip, despite the restaurant seeming to do a booming business at lunch time. Conclusion: Very good Vietnamese food in a somewhat unlikely part of town. I'll definitely be back next time I find myself in Tampa.

A friend bought me a fat wedge of classic Beemster after she tried some at a Christmas party. It's aged a minimum of 18 months, tastes dense, tangy and nutty, pairing well with wine, or port. Delicious to just eat as little slices, melting on your tongue. So, I received that cheese last December, and I cut away at it all year. Eight months later, I still have a good knob and it's remained in decent condition, just less moisture content now. I grated it into a fine soft pile with a microplane and it can now be mixed in dressings, sprinkled on grilled vegetables, and used in place of parmigiano reggiano with the similar sharp tang, but different flavor. If this kind of cheese intrigues you, scamper on down to Lazy Acres. Note: I have shied away from the ready-meal deli section. It looks good, but two friends of mine who've bought stuff from that section twice, each got dysentery twice afterwards and had never suffered from that before, and have never gotten it since. text: I was on the way back from wine tasting up in Paso Robles on a Saturday night and a group of us wanted to get a bite to eat while we were passing through SB on our way back south. I fired up Yelp and found this place and Zen Yai Thai. Galanga not so great and Zen with a better rating. When I look up places to eat, I look at the reviews and number of people reviewing. I try to go with places that have a lot of reviews, high rating, and detail of reviews. A place that gets a 4 / 5 start rating with a lot of people reviewing tends to be more accurately represented when compared to a place with only a few reviewers but with a 4 / 5 star rating - that's just my opinion. We parked and walked by Zen Yai but to no avail, it was packed and what looked to be a wait. We then proceeded up State and passed All India Cafe. I noticed a Zagat rating but didn't see the ratings up close. I don't consider myself a "foodie" or "food snob." I actually abhor those terms - I just know what tastes good (to me) and how dishes should be executed. Usually I'll use Zagat, Gayot, Citysearch, and even Michelin as references for places to eat but when I'm on the go, Yelp is what I use. I've written reviews for Zagat so thought All India would be ok but one of the guys in the group insisted we go to Galanga further up the street so off we went since it was "close" to authentic Thai food. Close as in a 1000 yards close or the size of a pack of peanuts close? First off, I want to preface this review that when people use the word "authentic," I personally believe it's open to interpretation and is subjective rather than objective. What one person may think is really good and authentic, may not necessarily be true from another person's perspective. I try not to use "authentic" in any of my reviews but may be guilty from time to time. Also, when I mention a dish was executed means whether or not a dish comes through with flavor profiles and is finished well. You could have a grilled cheese sandwich with soggy bread and unmelted cheese, which in my opinion would not be executed well. The intent was there but not executed. Anyhow, we arrived at Galanga and the place looked a bit...grimy. Someone needs to get a carpet steamer up in here and get some cleaning going. Nothing special about the interior; I noticed various pictures hanging on the wall - probably family members. We ordered the Green Curry Chicken - hot, Garlic Pepper squid, and Pra Luck chicken. The green curry had watered down coconut milk along with carrots, peas, and green beans in addition to chicken. Strange, I've never had carrots, peas, and green peas in any green curry dish at other Thai restaurants. The Garlic Pepper squid was executed well - flavor wise but the squid was chewy; this is a sign of either overcooking or undercooking. The Pra Luck Chicken tasted ok - the only thing I liked was the fact that the spinach was fresh. The only saving grace was the fish sauce with chili condiment. It made the dishes taste somewhat better. I think when Galanga first opened, the dishes I'm sure were very tasty and done well but I believe over the years either the technique was not passed down correctly or someone is cutting corners. So in short, I won't be coming back to this place considering I've had better tasting Thai food elsewhere. Service was spot on - no problem there. For the quality of food, I think the pricing is high.

The appetizer arrived quite promptly - 6 pieces of ravioli in butter sauce, accompanied by a good amount of bread "for dipping in the butter sauce". My favorite was the sweet potato tart (tart is my name for it, the chef might not agree) that was the side. My husband's choice had exceeded his expectation, he said. I am not a big fan of French haute cuisine but this was country-style - bolder, heartier and much to my liking. By 7:00 pm, they had one duck and one filet available. text: i tried the new Seasons 52 for lunch today at the Cherry Hill Mall. I didn't expect much, but I was pleasantly surprised. The big thing with this place is that their menu changes every season. This means the rewrite the menu 4 times per year. My waitress, Beth, explained this to me as I sat at the bar and sipped a Fuji water. Everything looks really nice as far as decor and ambiance goes. If I had to describe it in one word i would say, sophisticated. I had a plain rosemary and parmesan flat bread and a ceaser salad with medium cooked steak and mushrooms. The flat breads seem to be their specialty. I saw many tables getting these. They have about 8 or so to choose from with all kinds of toppings. I went with the plain flat bread. The bread was presented in a cone. It was crunchy, but yet a little softer on the inside portions. I liked it. The salad came in this cylinder tower thing. My waitress removed the cylinder and the salad just fell together on my plate. I think this really adds some pizz azz to the presentation. I like having stuff done in front of me. Speaking of which, they have an open kitchen. I looked over and saw the chefs all line up and cooking. This is good because you can see how clean their working space is. The salad was fantastic. The steak was grilled perfectly. They put huge slices of red, yellow, and green grilled pepper in the salad. All the vegetables were grilled perfectly with not a whole lot of char marks. They pride themselves by how fresh their ingredients are and it really shows in their food. They also have an extensive wine list. It was to early for me to drink, so I had to give the alcohol a pass. Next time I go it will be for a much fuller meal. I really like this place, and I think it will do very well in it's location. I'm going to go out on a limb and give them 5 stars just because I can't even begin to criticize them on any level of their service. If you're going to the Cherry Hill Mall, you should definitely stop by and try this place out. You won't be sorry you did.

I ordered my lamb medium, and it ranged from bloody to rare. I had to literally saw through the large chunks to cut off a bite small enough to chew, and chewing it was a massive undertaking. The rice was water-saturated and flavorless. The green beans were canned! And this was for like $17 a plate or something. My husband also hated the rice, and said his shrimp were flavorless. Neither of us finished our food. Then, no one ever came to check on us or give us a bill, so I just put the gift certificates down and left. text: :: the birthday kid, part III :: hating on starr restaurants is like cobra kai beating up on daniel-san. just because all the kewl kidz are doing it, don't mean it's for me...at least when it comes to alma de cuba. i'd previously only been to alma for drinks - probably about 5 times in as many years - and each time i enjoyed sipping sangria in the swanky downstairs lounge. this past december, lucky me got to head upstairs for more than just a trip to the ladies room when the boy took me here for a day-after-my-birthday birthday dinner. it was a bitter cold nite outside, tho you'd never know it inside the invitingly warm alma interior with lights low...candles aglow... were we instantly transported to cuba? not even close. but the mood was perfectly set for a budding romance on a special occasion. drink orders placed - mojito for him, dark & stormy for me - we diverted our gaze from one another and towards our respective menus. my selections were easily made as, in typical restaurant fashion, the veg options are limited. while the boy continued to peruse, i dug in to the warm mini rolls placed before us by our server. only a little tho, as to not ruin my appetite for the black bean soup (topped with crema fresca & 3 rice croquettes) that would soon be my first course - and good thing for that, as i savored every thick, soupy spoonful! meanwhile, the boy was gushing over each bite of his yellowtail ceviche. he pleaded with me to change my non-meat-eating ways...assuring me that i wouldn't regret my decision upon tasting the other-worldy magnificence upon his plate. 'A' for effort, but i of course declined, to which i believe he was secretly grateful in that he did not have to relinquish a mere morsel of his new-found heaven on earth. his second course, the vaca frita, was destined to pale in comparison to the ceviche, of which he continually wished he had ordered a double portion of instead. my entree, the pionono, was a puerto rican sweet plantain roulade of zucchini, basil-tomato sauce & queso fresco served with roasted garlic & broccoli rabe - and it delivered. the flavors and textures of each ingredient meshed perfectly, altho i refrained from cutting into the stinking rose on date nite...instead pushing it to the side to be wrapped up with my uneaten half for lunch the following day when the promise of a kiss was not in my immediate future :) dessert, having been skipped the nite before, was inevitable, however, when our banana tres leches was brought to the table, it arrived sans candles, despite the boy having made mention of my birthday when he made the reservation. shame, shame, alma! all in all, a small hiccup in an otherwise stellar birthday celebration.

text: Haven't used their shipping or packing services, this is solely for the fun time I had getting a passport photo on Saturday. We got off to a bad start before we even arrived. The following conversation ensues: (My wife) My husband needs to renew his US passport, do you take passport photos? (Employee - in angry tone) Yes, but only for American passports. (My wife) Ok we will be right down. (Employee - still pissy) Fine, but just for American passports. Sheesh. You'd think the fact that my wife asked about a US passport would be a clue, but apparently the accent was too much for this genius to process. Needing the photos, and undaunted, we ventured down to South Reno. We walk in and there is one customer there and a handful of bored looking employees. An employee (clearly the one from the phone) comes up to help. I tell her I am here to get a passport photo. She runs through the "we only do US passport photos" schpeel again and I rush her along as that's what I need. She fumbles with the camera, take a photo and then says it will be 2-3 minutes and proceeds to head back behind the counter. Seemingly bored with me she sends some other poor schmuck out to retrieve the photos. He picks up the camera and sighs. I briefly think of making him retake it, but can't be bothered. I'll spend the next DECADE staring at this sucker. Having to go through the mess again is that bad. But wait, we aren't done. They then ring me up (American passport woman returns to do the honors) and it costs--wait for it--$13.95. Yes a full $14 for two tiny head shots. What a rip off. If you need a passport photo, do yourself a favor and go somewhere--anywhere--but here. Ugh.

text: Not a big fan of this casino. Personally I think the only place anyone should gamble is Las Vegas. At least in Vegas you feel like you're having fun even if you lose, in Edmonton it's just downright depressing. The main floor is huge. It is filled with blackjack tables in the center and a bunch of other table games, that I have no clue about, surrounding them. Slot machines make up the rest of the floor along with a small bar. Upstairs has a poker room which is the only game I would play or watch. If you look around the casino, everyone just looks depressed or shady as if they are up to no good. I don't recommend going to any casino in the city but if you must, steer clear of this one.
label: NEG

text: Columbia Restaurant at The Pier, St. Petersburg, FL My husband, in-laws, and I arrived at the restaurant at approximately 1p on Sunday, August 23, 2009. We were seated quickly. The restaurant was fairly empty as they were only seating in one area of the restaurant. Approximately 7 to 8 tables were occupied. We waited approximately 7 minutes for our waiter to come to the table. He asked for our drink order of 3 teas and 1 diet coke. After another 5 minutes, he brought our drinks and left. Approximately 10 minutes later he took our orders. He brought our bread about 15 minutes later. He then brought soup for my father-in-law and some salad, but gave the salad to the wrong person at our table after another 10 minutes. After waiting another 7 minutes to get his attention to ask about it, we finally got the order straightened out. Our food was brought to us approximately 20 minutes later. Each of us had completely drank all of our purchased beverage and our water. He did not refill our drinks at all while we waited and ate our bread. I had to ask him to refill our glasses after he brought most of our food out. I asked for more bread, and was never brought any nor did he ever acknowledge that he forgot. Our food was great, but I lost my appetite after waiting and never receiving the bread. I ended up eating a few bites, and pushing it away. I understand great food takes time, and I have no issue with that. I am extremely disappointed in the level of customer service we received from our waiter. As he only had 2 tables the entire 2 1/2 hours we were there, I expect that our drinks would always be full and that he would be attentive to all our needs. I do not believe I will be returning to this restaurant, and I strongly urge anyone else not to waste their money also.
label: NEG

text: Wow, really? $11 for a round of mini golf? And for your $11 you get broken down courses that are in dire need of maintenance, a bare bones arcade that doesn't even have a snack bar and more restrictions on behavior then the heavily regulated casinos down the road. It's not to say that I didn't have fun with my friends, just that this is a sorry excuse for a mini-golf course. We chose the "castle" course, where the faded and bizarre statuettes that represent the theme are, for the most part, malfunctioning or absent. One hole had a mechanical apparatus that clearly used to be a working decoration, but is now just a rusted and odd edition to the course. The course has a ton of restrictions- open container = $500 fine, no more than 4 in a group, no more than 6 swings per hole per player, golf holes in order (even if a group of small children is taking over 20 minutes ahead or you), no swinging above your knees, no food on the course, no cursing, no non-golfers on the course, no, no, NO. Some of these I'll grant are common sense, but cumulatively they make you feel like you're under surveillance. Skip it and go bowling!!!
label: NEG

text: Very late-travel day dinner for our small group of uninformed travelers. What a pleasant surprise. Instead of the usual bread and butter pre-meal nosh, the geniuses at Deanie's serve perfectly cooked whole (steamed? boiled?) red potatoes! Creamy and ever so slightly spicy and very addictive! If you are fortunate to be informed that CRAB NACHOS are on the menu that day, get them! Absolutely the best nachos of all time. Served on fresh homemade potato chips!! 'nuff said I wanted to try something completely new for me and had the spinach salad which is served with a generous portion of fried oysters on top. Glad I ordered it. It was a taste of the region and quite delicious. Plus, nothing that I would regret when going to bed not-so-much later. We were lucky to be seated without a reservation (9pm-ish). Throughout the rest of our stay in NOLA, Deanie's was pretty much packed.
label: POS

text: I just had to update because the Italian Cream cupcake was absolutely incredible and really fresh and my service was really friendly. In the words of Peter Griffin, that is all. Also, this place has been renamed: it's now The Cup.
label: POS

text: Indian Fast food. Period. The location is convenient and the service is quick. But I would not send anyone here who is looking for quality Indian cuisine. The meat is always over cooked. And the food is served on disposable plates with plastic utensils, something I would willingly overlook if the food tasted better. Not that its totally bad. For the price and proximity to the city, you get, well, fast food. It fills you up, but it's nothing to write home about. I remember when I first moved here, I would ask around for a great place to get Indian food. I was meet with thoughtful sighs and was told that when Minar Palace closed, so did the last great place to get Indian food in the city. So, I was stoked when this place re-opened in this new location. I was so ready to try the food that so many Philadelphians thought was lost - but alas, I was totally underwhelmed by the experience. This is a great place to grab a quick bit to eat. But you can find better flavors and better cooked Indian food in the city. You just have to look for it.
label: NEG

text: The best Chinese food you will ever have, served by the most caring owners in the entire world. Not only did I work on and off for Old Peking throughout college, the owners always treated me like family. Unfortunately, they closed a couple years ago. On the last night they were open I stopped in for a final meal, walked around to say goodbye to the owners, saw they were taking some pictures with aunts and uncles and siblings in the main dining room, and hung back to say my goodbyes during a picture break. This was ridiculous, apparently, and they basically "forced" me into taking some family pictures with them. The owners have a cool story. Kin Sun's husband is an American she met while he was in the service. She barely spoke any English, they were able to fall in love anyway, and she ran away from home to be with him instead of marrying the rich doctor her father had chosen for her. Eventually, her brother convinced the family to give this guy a chance, and everything ended happily ever after. I miss Old Peking! They always served us dinner before the evening shift, and I tried literally everything on the menu. It was all awesome. There is a new Chinese restaurant in the building now, but I've never been because I don't want to ruin the Old Peking memories I have.
label: POS

Because of #1, it woke us up earlier than we liked. We called the front desk every. single. day. Once, it took them about 30 minutes to come upstairs and turn it off. text: Pho 75 is one of the first Pho places thats really famous, thats because a Johnny came lately in Pho Hoa is yet to be discovered. The soup here is great but clearly its just a Pho place that lacks the personality of the folks over at Pho Hoa . I hope they take pointers that it takes more than just good soup to get good ratings by word of mouth. The menu is so limited here , when you step inside its like youre in some dingy eatery in Southeast Asia I guess they keep it that way to have a more authentic feel to it. It is dirt cheap also I see a lot of people getting into this Pho thing which is quite a very refreshing meal in itself. No credit cards here too... Barnacles!!! Walk across the 11th street and go to Pho Hoa instead look for "Thien "he is the man at Pho Hoa the guy with the glasses and gelled hair.

text: Bouchon is a cozy, elegant yet casual place. The service was outstanding. The waiter suggested excellent wine pairings and really knew the menu. We had two seasonal first courses - the duo of carrot soup and roasted root vegetable salad. The carrot soup was simple and tasty. The salad was one of the best I've had. Beautifully roasted vegetables, arugula, hazelnut, crispy chickpeas and a great vinaigrette. The duck was cooked perfectly and the succotash was smokey and sweet. The lamb was flavorful. We ended with the blueberry upside down cake which was perfectly balanced. A great coffee too. They focus on locally grown food and prefer local wine. An excellent place to go for a great meal.

text: Apparently I ordered the wrong thing at this place. 'Tis what you get when you go somewhere to eat without first consulting Yelp... The place has a nice relaxed atmosphere, and staff were friendly. Chain restaurants seem to have overtaken the surrounding few blocks, and it's decent as a non-chain restaurant option. Food wise? Turkey sandwich was pretty blah - looked like prepackaged turkey slices that were grilled + some cheese on white sandwich bread. Was improved with a dunking into chipotle hot sauce. Take away? Check it out, unless you have an affinity for Applebee's. Check Yelp BEFORE you go, so you know what to order. Skip the turkey sandwich.

text: This is a regular spot for my family. There are several things that I love about this place: 1. Without a doubt they have friendliest staff in the city. They truly are a remarkable group of people that go out of their way to serve you. 2. Fresh real food. There may be a lot of butter on your toast, but you know what? It is the best damn butter that they can buy. You can even buy it there. 3. One of the only places in the city with a cheese course. I like cheese (my problem), many restaurants have done away with wine and cheese. They have not. 4. Excellent crepes. Dining is about the entire experience. They have great food, GREAT SERVICE, great atmosphere, and my repeat business. Yes, it is expensive, but when food, service, and atmosphere are top notch, then I really don't care as mush about the tab.

text: I brought my neighbor here last week for what was my third visit. We tried a sandwich item that you can have with beef, pork or chicken, and we split a veggie burrito. She loved everything and so did I. Each of these items was only $4. We split a cheese pupusa and it was great too. These cost $1.75. It's taken me a while to find out what's good here. I do like the empanadas but the price has been raised to $4 for three. You really can only eat one, so I don't reccomend ordering this for just yourself. There's definitely a language barrier here, but we struggle through. Also, half the menu is translated, and half of it isn't. Asking the son or mother (who always wait tables and cook) what's what on the menu is bound to be an adventure, so be prepared. Where family run restaurants are concerned, I am learning as I go. Above all else, I've learned the hours are flexible when you are your own boss. Therefore, if there's no one in the restaurant they will close at 7PM despite posted hours of being open until 8PM. Just to be safe, give them a ring if you plan to go after 6:30 PM. I know how hard they work and the long hours they put in, so I can't be mad about this even though it's a pain in the rear.

text: I have tried four times to give this place a chance. One time they weren't sure whether or not they were serving food but thought maybe somebody could make us something. Uh, no thanks. Another time I had a less than mediocre hamburger while shouting to be heard by my dining companions. I left feeling dirty. A third time I had the worst fish and chips of my life. The fourth time I figured, well, I guess its mostly a bar, so I'll have a drink. It was so unpleasant up by the bar. There were flies zipping around, the room was overheated, and the crowd was bizarrely unfriendly and dull for what is reputed to be a hipster scene. When I walk into SPTR I know and feel and believe that I'm in my friendly neighborhood, even if I don't know anybody there, but not so for POPE. I swear it was like I was in an inhospitable foreign country. I left before I even got the drink.

The meat was very tender. It is BYOB, there is a state liquor store very close. You can buy the margarita mix at the place if you want. The only problem is this place is kind of expensive and they only take CASH. I would definitely come back though.

text: Reopened as of October 19, 2007! For those of you who remember from TV coverage, Oakwood Shopping center was raped, gutted, and set on fire during the Katrina episode. Millions of dollars and two years later, it has finally reopened its doors to eager shoppers. The rennovation is beautiful and sleek. The minimalist look suits well as the shoppers and storefronts truly outfit the shopping experience. In the center of the mall is a large fountain with granite and available are sofa couches and benches all throughout. So far only three flagship stores are open (Sears, JCPennys, & Dillards) with the usual footwear shops and what not. What's exciting is that Forever 21 is coming in December!!! Finally, no more going to Lakeside all the freakin time! The food court had a major face-lift as well. Tons of seating and for now, clean tables! Open are Chick-fil-A, Chinese take out, pizzeria, cheesesteaks, and Daiquris! So if you feel like staying on one side of the Mississippi, you can burn cash @ Oakwood....

text: Last Thursday was my second time dining at Wildflower and it did not disappoint. We started with the Smoked Salmon appetizer. The potato's on the bottom were amazing. Almost like a hash-brown, and nice and crispy. They stood up well to the chive creme fraiche that went on top. And there was four decent portions to the appetizer. For the entree we split the Maple Braised short ribs. The meat was so tender on the short rib that words cannot describe. It simple fell apart and was absolutely delicious to consume. And the horseradish mashed potatoes were the perfect compliment. In addition we had a side of mac and cheese, because, well... I don't really need a reason, but we did. The mac and cheese was top notch, but definitely a side kick to the star of the evening which was the short rib. We had a butterscotch/caramel desert that came with a brownie as well. It was a great way to end the meal, but I am still thinking about that short rib. The service was awesome, wine was good and a decent price, food definitely above average. Will be back as soon as possible.
label: POS

text: I've yet to give a one star review; sadly today is the day. I was in the Meadowood Mall with family and my mother, who was in a wheelchair from an accident, and was craving a corndog. The food court had just opened, it was around 11 o'clock in the morning, therefore it was pretty empty. After waiting for about 10 minutes without being served, along with another potential customer, my mother wheeled back to our seats. We had already gotten our food from the other places in the court and my mother had been very patient. "This is enough," I thought and walked over to the Hot Dog on a Stick. I was going to try and use the "kill them with kindness" method. Unfortunately that doesn't go over too well with teenagers, especially ones that are a partial owner of the company. The only reason I know this is because I had waited so long (about 10-15 minutes) for her to appear I read the useless pamphlet on the counter. She took the order, put the corndog in the deep fryer and escaped to the back yet again, probably to text her boyfriend, or whatever she was doing. I will never visit again, especially knowing they will be earning additional pay from my purchase. Worst customer service ever. BOOO!

text: I read other reviews and was excited to go to the salon - it is not far from my home. I got there early - about 9:30. A stylists came in and started working on my hair. Really tiny braids in the back of my head. PAINFUL. She gets up and another stylists arrives and starts working on my... no transition, never says a word, just took over. I was not upset because the other woman was not for me - too tight. as a matter of fact I ended up taking them out the following day and rebraiding them - I had stress bumps from the pulling, The lady was slow - I was watching people come and go around me.. and the other stylists were asking her why she took so long. I asked how much longer and she blamed me for not being closer to her AND she is pregnant - like I did it! To be fair and honest, my hair looked good, The cost was average, but the customer service STUNK! if you don't care, be my guest, but I wouldn't do them twice. I was there long enough to see how they were treating other clients and counted myself lucky. One lady had to wait for her stylist to show up - 45 minutes. When she arrived, she told the client she was just going to have a quick coffee... another 15-20 minutes pass because she had her 3 year old with her and her daughter had to be fed breakfast . Insult to injury was watching what the lady did to her hair. She got a 2 strand twist - but er hair was bone straight and sticking out of the twist - no way to camaflouge at all.. well maybe a scarf would work. She sat... maybe a half hour, then they suggested that she come back tomorrow cause the stylist meant to do her hair was tired and didn't feel like doing her hair anymore.... AAGHHH!! She went off, can't blame her. it is winter and her hair is wet cause they washed it to keep her in the salon. and now she can't get her hair done...

text: This place is pretty terrible. Cool concept, but it just doesn't pull it off. Maybe if I had ordered the peanut chicken satay pizza instead it would be better. I ordered the red curry pizza, which had pineapple, bamboo, chicken, chili paste, and more mozzarella than you would ever want on a pizza. Granted I'm biased when it comes to pizza (more of a minimal-cheese New Havenite than a New Yorker) but still... the crust was decent, toppings were interesting, but the cheese just completely overwhelmed the whole thing. Some bites tasted like cheese pizza, some bites tasted like Thai food, but the two never really met in the middle for something that could have been amazing. My friend had the pad thai with that whole "stir crazy" menu, which is a pretty great concept. Tasted like soy sauce and not much else, although it included scallions, peanuts, eggs, and chicken. Needed more flavor. Iced tea was fine, as thai iced tea often is. Seems like it would be great drunk food though. Incredibly cheap. A bit hard to find by car but drunken stumbling could lead you there.

text: If you're a fan of real sushi then do yourself a favor, drive 5 minutes to Samuari Blue and skip this place! Rice was soggy, tuna not fresh and the spicy tuna hand roll had no spice. Perhaps the hibachi is better but if you're going for sushi you can get the same quality at your loacl Publix :(

Without tasting any of the other dishes I can only give them 4 stars for now but definitely, you must get the oysters when you dine there.

text: There are a few categories this review could fit under, restaurants, religious activities and local flavor. Why? The Wat Mangkolratanaram Buddhist Temple off Palm River Road is an inviting compound right on the river. There is a temple and another building where they cook Thai food on Sundays to raise money for the temple. It is such a relaxing place and the food was great and cheap. The ingredients are donated, and they are cooked by the women and men that belong to the temple. The dishes are $3 to $5. There are a variety of meals (pad Thai, curry, fish, chicken) and other items (coconut rice cakes, fried bananas, sweet potatoes and taro root, Thai desserts and tea). This place is definitely worth the trip and it was great to experience some of the culture.
label: POS

text: Came here for a second dinner last Friday night around 9:30 with my boyfriend, who hadn't eaten yet. The place was pretty crowded with warm, cozy and hip decor. Yeah, yeah, the beer selection is "great." To be honest I don't know much about beer and the strong stuff usually gives me a stomachache, but I had a Sierra Nevada Celebration and it was good. I had the arugula and feta salad which was simple and so delicious ($7). Arugula tossed with orange olive oil, dill, shallots, and the freshest feta I have EVER tasted (and I gorged on the stuff in Israel). Huge, creamy chunks of cheese were tossed throughout. My boyfriend had the Ragu Bolognese open-faced sandwich ($12) which he enjoyed, but was so heavy he didn't finish. The fries were thin, crispy and served with Harissa aoli, a flavor I've never tried. Very interesting.
label: POS

text: Man did I get lucky. Went to Cure after the Saints destroyed the Patriots in MNF. A perfect end to a perfect day. The owner, Neal, was there along with the most bitchin', knowledgeable bartender I have ever met. If you like Jaeger Bombs, Fetzer wine, or Abita beer then this is not your bar. But, if you like to explore what alcohol is really about this is your mecca. They have drinks containing ingredients distilled from monks. It's almost like a laboratory. They can tell you the history of their cocktails, make you anything that has ever been made (or almost) and have the most amazing collection of liquors, mixers, and liqueurs. Oh and I did I mention the food is amazing too. Served in small tapas style portions. I had the Pretty Ricky sandwich which was amazing. My friend had the cured meat plate which was also fantastic. Other dishes that we tried that all were great were the duck liver crostini and some short ribs. Decor is very warm and modern. A nice addition to New Orleans, which has its many dive bars and traditionally southern decorated bars and restaurants. If you like to eat and drink... You MUST go here. They have music playing via an iPod speaker system, but only enhanced the mood.
label: POS

text: As you've probably heard from your friends, from your landlord, to any random-o on the street, Chipotle's food is really good and really fresh. The guacamole might have been my favorite, even though I visited about a half hour before closing. Still tasted like it had just been smashed a few minutes before, although it does weird me out that there are no tomatoes in it simply because I could not live in a world without tomatoes on every dish that I eat. I'm writing this review solely for the awesome service I got on my first, and recent, visit. I went on a Monday night as previously said, right before closing. I wasn't sure if they were even open, but the guy at the front literally waved me in and asked if he could help me out. Since the restaurant was totally empty, I admitted I'd never been there as I was still currently addicted to Qdoba. But I'd had a less than satisfactory burrito that night, threw it out and went across the street to Chipotle. The three people on staff that night were all so ridiculously friendly, helping me with my menu choices, explaining the whole Chipotle ideal shpeal, recommending the guac, etc. At the end, the cashier ringing me up told me that my total was zero dollars. Say whaaat? Then the lady who had helped me with the guac, and had rolled up my food explained that she was actually the manager there and that since she knew their food could stand on its own, she knew I'd be coming back all the time. I don't remember the details, I was just stunned by her paying for my meal for really no reason! Even without that, they were all just so nice, and the food was so good, I haven't been back to my semi-weekly Qdoba since.

text: I will start by saying that my experience at Chappy's was almost 2 years ago. I have not been back since... even with a free $100 gift certificate from Chappy. We went here looking for a good cajun meal. What we got was shocking on several levels. I have never been treated so poorly by a restaurant manager in my life. I don't send food back and I don't often complain at a restaurant about the food I'm served. Like many of you, I've done my time working in kitchens and at restaurants in high school/college. So my family went to celebrate two family birthdays for me and also my Grandmother. I think it was a Monday or Tuesday night and the place was pretty empty. We ordered a few different appetizers. They were average. I want to say I ordered the Veal Bayou Caddy for my meal. It got to the table and for starters looked absolutely terrible. I tasted it and it just wasn't good at all. There was some watery, eggplant mush in the middle. The waiter came by and asked how we were doing and right behind him was the night manager. I told them that my dish was not what I expected and that it seemed like it was cooked wrong. The manager immediately left the table and came back with a small side dish of the eggplant/shrimp concoction and sat it down in front of me and said something to the effect of, "see there's nothing wrong with it... it's always like this." He then told me that I was wrong and that people love this dish. He left the table and everyone including the waiter kind of sat there stunned for a minute. Usually when someone complains I envision first an apology and then an attempt to correct the problem. I never in a million years thought I would get an argument and a display prop by a rude manager. The waiter then tried to pick up the pieces by asking if I wanted something else to eat from the menu. I told him no, I had lost my appetite. I was done at that point. The waiter was very apologetic and told us that they had had some issues with the guy in the past. Apparently Chappy was not there that evening, nor anyone of any real authority. The waiter brought the bill later and said that he tried to take my meal off the bill, but that the manager REFUSED to remove it. Yes... refused to take it off the bill. It isn't like I ate half of it and decided against it. it was almost immediately after getting it that there was an issue. Then the circus that ensued. We all left in disgust. My mom decided to call in the next day in hopes of talking to Chappy. She got him on the phone and retold the story. I'm told he was VERY apologetic and wanted to do anything to make it right. He even mailed my mom a gift card for $100 that I have still not used. I may suck it up and give them another chance. If that experience is good, I will write another fair review. Until then, they get a 1 star because they won't let me vote with negative numbers.
label: NEG

text: I visited the Gaylord Opryland hotel/resort/conglomerate a few weeks ago when I was visiting Nashville with my boyfriend. We stopped by to see the hotel, but didn't stay there as guests. This place wasn't really near any downtown things, but we rented a car so it was no big deal to get there. (If you're flying in for a weekend, I really recommend renting a car- I have no idea how we would have gotten around otherwise.) Parking was outrageously expensive so we parked in some shopping center across the street and walked in. It was maybe a 10 minute walk, but you're mostly walking through nicely manicured Opryland foliage so it's a nice walk. The hotel was a sight to behold- HUGE glass ceilings, indoor river, many, many restaurants inside which had an "outdoor" feel because of the massive atrium. We took a boat ride given by "Delta River Boat Tours" which was a cute little boat on a track in their indoor river with a sweet southern tour guide letting us in on all the "fascinating" facts about the hotel. She told everything as if it was the most amazing fact that had ever left her lips: "Here we have the original interior wall of the hotel... it was built in NINETEEN SEVENTY SEVEN!" (So old!) or, our favorite, "Here in the hotel we have an INDOOR SWIMMING POOL, so that you can swim ALL YEAR ROUND" (You mean, INSIDE the building? Impossible!) Anyway, it was hilarious. Seems like a nice place just to see/have a drink/ maybe dinner if prices aren't insane. Extra star for our tour guide who we still laugh about.

text: Regarding the bag check policy at this store, I have been asked to check my empty re-usable grocery bag. When the security guy insisted on taking it, I pointed out that they sell re-usable grocery bags by the checkouts. The other comments here are very fair. I know people like to complain about produce sections, but this one is actually very bad. I believe that half the income of the store comes from selling sandwiches. You can easily stand in line for half an hour to buy one of their sandwiches at the deli. text: The bubbles were the only good part of this place- my friend and I both got a glass (I had Chandon blanc de noir, she had a George Something-or-other blanc de blanc), they were both nice and bubbly still, so at least we weren't let down by flat sparkling wine. That's what the 1 star is for. What we WERE let down by, however, was the sushi. This was, no question, the worst sushi I have ever eaten. Perhaps it was our mistake to limit our food choices to the sushi side of the menu-- but the rest of the menu is so disorganized and confusing I didn't feel like bothering with it. Maybe previous reviewers who liked the sushi here have never actually eaten good sushi? That's the only explanation I could come up with for anyone describing the sushi from Swanky Bubbles as good. Before the sushi arrived, a server came over and poured out large dishes of soy sauce. I thought this was really weird. First of all, leave the soy sauce on our table, please! Second of all, not everyone likes a giant lake of soy sauce-- I for one like to mix in an ample pinch of wasabi to make almost a paste... and having a full dish of soy sauce made this impossible. So that was odd. We ordered 4 rolls: Vegetable Timebomb, Unagi Roll, 247 Roll, and the My Thai. Only one of these, the unagi roll, was anything near tasty. The rest of them were miserable: the rice was completely wrong. So wrong that we could tell as soon as the plate of sushi was brought out-- flat and dense and squished and flattened around the nori and fish. That was the first mistake. We started trying the various rolls, hoping that maybe they just looked funny but tasted fine... but sadly that was not at all the case. The fish was not good. It was not fresh, it was not flavorful, it did not taste like it was supposed to- the tuna was overwhelmingly fishy and stringy. The salmon was meh- also not very fresh and bland. The My Thai roll- which was supposed to contain spicy sauce, cucumber, poached asparagus, tuna and fresh thai basil, was the most disappointing to me- there was no basil flavor, there was no spicy sauce as far as I could tell, and if it contained asparagus it tasted like wood. Or nothing at all, in fact. The vegetable timebomb seemed to have lots of vegetables, as promised... but lots of wasabi? No. Also a boring, flavorless roll and also surrounded by way too much gross rice. The 247 roll was a waste, too- same problems of overly dense rice and unfresh fish. Nasty. The only good thing, I guess, is that I didn't get ill from eating here (it's noon the day after) so I guess I'm better off than some. We asked our server about the sushi- her explanation was that they have a "different style" of making sushi. Ummm... like making it totally nasty and gross? I don't think I like that style, and I don't think that excuses the plate of stuff we were served: It. Was. Not. Good. From now on, I'm sticking to Koi (N. 2nd Street between Green and Fairmount) for my sushi fix. We considered ordering something else after we took the first couple bites of sushi... but then decided we didn't want to give them any more money. Glad that we ordered the bubbly- it was the only redeeming feature. Also glad that Franklin Fountain is right around the corner... Another point: not sure who thinks this place is wheelchair accessible. There are several steps to get in, plus the back part of the dining room is up one more step. That, and the restrooms are located down 10 or so rather steep stairs. So, it's accessible only if you eat outside (there are a few tables on the sidewalk), and don't need to use the restroom. I strongly urge against eating here if you at all enjoy sushi.
label: NEG

People generally prefer to keep their sex life private than air it out to the public, along with business like onDemand, Netflix and online downloading, video rentals are slowly becoming extinct. text: I am no expert on this whole steak and hoagie thing, but I did like what I ordered. It was called the PMC and was a steak sandwich with peppers, mushrooms, onions and marinara on a soft roll. My sandwich was very generous, I could only eat half. My lunch companion got a hot pastrami, ate the whole thing, and promptly had food coma for most of the afternoon. He seemed to really like it, though. What I liked about McMaster's was the simplicity of the food. Maybe that makes it more authentic? You tell me. Anyway, there was nothing done to froo-froo up the food. No avocadoes, no chipotle mayo, just solid and simple blue collar stuff. The french fries were hot and fresh, and were very similar to the kind of fries from In and Out, except bigger, if that gives you an idea of what to expect. I thought they were delicious and I'm normally loyal to the Belgian double-cook method of making fries. Service was really really good. The guy behind the counter was extremely friendly, gave honest recommendations, even admitted to eating the fries with mayo - viewed with absolute horror in the US usually - and that's how I took my fries too. Thanks, brother. He also happily pointed out the drinks were refillable and asked several times if he could top us up. One thing to keep in mind is that IV is a dead zone right now, thanks to spring break, so service might not be so hot when the hoardes of students are back. The remaining half of the sandwich became my lunch the following day and it was still good. Bonus. ps. lots of room to sit outside.

text: Since I live nearby, I've been a frequent shopper at this Whole Foods for the sake of convenience. I've shopped here at least once a week for the past three years. There are some serious quality issues at this location. Milk goes rancid days before the "sell by" date. Packaged cheese grows mold before its expiration date, even when properly sealed after being opened. Many times I've come home and opened my carton of strawberries to find them covered in mold. Cucumbers are soft and gooey in the middle. Packaged spinach wilts and starts to smell before the "use by" date. Like the reviewer below, in the summer I've seen flies swarming around the deli and landing on the cold cuts. The one time I purchased and cooked mussels from this store, I got diarrhea. I've shopped at the South Street and Plymouth Meeting Whole Foods stores, and I'm a frequent customer at Trader Joe's. I've never had any quality issues with food purchased at any of these stores. This suggests to me that it's not my refrigerator that's the problem; rather, there is a serious problem with handling and refrigeration of perishable food items at the Art Museum store. It's really quite outrageous, because if I'm going to be gouged by ridiculous prices, the product had better be fresh. It appears that the policy with produce is to keep it on the floor until it sells, regardless of whether it's still fresh or not. It's great that edible produce is not going to waste, but if the store is going to do this, there should be a discount for produce that is past its prime. Why would I want to pay $3 for a bag of spinach that smells like a garbage can? Customer service is hit or miss. It's obvious that the cashiers have been instructed to engage the customers in conversation while ringing them up. ("How was your day? Any plans for the evening? What are you doing this weekend?")
