text: If you go to New Orleans to hang out in a bar with absolutely no local flavor so you can listen to a white guy karaoke crappy pop songs between sets of lousy bands, then this place is for you. A dirty, loud, college frat house type bar. It even has those annoying shot girls who try to make you spend money on watered down vodka and fruit juice shots. You are MUCH better off walking up Bourbon St. to Lafitte's Blacksmith Shop or head over to the Maple Leaf in the Carrollton neighborhood of Uptown to listen to great bands. Maybe try any place on Frenchmen Street. Seriously - do anything but go to this sorry excuse for a place.

text: OMG! I'm in Honey Heaven! Cute little restaurant --- very laid back atmosphere. Staff here is awesome --- on top of their game, very efficient and friendly. Wait wasn't too bad --- we opted for whatever was opened first --- we sat at the counter. Hubby ordered the french toast with a side of eggs and scrapple with a cup of black coffee. French toast was super hot and fluffy --- coffee was brewed to perfection --- rich and dark! This was my first time trying scrapple --- good god it was so good! I'm a spam girl --- and scrapple totally blew spam outta the water! I had the Big Boy (I think that's what it was called) --- which was one big pancake stuffed with scrambled egg and your choice of meat (I picked their homemade sausage). Our waitress was a sweetheart and suggested I have cheese with it. It sounded kinda odd ---- but oh god, it was sooo good! I tired their potato latke for the first time --- it was okay --- a bit hard for my taste --- but still very good! I also had their fresh squeezed OJ --- oh so good! I will so come back!

text: pretty yum. burgers are good. shakes are awesomely yum. and service really isnt that bad. I feel awkward paying restaurant prices for diner food but i guess its just santa barbara. Still yum

text: My first experience here was for a co-workers shower. The food was excellent! My second and more memorable experience was to celebrate a co-workers pending nuptuals. We opted for the family style dining. Holy food - so much! It was all delicious (the gnocchi was to die for!). I will definitely be bringing my family here.

text: The ingredients are fresh and the menu is certainly creative. However, in all honesty, I found everything I ordered to be bland. There was seasoning, it's just that the food reminded me of Chinese places that dumb down their food for American tastes. Are alligator balls with chili aioli supposed to only have a hint of seasoning and spice? Is the Louisiana cochon with turnips, cabbage & cracklins supposed to taste like shredded pork with sweet sauce, with the cracklins tasting like something you get out of a bag? The decor is gorgeous, with natural poplar, and their service is the some of the best you'll see. Again their food is pretty fresh. It's just not cooked to its full potential. Their other restaurant however, Cochon Butcher, is absolutely off the hook.

text: I was super excited to find out that Sushi Land had baked rolls (Lion King Roll, Bay Scallop Roll), so I decided to order both. The reviews warning about the small portions were no joke! text: I read the reviews and went down on a Sunday around lunch time a few weeks ago and the place was packed! We waited in line for about 45 mins, figured that it must be pretty damn good, judging by the wait. I ordered the pulled pork and split a slab of ribs with my friend. Here's my advice, order the ribs and don't bother with anything else. The ribs were really good, but far from the best I've ever had. The pulled pork was pretty much inedible. My buddy also got the brisket, which was almost as bad as the pork. The fact that this is ostensibly the best BBQ in St. Louis speaks volumes about the state of BBQ in St. Louis. To me BBQ should be all about the pork, and if you're pulled pork is not good, then you don't have much of a leg to stand on.

text: Guy Fieri - today is the second time you've disappointed me. Boise - I do not know why I keep expecting more out of you... =/ Came here for dinner with a couple coworkers - one had been interested because of Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives - Kodiak Grill got a spot and Fieri tried the Kodiak Burger - a burger topped with a kielbasa. All three of us got one - but we started off with prime rib bites and wings. The wings weren't memorable at all... the menu claimed that it was a 1 lb plate of wings - but I barely counted 8 wings/drumsticks. The prime rib bites were small and had tons of fat left on them =/ They were served in au jus and served with bread - didn't think they were all that great. The Kodiac Big Bear burger - after I saw Fieri on YouTube - pretty much looked like it did on the show - A MESS. I thought it was strange how they didn't even attempt to make that place look good... that's pretty much true in reality. There was way too much on that burger, but the strangest part was that there wasn't much flavor in it at all. Why did they insist on saying "NO SAUCE" on the menu? Odd... and kinda sad. I tried to bolster the flavor with hot sauce and ranch... the only thing that came out of it was me sweating a bunch 'cause the waittress got us a bottle of "Ass Blaster" hot sauce. That was probably the most fun I had all night... =/ The place is pretty remote - you've gotta drive up a windy mountain road for about a quarter hour past the free way. My coworkers enjoyed the "view," but all I saw was a bunch of dead grass punctuated by a shrub here or there. Sorry, Boise. You've once again succeeded in failing expectations...

Kid got nachos with beef not bad but not amazing but on the salty side. Overall I am sure we exceeded our sodium content for the week. Very salty food. The staff seemed pleasant and the facilities were very clean!

text: My daughter actually sees a specialist for her eyes, but we decided to try America's Best for getting her glasses. Once they came in we took them to her eye doc so he could see if the prescription was right. He was surprised. Her prescription was exactly right! He was impressed! And we were incredibly happy! We had been paying $300 for glasses for her and she would outgrow them in a year. We paid $90 and got two pairs AND they are scratch resistant! I get my glasses and eye exams there now too! I highly recommend them to anyone!

text: Why do I always get off the train feeling like I've been punched in the face? SEPTA's got us all in a corner, because there simply is no other option. In fact, a lot of the time, there is NO option (i.e. Going from South Philly to Northern Liberties? You'll need at least 2 buses). SEPTA may be the reason I am an alleged "militant walker." I prefer walking the 2.5 miles to and from work every day to giving SEPTA $2.90 and STILL having to walk 10 blocks. Just last week I was taking the R6 from Norristown to Suburban and was transporting my bike with me. As circumstances had it, I had an appointment in which I had to wear a business suit (high heels and all!), and the SEPTA workers unapologetically informed me that they are not allowed to touch my bike, not even to help me lift it up the three steps on the train. "Uh-uh, I can't touch your bike. Not allowed. I don't touch no one's bike." ...whatever that was about. On top of that, the Norristown train station ticket office closes at 1pm. COME ON! So when I accidentally asked the girl at the Information Counter if I could buy a 1-way Zone 3, she just said, "No." How's that for customer service? "Um, why?" I asked. "I don't sell tickets." "I'm sorry, where's the ticket counter." "Closed at 1." (No eye contact made on her part). So that brings me to tickets/MONEY. Why is it that SEPTA has no money, when every G.D. bus is a mobile advertisement for high rolling companies (T.H.P, CCP, The Phillies... you know they paid up to cover those buses in ads). But, no, SEPTA is so broke, that they went and changed the Regional Rail ticket buying policies so that it's extra on the train, even if there is no ticket office at the station. And then they changed their ticket hours to close at 1. Brilliant! Oh, one last thing, thanks for all the strikes, SEPTA workers. It's really a great annual tradition. I move for a SEPTA commuters strike.
label: NEG

text: The Airport Marriott is on the grounds of Philadelphia International Airport (PHL) and is literally connected to the airport by an enclosed walkway that ties into Terminal B/C which is USAir flights (PHL is a USAir Hub). The hotel is pretty standard of a Marriott. The rooms are decently sized, clean and well kept. It is a good choice if you want to stay close to the airport with no hassles. On the hotel alone I'd give it 3 stars, nothing great and nothing bad. However the price is going to cost it a star. The standard rate is often double or more than what you can get a comparable or better room for nearby at one of the hotels on Bartram or Island Aves. If you've got plenty of Marriott Rewards Points or a Free Night Certificate there's no reason not to stay here. If you are paying for it, save the money and go somewhere else.

text: I get that the Merriam Theater might have some historical draw, but I wasn't impressed by my recent visit. The artwork on the ceiling and walls looks like it's in dire need of some cleanup and/or restoration. They try to accommodate the snackers by placing a ridiculously over-priced cash bar on each level, but once you get higher than the ground floor, you won't get any ice in your drinks and the line of people waiting to purchase bottlenecks with those trying to find their seats. We showed our tickets to an usher who brought us to seats that we were pretty excited to have - front balcony, no obstructions. Then another usher came over, asked to see our tickets, and gave US attitude about being in the wrong seats. Turns out we were another floor up, so far back that we could have worked the spotlight. There was hardly any leg room (good thing I'm short) and about halfway through the show, the guy in front of me decided to place his glasses on top of his head. I spent the following hour dodging my head back and forth, avoiding feeling like I was watching the show through a fun house mirror. Good thing the Vince Vaughn & Kevin James Comedy Roadshow was hilarious in its own right, because the theater didn't do it any favors!
label: NEG

text: If you've ever walked down 3rd Street (towards Arch) then you've smelled the amazing aromas coming out of this spa...they're enough to make even a jaded city dweller stop in their tracks and breathe deep. Now just imagine how great it is to step inside and get treated to a massage, facial or any other treatment they offer. It's pretty darn awesome! I credit Terme Di Aroma as being the only place to give me a massage that made me fall asleep on the table - no small feat as I get lots of them but still find it really hard to relax. I highly recommend adding on the reflexology option to whatever service you're getting (your tootsies will thank you), as it just prolongs the magic. You'll love the whole experience from start to finish, from the helpful staff to the serene decor. Go ahead - you've earned it!

text: I haven't found a better corner grocery store/deli anywhere. The staff is friendly and make wonderful sandwiches. They have healthy, fresh ingredients, and most things are reasonably priced. The soups I've tried are delicious. Any produce I've bought has been ripe and ready. I love stopping by for a bowl of cold, cubed watermelon. Even regular grocery items are cheaper here than at a Rite-Aid or what have you. They do have a $5 limit to use credit/debit cards.

text: So I hate to give this company a bad review, because I had two good friends that used them and had absolutely no problems. They are also used by a lot of people looking for the big, grand vehicles at a lower price. All I have to review them on was an experience I had about a month ago. I was invited on a wedding party bus as the wife of a groomsman. First of all, the vehicle was too small for all of us. This could be all on the bride and groom's (or their parents') decisions, or it could be all on the company. I know some limo services are not up front about how big of a vehicle you REALLY need. An 18 passenger party bus does NOT fit 18 adults in formal attire in the summer (especially if you have bags, coolers, etc). Remember that anywhere you go. My main beef with A Perfect Touch is that it was a sweltering June day in St. Louis, and the AC wasn't working. Air was blowing, but it wasn't cold. You'd think this would be something that would have been checked to begin with. Everyone was just trying to deal, but when the wedding party got off the bus for pictures, I turned to the driver and told him that the AC was definitely not working. He suggested drawing the shades. Umm, yeah, that's just going to stop it from getting even hotter. He also said it should cool faster while driving, so we took a lap around the block. No dice. I think it needs cool air to begin with. Finally, I was blunt and asked if he could call the office to see if another vehicle with functioning air could meet us. His reply was that it "would take a long time". Seriously...your office is just off McDonnell and 270, we were at Keiner Plaza, and we still had an hour or so to go on pictures. It wouldn't take THAT long. He did get off the bus and make a phone call. Didn't know if he called the office or even just pretended to make a phone call to anyone just to escape my questioning. I doubt he ever called the office and didn't say anything one way or the other after the phone call. The only thing that saves this company from 1 star is that we did use them for a limo to the ceremony for the guys (we used BEST Transportation for 3 other vehicles). They are one of the only companies in the area with reasonable prices on hourly contracts. According to the guys, everything went well.
label: NEG

text: I know, I know, I say this all the time--when you rate/review something, you're making a comparison; I think "x" is amazing because I've had "y." With this in mind, once again, I'm left with a headache inducing conundrum. Do I rate the Deacon under the "dive bars with food" category, or do I rate them as a regular restaurant? I've been here a few times now, because I wanted to check on their consistency. Here's what I know: 1.) The hummus and sweet potato salsa are both excellent (and I have a firm dislike of sweet potatoes) 2.) Their salads, while not amazing, are definitely solid. Kudos to you Deac, for making your own dressings. 3.) The curly dog sandwich is definitely unique, and also delicious. The fish and chips are decent. The veggie boudin burger wasn't to my liking, but then again, I'm the guy that would order "pork" if they offered it as a side dish. However, I'm going to agree with Nowell in saying that it is refreshing to try a veggie burger that doesn't taste like every other veggie burger--the lady seemed to enjoy it. 4.) Their vegan pineapple upside down cake was toted as "so good, you won't know it's vegan." Yes, yes you can tell it's vegan. Fail. Fire your copywriter. 5.) Their jukebox is pretty amazing. Limited selection, but hey, I can't complain since they decided to kick it old school and have a flipping board showing CD cover art (they still have CDs? I kid.). It is no surprise that the last two times i've been here, I've walked in to a fairly large intoxicated woman (different times, different women) singing along to Journey. Hey, it's the Midwest--I'd be happy to be a part of your reindeer games. But seriously, they have some pretty solid jukebox listings. 6.) I love the totally incorrect latin translation for "Saint Louis" in their avatar. I find it either ironically hip, or endearingly retarded. Overall, very decent food for a very good price. This may sound unfair, but the food is too good for a bar. I can't in good faith rate it as anything less than a full blown restaurant. The place is a little more on the "divey" side than I'm used to, but hey, I'm hip. Let me just find my self-deprecating t-shirt that alludes to my 80's youth. I know it's around here somewhere. Gather round kids, because apparently it's Halloween time and I'm handing out 4 star reviews like its candy...
label: POS

text: Think zero stars or maybe a .001....just for parking. text: i am leaving for a three-week road trip in two days with four friends. i wanted to get each of us a little going-away present, and i thought cute little handmade notebooks would be the perfect thing. so i'm on a mission. i walk in to a woman standing at the counter. does she work there? can she help me? no, she is waiting to be rung up. where is the shopkeeper? i venture deeper inside and there's my answer - she's talking to some more of the help in the back. i browse. the customer waits. eventually she makes her way to the back of the store to get some help. you'd think they'd apologize profusely and rush up to the register. nope, they go on with their conversation. if this place didn't have such cute shit i'd rate them one star in a heartbeat. no one greeted me, asked me if i needed help. which i did. i was lost in a seemingly endless world of address books (in the age of cell phones does anyone use those things anymore?) when i was just looking for cute $10 notebooks for my friends to write in on our trip. alas, i looked at my watch and the meter on my parking spot was up so i left. no goodbye on my way out, they were too busy squealing over their just-arrived friends' new bleach job. a little customer service goes a LONG way with me. i will find another stationery store tomorrow.

text: We went here for my girlfriend's dad's birthday last night and it was actually delicious. I got the goat cheese and beet starter and the grilled leg of lamb for an entree. Both were well-sized portions--I am new to St. Louis and still am pleased by the serving sizes here--and both were very tasty. The lamb was perfectly cooked and tender and was served with a really tasty reduction. My girlfriend got the special (salmon with mushroom risotto) which was also good. My girlfriend's mom got the mussels to start and they were also very good. All and all a very pleasurable experience and I will go back. We shared the flourless chocolate cake--very rich, but enjoyable--I want to try the bread pudding, it sounds sooooo good, we were just too stuffed to order another dessert. AND, I love that they offer seasonal and, when available, local ingredients. In addition, I read on their menu that they are the FIRST restaurant in STL to switch to all wind power---hmmm, pretty cool! Not only a delicious restaurant, but a responsible one too!! I'll be back!
label: POS

text: Dadeo's is a great place for Cajun-style cuisine. Their Po-Boys are generously filled and always leave me stuffed. I always substitute their potatoes for sweet potato fries and trust me, it's worth the extra dollar. This comes with a chipolte-mayonnaise mixture and I always find myself overloading on the dip on my fries. I like the old style diner feel of the restaurant. They have a miniature jukebox on some of the tables, which adds a nice touch. There has sometimes been a wait, but it has never been too long, and it is worth the wait. Prices are reasonable at this location too. Their Po'Boys are around $11, and you can get them for half price on Monday and Tuesdays. They are also open quite late (11pm on most days) which makes it very convenient for a late snack. Food service is also very quick here, although sometimes it feels as if they're trying to rush you out to serve other customers.
label: POS

text: I've loved going to Bridgid's over the years, as the place never has disappointed and has always been a great neighborhood bar. After a long absence, I finally had dinner there Wednesday and think my love affair is now over. I think this place, especially in the kitchen, just lost that "lovin" feelin. Literally, in every step of the experience (from drinks, to apps to entrees) we were the recipients of a screw up. It was like we were being punked! First, one waitress served the entire busy dining area, and though she tried her best, they definitely needed another server. Second, we struck out every step of the way when it came to ordering. Lastly, they need a new chef, pronto. The debacle began when I asked about the description about a beer special. The one served to me was a sour ale- not at all what was described- and I couldn't drink it. The waitress apologized, took it back and returned with a "safe bet". Minor hick-up. We ordered mussles in a white wine sauce, then asked about the dinner specials. My boyfriend ordered the Asian Bass w/ a red sauce and I had shrimp diablo. The mussles smelled great, but was inedible b/c it was way too salty. It tasted like the chef poured garlic salt into it, so we sent it back after 2 bites. I felt like i had a salt slick in my mouth the entire next day- it was that bad! When our entrees came out, turns out the waitress ordered my boyfriend the wrong item, even though he asked questions about the Asian Bass. She apologized, said she got confused (a testament to how frazzled she was). Mistakes happen; that's life. text: We loved this place. The menu is enormous and everything except the fondue but including the omelet which was referred to as a quiche (either way, it's cooked in a hot pot). We arrived ~7PM last Friday. 2 other tables were filled, but then either a couple or small family would arrive every 20 minutes. We brought in a 6-pack from Gilligan's, and were brought a tall champagne bucket to keep the beers cold. I questioned whether I should get the crispy fried egg noodle plate, but was convinced not to (just in case it wasn't right). Until I saw it at the table behind ours. Why this was an issue? I haven't had it in 20 years. Every time I ask for crispy fried egg noodles I get that awful bag of mealworm looking things. Or they make some gelatinous mess of rice or noodles because obviously I'm insane and have no idea what I'm talking about. More on these noodles later. We started with cha gio. These were crispy, not the least bit greasy. The sauce could have been stronger, although we also could have added more fish sauce to the container (each table has fish sauce, soy sauce, hoisin sauce, chile garlic sauce, salt, pepper, and sugar). There were also only 2 pieces of lettuce for the 4 medium-long rolls; we were out of lettuce by the second piece. The filling were also a bit mild. One small order of pho tai with extra beef on the side. Mild but well flavoured. We split this bowl. Unlike a previous poster, we aren't fans of a lot of noodles. And no MSG reactions. Yeah! We were stuffed at this point. Having seen the noodles at the aforementioned table, we asked to have those noodles instead of rice with the catfish. They thought we were nuts, but decided to give us noodles, rice, and the catfish. Then an extra order of gravy. The catfish was void of bones and perfectly tender and sweet in a garlic-ginger brown sauce and cooked in a hot pot. I can't remember the last time I had such amazing fish. The sauce was perfectly seasoned--not overly salty as at many places--and the fish so good. That we made a horseshoe pie with the rice, noodles, and fish was probably completely wrong of us, but it was so good. We weren't charged for our noodles and sauce. The bill came out to $27 including tax and prior to tip. Great place.

The one problem I had was the portions. The mini salad and the huge entree seemed like a pretty drastic contrast. While my dining partners decided to to take the light fare route by getting apps for both courses, they agreed. They were also a but put off by the trendiness of the space. Yes, all the beautiful people were stationed at the bar, and the bulkiness of the aluminum menus kept knocking over the glassware on the way-to-small table. text: Eating at Zoe was a comedy of errors... I work in fine dining and so has my boyfriend, so while we understand the challenges of maintaining a fine dining room and kitchen with good food and service, we also hold high expectations which were woefully unmet. We chose Zoe based on good experiences at Whiskey Blue, the downstairs bar. Looking for a cheap, spur of the moment night out, we decided to go out for the COOLinary menu (3 courses, $35 a person) and bring our own bottle of wine (a very, VERY nice French white we'd been saving for a good meal). We were debating between a few places but we called each, asking about corkage fees, and were told Zoe doesn't charge one. Sweet! Except not... my bf and I arrived and were seated awkwardly at a huge table set for eight people... after our server showed up, we asked to be moved to a smaller table (since the restaurant was practically empty). After a few moments of confusion, we all realized that when my bf called in to make the reservation, he had asked for "a reservation for eight" meaning 8 o'clock... the reservationist said OK and hung up without confirming, so they thought they had a dining party of eight coming in. First sign of a poorly run place... Then we were told there had been a mistake, there was actually a corkage fee of $25. THEN we were told by someone else that the corkage fee was "only" $20 - which is a lot when you were expecting $0!! Ok, so we move to a smaller table and order cocktails... they take 15 minutes to get to us. Did I mention there was only two other diners in the entire restaurant?? The bread came out, mini french loaves, which were still cold in the middle. Our first course, crab cakes oscar, was underwhelming. There was too much breading, not enough crab or sauce, and they were topped with some weird "tempura" asparagus which tasted suspiciously frozen. Our second course was not much better... I had the wedge salad, which was essentially an unimpressive wedge salad with one strip of bacon, thinly sliced tomatoes and blue cheese dressing (you get what you pay for?). BF had the gumbo which was surprisingly delicious, but tasted more like Popeye's red beans and rice than gumbo (I'll admit it, I love the stuff!) The main course was just so bad it was laughable... literally. Pasta with VERY bland pesto, ringed by four gritty scallops placed over four tiny slices of sundried tomato, and the scallops were topped with - get ready for it - four rings of lemon confit. It was utterly bizarre - the confit was filled with seeds and did not compliment ANYTHING ELSE on the plate. Now, I make my own pasta, and my own pesto from homegrown basil so maybe I'm a little picky, but when I go out to a restaurant and pay for a meal, I expect something better than what I can cook myself - otherwise why go out? The only good part about our meal was the wine - an excellent obscure white table wine (the name of which is escaping me at the moment) and even that came close to ruination by the awful wine service. The glasses were NOT polished and were dotted with water marks and our server... well... as he uncorked the wine, he complimented the cork (??) and said it was easy to open, which was good because he usually breaks corks. Not a good thing to tell your tables... when he was pouring, he clanged the bottle against the wine glass rims so hard I was afraid they would break. It wasn't an accident, as he did that every time he poured the wine. To be fair, we did speak with a manager afterward who waived the corkage fee and seemed genuinely grateful for some feedback on the food. And he did say that our server was relatively new and still learning. Also they will validate your valet parking (but only if you "spend $25 bucks" in the restaurant). All in all, it was awful. I'm so disappointed I spent my hard earned money there and will never return. Whiskey Blue is a fun bar, but Zoe is all flash and no substance.

text: While visiting Asheville, NC, I was searching for the best BBQ places to eat. While on my Internet hunt, I kept turning up results for Sweet Lucy's, which was in my hometown on Philadelphia. I didn't help me at the moment, but it instantly made it onto my must-try list. I made the way out to the Northeast for dinner with Jonny and Kristen with out love our barbecue ready to be satiated. Sadly, we went on Monday night, which only offers a $20 all you can eat buffet. We were able to order take out though, so the night was salvaged. Peering into the dining room, I saw that we wouldn't be missing much in the way of atmosphere. The buffet was small but seemed to include most of sides and all of the meats. I can't and don't want to eat $20 worth of food, so the take out menu was a good alternative. There are a lot of good options on the take out menu, and there are different meals to feed any number of people. For the three of us to split we ordered a pound of four different meats, a half rack of ribs, four different sides, and cornbread. We ordered and only had to wait a short time to get our food. Back at my house, we divided up all of the food onto our plates. The first thing I had was the baked beans, and it was basically love at first taste. The baked beans, like nearly everything I ate from Sweet Lucy's, had such a good flavor. The blend of spices on the sides, meat, and sauce was perfectly blended. The mashed sweet potatoes were also a delicious side dish, and I would say those two are must-trys. I was less than impressed, however, with the creamed spinach. For the meats, we got to try five different things. We had smoked kielbasa, which was good if you're a fan of the meat, but didn't lend itself well to the BBQ style. We also ordered the beef brisket, pulled pork, and pulled chicken. All of these were tasty, with the pork being my favorite. I was impressed with all of them. Still, because the same sauce and general cooking method is used with the aforementioned three, the only real difference lies in the texture of the meats. Stick with the one you like the best for your preferred Lucy's experience. The ribs were very good, but not as tender as I like. The taste and blend on the meat was awesome, but the cooking could use some work. They were still excellent. The cornbread was a perfect accompaniment, tasty and moist. At the end of the evening, we all had enough to eat at about half the cost of the buffet. I can't really see any benefits to eating in at Lucy's, but it's nice that it's BYOB. Bottom Line: I'm holding Lucy's to a very high standard. And despite that, they still pass in my book. I love barbecue and there's so many good options at Lucy's. I like this place a lot and plan to eat here again, annoying Northeast visit and all.
label: POS

I became flat out smitten with the Women's Bowtie Blouses ($245) and Knit Ruffle Tops ($175). Many of the weathered Men's denim shirts ($150) were also something that I could see my boyfriend wear but he would have flinched at the price tag. Pricey but very polished. No. I'm not talking about me. Billy Reid...silly.

Service in the courtyard is generally better than it is in the piano bar, but things get cramped and crazy in the piano bar and you can't really blame the servers for that. text: I don't know about you but when my friends and I go out to party until the bar close down we get very hungry. But you need to tell your Designated Driver to get there before all the other DD's otherwise you will need to wait for a table. The other great thing about Denny's is you can order breakfast any time of the day, even for dinner if you want! I love that! The service is fast and friendly and the prices are pretty sweet considering the amount of food they bring out to you. You end up feeling like a pig for actually consuming most of the stuff they put in front of you. But it is all just so yummy that you can't stop packing it in. If you happen to be drunk we usually tell ourselves that all this food is required to soak up all that booze we consumed. Now if you are going to Denny's for breakfast then I suggest one of the following dishes: If you are too hungry for words and love the meat then order the Lumberjack Slam. If you like omelettes then order the Ultimate Omelette. The Fabulous French Toast Platter is mighty good if you like your French Toast. The Pancakes are famous here so defiantly try those. I like the Heartland Scramble (it comes with the country-fried potatoes... so good). If you want to order lunch then the Club Sandwich and the Chicken Sandwich is really good. If you are actually going there for dinner I can't help you out! I usually order breakfast for dinner when I got to Denny's just so I can feel like a rebel!

text: I am stunned and amazed that US Airways is still in operation. It has been a couple of years since I have flown them and I suppose I have become spoiled by airliners who have it together. Oh where to begin... - Both flights were overbooked and seats were assigned to more than one person. - They didn't check our IDs when we checked our bags, only days after someone tried to blow up a plane in Detroit. - They charged astronomical fees for checked bags (and even MORE to check curb-side!). As a result there was never enough overhead space which meant we needed to check our carry on baggage. text: Being gluten intolerant for over 20 years I have learned to search for a menu online and/or call ahead and/or contact corporate with any questions about gluten free menu items. In this case I contacted corporate and was assured there were gluten free menu items. Great! So off we go to TGIF. We are seated promptly and I ask for a gluten free menu to which I am met with confusion. The waitress quickly gets the manager who proceeds to tell me they do not have any menu items that are specifically GF, but "depending of the severity of (my) reaction to gluten there are some items to choose from." This guy had no idea what he was talking about and apparently neither did corporate who did not respond to my email describing what happened. Gluten intolerance is not a matter of degree. You have it or you don't, and if you do even a small amount of gluten can severely damage the intestinal tract and lay you up for days. Estimates are that 10% of the population have celiac disease. TGIF needs to understand this and not lead potential customers to believe they have something they do not. Needless to say we did not stay, and I would not recommend TGIF to anyone who is gluten intolerant or suspects they may be.

text: Stay Away!! Price Is Too Good To Be True!! The price seemed too good to be true, I should have trusted my gut. When I get to the counter at the off-site location a mile from the airport not indicated when I reserved, the guy seemed nice enough. He went through the company insurance options--seemed like the usual schtick that I always decline. He insisted that I needed it because my insurance company wouldn't cover everything, specifically the rental cost while the car was being repaired if I was in an accident. He insisted that because Florida was a no fault state I need their insurance (I lived in Florida for 6 years...I know the deal.) We went back and forth and finally he gave in that I didn't want the insurance and then says, "So I'll charge your credit card $200 since you declined the insurance." To which I replied, "But I'll get it back, right?" His answer, "Well, only if you fulfill all the terms and conditions of the contract and the car is in the condition you received it in." text: First off, the other review of this restaurant should be disregarded. The guy admits that he's never been there and that he never will. Why would he post a review? Anyway, my wife an I had the pleasure of spending our evening here last night. From the street, you wouldn't expect much; it looks like just another run-of-the-mill bar and grill. But we were looking for some live music and this place had no cover charge so we gave it a shot. The band was good, playing mostly classic rock/blues catering to their mostly older crowd (35+). The walls were covered in pictures of customer's dogs; this seems to be R.T.'s "thing". We're not dog people, but it was fun to see the enthusiasm that some of the previous patrons have for their pets. The relatively small establishment is split in two by a 3/4 glass wall separating the dining and bar areas. The wall is really just for a visual separation and not meant to keep smoke and music exclusive to the bar, and there was plenty of both. It was smoky and loud, but not in a bad way. The drink prices were on par, if not a little cheaper, than other bars on Main Street. They have a HUGE selection of bottles and draft, and they offer buckets at a discount (something that fewer bars are doing nowadays). The patrons, as I mentioned earlier, were a middle-adult crowd, maybe 35-55ish. This place in no way caters to the tween clubbers looking to dance to boom-boom music till 3am, there's plenty of those bars across the street. The service was great. Our waitress, who was the floor manager, was impeccable. She was fast, nice, and seemed to genuinely care if we satisfied or not. We did not sit at the bar but it seemed as though the bartenders have a pretty good repose with the regulars; it's one of those kind of bars if you know what I mean. But the highlight of the evening was the food. We had no intentions of ordering food, as we had eaten dinner down the street just a couple of hours earlier, but watching the food that was coming out of the kitchen was too hard to resist. We ordered a pizza called "The Kitchen Sink". If you like St. Louis style pizza you cannot miss this marvelous thin crust delight. We only live a couple of miles from Main Street so RT Weiler's just replaced Imos' and Stefania's as our "family pizza night" choice. If I had to find something wrong with RT Weiler's it would be that this; 1. If you're with a large crowd and in the mood for dancing, the floor is too small to accommodate more than a couple of people in front of the stage. There were 5-6 women dancing and I doubt you could fit more than 1-2 more. And 2: On a busy night, I would be reluctant to bring my children here. The whole place is very smoky and the live music on Fri and Sat is far too loud. But I don't think the smaller weekday crowd would be more family-friendly. With that said, I highly recommend RT Weiler's and cannot wait to go back.

text: (Visited 3/27/2010) Found this place via Yelp while we were wandering around the Garden District...thank you Yelpers! After reading the Yelp reviews and plugging the address into my GPS my girlfriend and I were rewarded with one of best dining experiences of this trip. (They also use OpenTable.com for reservations). I've been going to New Orleans every March for years but have never heard of Coquette. Arriving just after noon, we were able to nab a perfect outdoor table on the side of the building under a tree and umbrella. The weather was perfect. Having hit the local food and beverages hard the two days before, we decided we'd try to go a little light on the calorie intact. After walking for nearly 4 miles, we decided to have a glass each of a Spanish Cava sparkling wine which was perfect for the weather and the mood. Just in passing, we mentioned to our server (who was outstanding - more below) we were going to "split" and order of a roasted oysters appetizer and an order of fish and chips. The oysters were served excellently - hot, juicy with a wild onion topping. Our server took the extra step to have the app ACTUALLY split in half with 3 oysters per plate resting attractively on course rock salt! As an oyster lover (and glutton while in NO), I couldn't stop talking about these oysters all week. Next came the fish and chips, again thoughtfully separated for us on individual plates. The fish was delish. Period. Light and fluffy with a tasty breading. The great little twist on this dish was that it was served over a drizzle of Louisiana Hot Sauce reduced with sugar. A little spicy, a little sweet but very tasty. I could have eaten this meal my entire time there. Back to the service which was definitely top notched. Besides being very impressed with our own waiter, who seemed to know every detail about every menu item, we noticed the staff across the board was invested in their customers. It was refreshing to see such cheerful teamwork. We were enjoying ourselves so much that, while we skipped dessert (calories...); I had to have the sazerac advertised on their menu. I recommend you do as well. They also have a very extensive wine selection which unfortunately, other than the Cava, we didn't get to explore. Our bill came to about $50 which is something of an inside joke to us. For some reason, almost every meal we had in New Orleans came to about $50...this one was the best spent $50 of them all, though. Make this a must stop if you are in the Garden District and let this place nudge you to escape Bourbon for awhile if you are not!

If anything, I think the wine selection has improved over the years. The wine specials (a red and a white) are always good, yet very affordable. The Delachaise also has a great selection of liquor and beer. The Delachaise was the first bar to bring the "gastropub" concept to New Orleans (without ever calling it that). The menu has changed a great deal over the years, but it has always featured high quality food. My favorites on the current menu are the Flank Steak Bruschetta (watch out, the pesto is loaded with garlic, but the steak is delicious), the Grilled Cheese Annabella, and those famous fries (fried in goose fat!). If you are looking to hang out, drink a nice glass of wine (or two or three), and have a bite to eat, then The Delachaise is where you want to be.

We went late-ish on a Tuesday and expected it to be empty, but it was full, and we had to wait a few minutes even though we had a reservation. It wasn't a big deal, but they were so nice about it that by the time we sat down we were in a great mood. We ordered the tasting menu, and that was a huge pleasure. They just kept coming by with these fabulous plates of food, and we didn't know what we were going to get. Sort of like combining a personal chef with a guardian angel. Everything was fantastic and there were some real surprises. If you asked me how the service was at about course 2, I would have said just fine. Very nice. The staff was working really hard. But as the other tables finished their dinners and the restaurant emptied out, the staff got more and more relaxed, and the service took on a very warm, personal quality that was unusual. They were clearly having a good time, and it was contagious. The kitchen is open and visible, so even the cooking seemed personal. I am being intentionally vague. I don't want to tell you what we ate, because the chef changes the tasting menu from night to night, and for all we know it could be from moment to moment. I don't even want to tell you specifics about the service, because we left with the feeling that we had gotten extra-special treatment. If we did, then I don't want you to be disappointed if you don't get it, because just the wonderful food and nice service is enough to be happy about. If they really treat everybody this well, then I'll let you be surprised like we were. To sum up: this is a great place for people who love good food, and who prefer neighborhood service and prices to the more snobby alternatives downtown.

text: So it's hard for a man to find a good barber these days. Either you go to a fancy Salon, which tends to cater to women or the trendy 20something set, or you go to an old school barber, most of which are now 70+ years old and have one tool of the trade, a razor with a #2 guard. Not so David Wilson! In a brisk thirty minutes one of his talented (and very pretty) skilled staff members will give you a perfect cut, clean up and stray hairs with a straight razor shave, give you a neck massage, and have you on your way. Trusty me we won't skip over any of this process, which is probably one of the best things you can treat yourself to that's legal in Jersey, but a bit of history on the shop. The shop used to be exclusively men's clothing. Nothing cheapy here. Allen Edmund shoes, high end shirts and pants, the newest styles, everything a gent needs down to the right socks. On site tailoring is available, as is a shoe shine. The shoe shine also allows for drop off, which is nice if you're in hurry. David Wilson realized there was no place a gent could go to and get a great shave and haircut anymore, so he expanded and added the Salon. Probably the best offering here is a real shave. You heard me mention it earlier in regard to the haircut. This is the whole works. Hot towel, heated lather, straight razor. What a treat in today's fast paced, metro-sexual world to kick back and have an old school straight razor shave. Baby smooth skin guaranteed. Jennifer, the woman who takes care of me, shaves so close I swear she takes off the wrinkles too. Not that I have any wrinkles, but if I did... Anyway, back to the haircut. Large comfy chairs and spacious surrounds are illuminated by the huge front windows, allowing for meticulous inspection of your quality cut in progress. Once you give it the thumbs up, a hot towel is applied to your neck and any stray hairs are removed with a hot lather/straight razor combo. To finish up your haircut, a neck massage is administered to get rid of any remaining stress that hasn't been hot toweled away. Don't think this is just your granddad stopping in here either. Today's men yearn for old school quality and service like this, so you may be sitting next to your paperboy on one side and a waiter from Nunzio's on the other. Add the fact that the whole cut is $20! Best deal ever.

text: I've been in Tucson for about four years now and have experienced the ups and the downs of cuisine in this town. I once had to send back a roll because it was completely inedible, tasting as if it had been sitting out for many hours. My vegetable ramens of the past have always been rather gamey with scrappy vegetables. There is always a problem with freshness. This again was in the dine-in section, so I speak for only this part of the establishment. Yoshimatsu could be one of my favorite places in Tucson if quality control was better in the kitchen. There are wild fluctuations in the preparation style here -- your vegetable yakisoba may be the bizarro counterpart to the real stuff and the end result is often confusing and bland. I'm not saying here that Yoshimastsu should try to emulate authentic Japanese dishes, but if you're going to "innovate" do it well. Yoshimatsu does so many things right -- the ambiance is amazing, the music is always at good levels, the staff is generally amicable, the gift store is super cool, and of course karaoke on Fridays -- if only the food were better.

text: I went with a friend a few days before Halloween with the goal of going apple picking. Since I went when it opened, it was not that crowded, but as the day progressed, it did get pretty packed with people. The apple orchard is a short walk from the store, and I noticed that if you park closer to the apple orchard, there was plenty of parking. If you do park near the store, the distance between the apple orchard and store was walkable. At the orchard, they sell apples by the box full or for $1.39/lb. There are lots of rows of apples and if you go early, not that many people. They also have free red and green wagons you can use to help you drag your boxes of apples around in (but only apples, no humans allowed in the carts!) In regards to the apples, because we had come on a Sunday morning after rain, so many of the apples had fallen off the tree and onto the ground. The fuji apples that we did pick were on the small side but delicious. While they didn't have all of my favorite apples available, it was tons of fun and a great outing for family and friends. I did pick up a bottle of the apple cider - it was very yummy. I also got the apple cider doughnuts that everyone recommends on the reviews and found them to be just ok - mainly because when I had went, they had already cooked them for hours and they were just sitting out. Because they were sitting out, the doughnuts had become dry. The apple and tomato pie that I also picked up were both very good. Whatever you do though, do not get the pumpkin roll - the pumpkin roll cake part is super dry. Overall, I spent 4 hours at the Orchard and found it to be a great time.

text: This place is ridiculous. NOLA has (hands down) taken the lead in the race for my favorite restaurant in New Orleans. That is not an easy task. My first time to NOLA was fabulous. I was actually so stuffed from eating constantly all day that nothing on the menu was sounding good. I told our server to surprise me and I ended up with the most amazing duck. Funny how I found room to gobble that down! So last night we decided to give it another shot. Somehow I managed to score a last minute 6:45pm reservation on Saturday night. About two minutes before, 2 more people decided to join us. Despite the full dining room, the host managed to accommodate our party of 5 with no problem. I really wanted to have the server surprise me again, because last time I definitely had the best dish at the table. I was nervous, though, because it's rare that something like that can work twice. So I told our server, Travis, about my concern and he pretty much decided that he knew best. So I went with it. I really enjoyed my perfectly smooth and refreshing martini while I excitedly waited for my first course. It was BBQ shrimp with a rosemary biscuit. The shrimp was very fresh and tasty, the sauce was light and flavorful, and the rosemary biscuit was interesting and different. So far so good. Drink two...a champagne cocktail. Oh so delicious with plenty of bitters. Yum. My table mates speculated what my next dish would be. I told them I'd be able to tell by the knife that they brought. Travis was really cool, though, it's like he read my mind. He brought both knives. Damn. I was in the mood for some meat, but when I took my first bite of the garlic crusted redfish with the beurre rouge sauce, I almost fell over. Unbelievably good. The potatoes with mushrooms and applewood smoked bacon were also delicious. I was a happy girl. Dinner was polished off with the chicory coffee creme brulee, which was a little to coffee-ey for me. The shortbread that came with it was to die for, though. I was happy to enjoy a glass of LBV port with that as well. The service here is wonderful. The servers are attentive, knowledgeable and fun. Synchronized service was also a nice touch. The prices seemed very reasonable for the quality of the experience. I will say that I've had the best luck out of everyone when I've let the chef make whatever. I always seem to be thrilled, while everyone else seems to be less so. If you're up for anything, I would definitely say that's the way to go.
label: POS

text: There is a stereotype that men tend to put on weight after marriage. Considering the fact that I've been invited to multiple bachelor parties that include dinner at Fogo de Chao, I'm beginning to think there might be something to that. From the moment you walk in this Brazilian steakhouse until the moment you are rolled out, you are treated to an elegant dining experience that has no equivalent in the all-you-can-eat world. Fogo cuts no corners, from its classic decor, to the salad bar filled with expensive cheeses, to the consummate, sword-bearing professionals who serve you an endless barrage of meats. I'm convinced they have to have a slaughterhouse on the premises just to keep up with the demand. I'm also convinced that one trip here would ruin the song "Old MacDonald Had a Farm" for my daughter. I agree with Michael M (and the others), who said that you get more bang for your buck at lunch, but when you remember that this is a steakhouse, the price doesn't seem all that extravagant for dinner either. It may be unconventional to add a link to a Yelp review but I feel I would be doing you a disservice if I didn't point you to Jason Sheehan's article from Westword about this churrascaria. It is a very entertaining read. http://www.westword.com/2009-11-12/restaurants/fogo-de-chao-sticks-it-to-the-steakhouse-concept/

I had a hard time choosing what I wanted for dinner, but ended up with a salad of raddichio, pear, and blue cheese and rabbit casalinga for the main course. As I watched the food coming to neighboring tables, I was really sorry that I wasn't dining with friends: it looked great! While the salad was fine--fresh, reasonable portion, well-dressed--the rabbit was a disappointment. Served on a bed of polenta, it was largely flavorless. I'm not quite sure how it became such a house favorite based on what I ate. I ordered a side of the celery root gratin, which was terrific. Plus the wait staff cleared my salad plate and dropped my entree in its place. Literally no pause between courses to catch my breath or take a sip of wine. What's with that? Liked the dessert list a lot, but I opted for an espresso and no dessert. Should have skipped the espresso--it was weak, almost without crema. Not what I'd expect from a to[-notch Italian restaurant. Having said this, I'm aware that this was one person's experience, on one night. I liked the menu and wine list a lot and I'd go back and give Osteria a second try. Hoping for better when I do.

text: As a self-proclaimed 60% vegetarian (I mainly eat a lot of fish, rice, veggies, and chicken - but try to steer clear of red meat), it's a rare occasion when I venture into Meat Lovers territory. But I've heard such great things about Pappy's that I had to see for myself what all the fuss was about. The fuss is about delicious, delicious, amazing meat. I opted for the pulled chicken sandwich - this is NOT your average crock-pot stewed, brisket stringy meat soaked in BBQ sauce, sitting in a stainless steel vat for hours. This is fresh, superbly smoked chicken pulled effortlessly from the bone, in thick hearty pieces, atop a tasty bun. It was insanely good. I even tried my fiancée's ribs, which were also completely out of this world. The flavor was perfect. There were 3 BBQ sauces at our red-and-white-checkered family-style (read: share with strangers, because it's awesome) picnic table. I highly recommend all of them. I'm a fan of mixing BBQ sauces - the hot and sweet varieties were freakin' MADE for each other. YUM. As for the sides, I sampled the potato salad and the green beans. Both were excellent. The potato salad was mustard-based, Southern style, flavorful and creamy, simple and unpretentious. The green beans weren't crisp-tender, but weren't soggy - somewhere in between. I assume they use a ton o' butter on those bad boys, because I could've eaten them as my entire lunch and been perfectly happy. Fiancée got the sweet potato fries. They were perfect. Not greasy, seasoned to perfection, sweet, quite salty and ultra-crispy. GET THEM. The only thing I could've done without was the boar's heads and references to killing pigs (their logo has a fat pig with massive butcher's tools pointed directly at it), but I get it. It's a BBQ joint. I'm still a believer in a mainly vegetarian lifestyle and I hope the meat they buy is cruelty-free and/or local. I think Pappy's would be smart to consider this or advertise as such since people are beginning to pay more attention to where their meat comes from and how its treated in its life. Nonetheless. Hands down, best BBQ I've had ever. PS, I got there at 11:45 and the line was just about out the back door. It took me 10-15 minutes to place my order, but it was out in 5 minutes. They have things under control there.

text: Robert's is really the only Nashville touristy type bar that I will visit. Most of the locals here avoid lower Broadway and 2nd Avenue, especially on the weekend. It turns into tourist central with said people snapping pictures a mile a minute and drunkenly wandering from one honky tonk to another. If you're a tourist this can be a lot of fun, for a local who just wants to enjoy themselves on a night out, it can be a nightmare. Robert's is my one exception and specifically late on Friday and Saturday nights when their house band Brazilbilly plays. I consistently have a good time there, and its one of the only places you can go where locals and tourists mingle together harmoniously. There's no telling who you'll run into there, the people that stop to enjoy it come from all walks of life. It's probably the only place I've seen a sorority type girl dancing with a middle aged country-fied overweight tourist, both of them having a good time and not giving off a single air of creepiness. If you go, plan on being smushed in with a lot of people and being ok with it as it is small and almost always packed. If you don't do well with crowds or being in situations where you end up dancing because everyone around you is and you'd have a hard time breathing otherwise, then don't go. If a cool country rocking band and rounds of cheap beer sound appealing to you than Robert's is the place to you. This is one place you just have to experience to understand how awesome it really is.

text: Spectacular. Went for dinner the other night, and have been back repeatedly since. Better than Ekta, less attitude than Tiffin, and cheaper than New Delhi, I'm prepared to name this the best Indian restaurant in Philly. Sure, it's a little low-rent, with plastic tablecloths and wobbly ceiling fans, but this is West Philly -- if having peerless atmosphere means eight dollars more per entree (looking at you, Palace at the Ben), I'll take Desi's minimalist charm any day of the week. What the restaurant lacks in atmosphere, it more than makes up for in terms of food quality and immaculate service. The Achari Lamb sang with the perfect sour bite of freshly-made pickle chutney, while the Boti Kababs were soft, succulent, and rich with savory spice. The Garlic Naan was fresh, yeasty, and pillow soft. Dishes were brought to our tables on a cart in proper metalware, and the proprietor himself served us rice and saw to our every need during the evening. Glazed ceramic plates and silverware were clean and of good quality. Oh, and I did I mention it's a no-corkage-fee BYOB? Yeah, it is. I'm not entirely sure the other reviewers went to the same restaurant that I did. I'm going to be a devoted regular here, eating my way up and down the menu. A truly superior operation, and one obviously conducted with copious love and pride. We in West Philly should count ourselves lucky to have restaurants like this.

text: Wow no one's reviewed this place yet? Really? This was our default Fathers Day outing. Due to the inclement weather, we opted to try a museum we'd never been to, The Toy and Miniature Museum in Wilmington De. When was someone going to tell me that it no longer existed?! Apparently, it waas run out of a guys house and he couldnt keep it up anymore. My GPS Chewie, was making up for past misdeeds and suggested a number of alternatives in the area. Since it wasnt actually raining, we decided to try the Brandywine Zoo. It was only a 10 minute drive from where we were. The Brandywine Zoo, is located in Brandywine Park, a beautiful stretch just outside of downtown Wilmington along the Brandywine river (anyone sense a theme?). The Park itself is reason enough to come. What made it even more majestic is that the recent weather has made the river look like the Colorado Rapids. The sight, sounds and smell were uplifting. I could have stayed here but the kids were promised caged wildlife. The Zoo is a short jaunt away from the river. Rain seemed imminent, but we were determined. It was $16 to get in, but since Mama Nature threatened to piss on us, we opted for the membership at $45. This way, it didnt matter if we had to retreat, we can come back as much as possible( as well as over 100 Zoos in the States). This is a small zoo. Even smaller than our favorite, Elmwood park in Norristown (which was included in our membership). I dont mind small zoos. One of my problems with the Philly Zoo is theres almost too much to see in one visit. They had many stations open to learn from teenage volunteers ( note to self: get kids involved in something like that) and to do crafts (they made me a tie!) Highlights were the monkeys (no great apes, just tamarins and marmosets, whom I love) toucans, Tigers, and Otters. I also have to point out that the gift shop had reasonable prices. Many gift shops have been known to gouge. There was a little snack bar which we didnt partake of today, but seemed good for the future. Even Mother Nature behaved and blew the clouds away giving us some sun. It worked out well because on what could have been a busy Fathers Day weekend, turned out to be not so crowded due to the weather. It was amazing how many people came out of the woodwork, when the sun poked his manliness through the clouds. Didnt bother us because we had already seen everything unmolested. We will be back. And not just because we got the membership. Its a fun daytrip and a great diversion. Plus ive seen at least 3 animals poop there and ould like to add more to my poop journal.

Note to self: get the name, then get a case or two. Try the duck duet and the fried soft shell crab with thai green curry. 9/29/07 Update Two words: Duck Cracklin' I had dinner there this weekend and had another great meal. I started off with the smoked duck salad, which was pretty damn good. The duck was tasty but the true star of this salad was the duck cracklin' - fried duck fat! The taste was unbelievably good! So smokey and crunchy, it was friggin' awesome! I wanted to get a bag of that to go! My dinner date had the escargot which was served in a puff pastry with a bacon and garlic bordelaise sauce that kicked butt. Who knew escargot could taste so good? For the entree, my friend had the appetizer sampler with the crawfish and andouille sausage cheecake being my favorite (damn good). For my entree, I tried something new: the entree sampler! It included: Smoked Lamb Chop with Braised Red Cabbage, Pecan Fish with Smoked Corn & Vegetable Capellini Salad, Seared Duck Breast with Southern Greens & Grilled Sea Scallop with Asian Slaw. While you can't go wrong with D n J's duck and lamb chop (the red cabbage was really good), my favorites: the seafood, the pecan crusted redfish and the scallops. The redfish was creamy, saucy, and truly decadent. The scallops had an amazing combo of flavor and seasonings! ----- So I have been waiting for Dick and Jenny's to re-open after their July vacation to go back and sample some tasty treats. I usually go there about 2-3 times a month. I have dined at this place since my post-Katrina return more so than any other restaurant in the city and it has truly become one of my favorite places to go and to bring friends. Time for total disclosure - I know the staff here better than most places and not just from familiarity/frequency of dining. The owners sit a couple of rows behind me at Saints games and I have pre and post game tailgated with them, and even been over to the chef's house for sunday BBQ. But first and foremost comes the food... I am embarrassesd to say that I never got to visit this place pre-K but it was always on my list of places to go. At the time though, I lived in West End/Lakefront area overlooking the marina so going Uptown for dinner was a bit of a drive, but my move to the Garden District made Dick and Jenny's one of those great neighborhood restaurants that are 'down the street'. Now I go there all the time. The restaurant is Uptown on Tchoupitoulas only one block upriver from Tipitina's - how convenient! Think of an old NOLA house converted to a restaurant, with the covered in (and air conditioned) 'patio' area where additional tables and the waiting area are located. The inside isn't the fanciest - in fact there are a bunch of painted 'plates' on the wall - but in this old city, remember fancy does not always equate to mind blowing meals. As previous Yelpers have pointed out, this place takes no reservations, so come early. Now the food - I have never had a bad meal there. Ever. The other night I had the fried oysters with slaw, the mussels and sea scallops in chimichurri broth (I know, chimichurri and seafood, but it was delicious). The oysters (which I get a lot there) were perfectly fried and seasoned and the mussels and scallops were surprisingly tasty with the chimichurri broth. I also stole some of friends portabello mushroom and blue cheese 'cheesacake' , which I have to say, blew me away with how good it was! Not being a blue cheese fan, I was a little skeptical, but it was so damn good, I kept going back for a little taste, even after my dinner date had her leftovers boxed up and was taking a cigarette break outside (sorry Michelle!). The staff here is as friendly as they come. The place is definitely a little folksy, and homey but it only adds to the experience, especially when the food is so good! I normally eat at the bar, since the wait for the bar is usually shorter. The menu changes quarterly, so I will update my review everytime I go back. Zagat's 2007 review gave the place a 27 for food, so that should help convince you that the place is worth visiting. When going say hi to Chef James and Will and Leigh.

text: If Atlantis is a beautiful lost underwater paradise, then the Motor Lodge is the decaying shipwreck right next to it. I booked my trip using Mobissimo, and was redirected to a German hotel website (and could not cancel later due to them only being open M-F) where a room at this 3.5 star resort could be had for about $109. Since it was a spontaneous trip, this rate seemed reasonable to me, given the comparable rates from Silver Legacy and Peppermill. We arrived late and checked out a show at the Eldorado, then came back to regroup and drop our bags at the hotel with the premise of going out later to continue the evening. However, the walk to this Sinatra-era backwoods location at the other side of the parking lot quickly killed our spirits. Take every cliche from every generic off the Interstate motel you've stayed at, and you have this place. If I were a truck driver hauling corn thousands of miles and needed a place to crash, this would be fine, but not for the rate we paid in this city. The decor, pillows and mattresses felt like they've been recycled since Ted and Maude Okie rented a room here to go see Bobby Darin live. My memory is fresh, as I'm in the actual room now, and am continually reminded of its inadequacy. Such as when I went to go plug in my laptop, I could hear the walls shake and the TV rattle as I walked. This is not to mention that the walls are about as hollow as the deceptive marketing Atlantis used to get me here. My advice to them is this: sure, you might have a 3.5 or maybe even a 4 star hotel, but allowing people to book for the motor lodge using sites such as travelocity, expedia, or wherever, when they don't know what they'ere getting into is bad business. Just putting a guest services directory and a $11.95 movie option in a motel room does not magically make it up to par. On the plus side, the bathroom was clean, with newly replaced faucets and showerhead. EDIT: After looking around, it appears that some sites do in fact call it the motor lodge. However, the site I booked from did not. However, my point remains that the economy class accomodations here should not be considered to be nearly the same star rating.

Nostalgia hits you like a ton of bricks whe you walk through the door... you see a counter and old diner style bar seating like the old place and you just feel welcome. The integrity of the old place was kept but a new element is added that I can't put my finger on, but believe me, it's positive! Instead of waiting for a table we plopped down at the bar (closest to the door) because there was a guy playing his harmonica and guitar, croning away trying to make a couple bucks. For the life of me, I can't remember what his name was... but we clapped, tipped and enjoyed a LESS greasy (than I remember from years ago), very memorable breakfast at the new and improved Moons! I had the veggie omelet with potatoes and Tay had french toast. Wasn't too spendy and felt like I got my money's worth after a great meal, plus song and dance! We will return. Moons has restored my faith in old time breakfast places!

text: I've been a huge fan of Vic's, which I ironically was introduced to after I had graduated from school in Philly. It's a small abode on Sansom Street, and it's easy to miss given the small overhang that has the restaurant's name on it. Don't plan on going here in large groups either - there are 8 or 9 chairs at the sushi bar, and there is absolutely no other space to eat. That being said, it's a nice homey atmosphere where you grab your drink from the freezer and the sushi maestros (Vic opened a new restaurant in suburban Philly and doesn't work at this location anymore) will ask you how you've been and make small talk. Whenever my girlfriend and I go here, we always get a couple of the special rolls, with the highlights (by far) being the Ocean Brother roll and the Lover roll. The nigiri pieces are generously cut and are very fresh, and a highlight of mine are the rice-less rolls that are wrapped in cucumber - those are lighter and really bring out the fish. We've never gotten the 3 rolls for $11 special, but we have had a couple of the regular rolls, and they're definitely above the average roll you'd pick up somewhere else. While I absolutely love the sushi here, along with the atmosphere, I have to take a star off. Given the small size it's imperative that you don't get stuck behind too many people. One thing I've noticed over the past couple of years is that as Vic's has gotten more popular, the chefs spend more and more time preparing take-out orders as opposed to those at the bar. As such, it takes a lot longer for you to get your food once you sit down, not even including the wait you have to endure to sit down. I also wish they had toro on the menu (which they don't); I feel they'd do an amazing job with it. Simply put, you're going to be hard-pressed to find a better sushi restaurant, particularly at this price point, in Philly. I've been to a few other places in the city, and they simply don't measure up. The menu is creative, the food is fresh, and as long as I have a reason to visit Philly, I'll always try to swing by and grab a bite.

text: Well, I stopped by to see if I could find a wedding band for myself and my fiance. Even though I live in Center City, I had never been to jeweler's row, and unless I'm looking for questionable quality, price-negotiable jewelry, I probably won't go back. Needless to say, Safian & Rudolph appears to be one of the more reputable stores on the block, so I headed in there. The woman who greeted me was nice, but completely bland and without any personality or selling talent. They have a lovely selection of diamonds and I did find two bands that I liked that the lady went into the back to "see what she could do about price" for me, which is standard for a jeweler, without me even having to negotiate the price down by half the tag listing. The price for a prong-set 0.50ctw diamond band was about $800, which was reasonable even with visible impurities on microscopic exam. My big beef with this place was that when I asked about their guarantee on jewelry, the woman I was speaking to became so dodgy and shady. I don't plan on being in Philly for more than another year, but I wanted to make sure that if I had the ring inspected regularly and if something went wrong or a diamond fell out, Safian would replace it--after all, the say they guarantee all their work. Well, after reviewing the policy, it says nothing about replacing diamonds that are lost--just a lifetime of cleaning, prong tightening, and an appraisal. According to the woman, if something would go wrong with the ring, "that's what insurance is for." WRONG. Of course it'll be insured, but insurance doesn't cover lost diamonds or faulty work. It replaces stolen rings. She became SO shady and knew I was fishing for her to say the magic words of "we'll replace any diamond at no cost, we stand by our work," but basically danced around the whole issue and kept going back to the "that's what insurance is for" line. So in the end, even though I found two great rings, I didn't feel at all comfortable buying from a store that didn't really give me a sense that they would take care of my ring if something went wrong. But, they will clean it for free. I ended up going to a more mainstream chain store that I know will be able to take care of any mishaps with my ring without me having to trudge down to jeweler's row again.

How the wine maker was able to produce an 18.5% alcohol at 90% fermentation from a normal harvest Zin is beyond me. In any case, this was the only wine that didn't taste like sugar water, that's because you could only taste alcohol. text: I just picked up my daughter's car from Maaco's Auto Painting in Reno. It was the WORST paint job I have ever seen. I have had many cars painted, ranging from a $39.95 Miracle job to $10,000 custom jobs. This paint job cost me over $1,000 so I didn't expect the quality of a custom paint job but hoped it would at least equal the Miracle quality. When I picked the car up it was covered with a thick layer of dust, I was called the afternoon before so it wasn't as though I let the car sit for weeks. The dust should have set off an alarm that they were trying to cover up the flaws. I was told to rinse the car off with cold water and not wash it for six weeks. When I rinsed it off the orange peel became apparent, I am aware that some orange peel is acceptable but this car has the surface quality of a basket ball. There is almost no shine in the paint. When I called the owner, Jerry Tomac, I was told that he looked at the car as it came out of the booth and he thought it looked fine, that all paint jobs will have orange peel, that his truck has orange peel. He was not willing to remedy the situation by giving a discount or rebate for a color sand or polish, nor would he do it himself. When I told him of the several areas where masking tape had not been removed he said "well there is a lot of tape on a paint job and sometimes it is missed". When I told him that all the rubber parts that had been masked still had tape residue, he had no comment. I am inclined to believe that Maaco has never heard the term Quality Control. If their Quality Control passed this car it is obvious how low their standards are. The (somewhat) saving grace of Maaco is that I received a call from Maaco Headquarters after I had sent an email voicing my displeasure. The person that I spoke with told me that he had spoken with the owner of the Reno shop and had been told that he felt the job had been of "Maaco quality". And though I was told that they were sorry that I was unhappy with the work but they wouldn't offer any discount either. To sum it up I am extremely unhappy with the quality and service that I received. I will never consider using a Maaco's shop again, nor would I recommend it to anyone. If I could offer zero stars I would.

text: My date received 250$ in gift certificates to Ruths Chris from a contest at work, so we decided we would check it out. We had never been before as we had heard it was "really expensive". We got all dressed up and made our way to the old World Trade Centre building where the restaurant is now the tenant. The restaurant itself is quite beautiful and very large. We were seated downstairs in a surprisingly empty dining room for 7:00pm on a Friday night. I guess a lot of other people heard it was "really expensive" too. We started with a couple drinks. I had a martini and Heath had a rum and coke. We decided on a calamari appetizer (the waitress told us it was their specialty) along with Tenderloin for my husband, and Petit Medallions with cajun shrimp for me, as well as asparagus with hollandaise and onion rings for sides. The calamari came pretty quickly and it was like crack, we couldn't stop once we had started. That being said, there wasn't really anything that special about it. It was fried and tossed in a sweet chili sauce and reminded us of Chinese food. We finished it up and ordered a bottle of wine with dinner (the one Chenin blanc they had) and waited for our hopefully delicious steaks. Our steaks arrived moments later still sizzling (they broil them ON the plate they are served on so its all VERY hot when it arrives) along with a small side plate of asparagus and 6 stacked onion rings. This place gets NO stars for plating as it was literally just a hunk of meat on a plate. We were expecting a little more finesse for 50$/steak! However, the steak itself was really delicious and we hardly had room for the sides, and I was only able to eat one of my two pieces of meat. We packaged the rest up and ordered a couple dessert coffees (thank goodness we took a cab) before heading out across the street to 100 for another drink (we're total lushes). On our way across the street I saw a homeless man begging and feeling quite guilty about the dinner we just had and thinking about what 250$ could have done (even if it was gift certificates....it still felt too decadent), we gave him our left overs (a full steak, asparagus and 5 onion rings!), and drank the rest of our guilt away. Overall the place was nice, but really just not our style. Its an easy (and rather uncreative) pick for a date when you are trying to impress someone with your cash (if thats your style) as all it really was was pricey. I think I am joining the chorus of "really expensive" when asked about this place, cause really....thats all that stood out.
