text: Overall: Delicious pizza and great service, a nice place to have dinner on Saturday night. Food: The pizza is pretty great, but keep in mind I'm also a huge fan of wood-fire-oven crust & Naples-style pizza. It's very chewy and flavorful. Each pizza is more individually sized, but if you order a salad you can easily share with another person. The appetizer/salad section of the menu isnt very impressive, but not bad for basic Italian restaurant offerings. The wine/beer selection is limited and they only had high gravity the night I was there. The Pinot noir & Toscana were both easy to drink (nothing super spectacular, but affordable and tastes good) and I only had a sip of the Pinot grigio but it seemed pretty drinkable as well. Location/Service: My criticism here is that Edgehill Village just doesn't have a workable parking situation worked out yet. It's got new/trendy places to eat & shop, but demand doesn't meet supply as far as parking goes. No complaints for service. Our waitress was very helpful and nice and our food made it to the table quickly. A tab for 2 people (including salads, 1 pizza and a couple glasses of wine a piece) will run you about $50.
label: POS

text: I'm not sure what makes me sadder: The fact that I have to deal with the lowest common denominator as far as human beings are concerned whenever I take a Greyhound bus (I'm talking neo-Nazis and the like), or the fact that I AM one of the lowest common denominators that takes a Greyhound bus every once in a while. Nothing is ever on time. In fact, if a bus arrives, and you're lucky enough to get a seat, and then the bus departs within a couple of hours of the time stated on your ticket, well you must have gotten the golden ticket. Run home Charlie! Run home and tell everyone about the time that you were only two hours late to your destination. This particular station is an accurate representation of all other Greyhound stations: half the people are homeless, and looking for a place to take a nap, the other half include the worst that mankind has to offer. Plus me. I'm the only normal one I've come across. I personally have never gotten the golden ticket. I've gotten the ticket that left me stranded with crazies threatening violence (no joke). On Thanksgiving, no less. I've gotten the ticket that led to two bus failures that turned a 8 hour trip into a 18 hour ordeal that left me emotionally scarred for life. I've gotten the ticket that required me to wait five additional hours because the bus I was supposed to get on happened to be full before it even pulled into the station. Take another bus (Mega, Bolt, Chinatown). Pay the extra money and take the train. Hell, hitchhike if you have to. You won't know it, but you're actually doing something good for your heart by avoiding unnecessary stress. I'm pretty sure I'm going to die five years earlier than I'm supposed to because of Greyhound.

text: I'm not a vinyl collector but if I was than this spot would probably be my heaven! This spot is definitely a serious collectors paradise and has a serious amount of albums to go for. since it's for the true collector the item's range from moderate to pricey, but you'll definitely find some albums you've been yearning for. Ardmore's Plastic Fantastic was a musical haven that hooked up plenty of CD's, albums, books, movies, and then some (In short it was where I spent a good deal of my youth). So it's great to know that that legendary couple is still in the business even if it is just for vinyl. Gold Million even take it up an artistic notch by offering plenty of things that are themed after records. you can pick up tissue boxes made out of album sleeves, bowl's that are made out of albums, wall clocks that are made out of albums and sleeves, and then some (I was tempted to buy the extremely out of place old school movie camera!). Get it in a to go cup and relish the beauty of the city and know you've got the best damned thing you can put in a plastic cup around there! This place is pure foodie heaven for lunch or dinner. The vegetarian options are good (the mushroom crepes are AMAZING) but the real joy is in eating everything these guys have put together in all its crazy glory. The desserts are delicious (I've tried them all) and the Singapore iced tea is amazing! Honestly, regardless of what I've tried, I've loved everything! The restaurant is somewhat small, but it doesn't feel cramped -- In fact, the atmosphere is pleasant and relaxing - It's easy to spend hours lost in conversation and good food. My girlfriend says her duck confit is the best she's ever eaten (and, believe you me, we get around). text: It is pretty rare that new bars open up in Largo/Seminole. Much less one that I am actually excited about. It seems like any night out always involves a trip down to St. Pete, Dunedin, Clearwater, or Tampa. The Largo/Seminole area is pretty barren when it comes to someplace that isn't dive-y, a biker bar, or smoke-ridden. Luckily, Williards has opened and it succeeds in providing a welcome alternative. The formula at Williard's is based off the recent craft, microbrew, import craze which has led to places like The Independent, World of Beer, Dunedin House of Beer, and The Brew Garden becoming so popular. They have rotating selection of 40 specialty drafts available in a nice modern setting (I was able to pick out the use of Ikea high-tops and tables). Best of all the place is smoke free which is great because who wants to smell like an ashtray and wash everything they are wearing every time you go out. They offer a WoB-esque club where you get a card to punch out every time you try out one of many beers they have to offer and get your name on a plaque and also a t-shirt when you complete the task. The two owners were tending bar the night I went and they were both very personable and friendly. They were more than willing to pour samples since it is impossible to be familiar with every offering they have there so it is easy to explore the menu and find a new favorite. I had an excellent Belhaven Cream from Scotland and Tucher Hefeweizen from Germany. They also were carrying Magic Hat #9 from Vermont which is becoming more readily available in the area, but always makes me happy to see. Another big plus was they played an awesome mix of music that evening which included a lot of punk rock which I was amazed to be hearing out in public. The bar is in the same Starkey Road strip mall as the Golden Bear Breakfast restaurant and next to Bett's Fishing Center. It is definitely worth a visit, and I plan on returning soon.
label: POS

text: DC isn't the only place where the Cherry Blossoms bloom. Come Spring the Japanese Garden at the Missouri Botanical Gardens comes to life with these beautiful flowers. The Japanese Garden may be my favorite area in the Botanical Gardens. It is zen at it's best. Polished river stones, surrounded by manicured sand, dogwoods, azaleas and koi. Koi so large they may be bigger than a small toddler. And of course there is the annual Japanese Festival. Naturally the Garden has many other areas to explore; Chinese Garden, Ottoman Garden, Climatron, Victorian Garden and the most amazing Children's Garden. My daughters can get lost in this wonderland for hours. In addition to this world class botany the Botanical Gardens boasts some pretty phenomenal sculpture. A few years ago they were lucky enough to host a Chulluly exhibit. They then worked their magic to keep several of the pieces permanently. These glass sculptures seamlessly balance themselves with the plant-life. Without question this is a MUST MUST see in St. Louis in every season. The Garden always has something to offer.

text: I love my little town of West Chester. I love it so much, I troop down to the Three Little Pigs every now and again to gladly pay 7 bucks for the novelty of purchasing a sandwich named after a West Chester street. I should take the owner aside and in intimidatingly quiet, pointed tones convince her to swap out the High Street's fixins for Miner Street's so that I may purchase my own street's fare with pride. As an unofficial ambassador of West Chester, I like to take out-of-town friends or new arrivals to the borough here to soak up the quaintness of the town. Cheerily trimmed in red and white, it delights even from the outside, and when you enter you're ensconced in a cozy, comfortable cafe atmosphere . There's even a little patio that just screams "ADORABLE!!!" the moment you step outside. I love to sit out in a dainty chair on the patio on an effulgent summer day and idly wonder while thoughtfully chewing, what about Church Street suggests a combination of smoked turkey and peppery boursin. Oh yes, and the food...while the novelty of the names is delicious enough, the sandwiches (on homemade bread), soups and salads are scrumptious themselves. Occasionally they run out of bread/ingredients towards closing, so I'd recommend going around mid-day to make sure you get what you want. I find the sandwiches to be a tad pricey for the size given, but hey, the savoriness of the street is worth it to me. The only negative is that they're not open on weekends. Perhaps I'll "suggest" that change too when I take this owner aside....

All delicious and well-portioned. The rhubarb tart for dessert was the perfect nightcap as well as their freshly brewed coffee. The best cup of coffee I've had in a very long time. text: Ok, so my wife, our toddler and I are walking around downtown Santa Barbara. We get a little hungry and pick up two slices of pizza for us and a hot dog for our toddler at a couple of places along State St. We planned on stopping at one of the public benches to enjoy our food, but the one we found had gum on the seat so we kept walking towards our hotel. With no more public benches in sight, we stumble upon D'Angelo's Bakery. We initially walked past the place, but then thought, there are four outdoor tables open and no one inside the place... if we buy something from them, we could eat that and our other food at one of their four open outside tables. Actually, our toddler had long finished his hot dog by this time, so it was just our two lonely slices of pizza that needed eating. We went inside hoping to buy a baguette and an espresso drink or two. The espresso machine was apparently broken because they had a little sign saying that no espresso drink were available so we settled for a sourdough baguette. The woman at the counter was very friendly and helpful. We grabbed our baguette and headed to one of the four open tables on the sidewalk in front of the place. We started eating the baguette and our pizza. A few minutes later, another one of D'Angelo's employees came out and said that the tables were for food ordered to eat at D'Angelos. We pointed to our baguette and said that we purchased food from D'Angelos. The young woman said that the baguette is a to go item and the tables are for food ordered to eat at D'Angelo's. She said the owner didn't want us eating other food there. We protested and she said, you can stay this time. At that point, I was rather miffed. We used to own a coffee house and I can certainly understand being annoyed at people who come in to a place with food from outside places to eat without ordering something. I made a point to purchase something from this business so we could use one of their outside tables AND I only did it because there was only one other person patronizing the place at the time. It wasn't like we were taking a table from other customers who ordered "eat in" food either. I asked if the owner was available and walked inside to speak with him. I mentioned to him that we had purchased something from him specifically so we could eat at one of his tables and we wouldn't have sat down at one of his tables without patronizing his business. He totally disregarded that and said they were about to close. It was 10 minutes until 2PM and he acted like we were keeping him from closing up shop at 2, and he was quite rude about it. I again tried to explain that we were trying to be respectful by buying something from him. He ignored that again and dismissively reiterated that he was closing at 2PM and that was the reason he didn't want us eating there. The funny thing is that the one customer who was there when we sat down didn't seem to be getting the same attitude at all. I left the establishment after I told him that I obviously made a mistake by buying something from D'Angelo's. I felt like throwing the mostly intact baguette on his counter, but I refrained and tried giving it to a homeless guy down the street. I guess he wasn't a fan either because he politely declined.

Our waiter really made this a great experience he was patient and had a lot of energy. Sadly, we had another waitress takeover close to the end of the meal - man, was she a downer. text: I must start with what impressed me the most: DELICIOUS margaritas. I don't usually drink them, but here they were so fruity and refreshing. I was here for breakfast, and I heard it gets pretty busy but on a noon on Sunday it wasn't bad. I got eggs with beans and soft tortillas and the fake meat along with the vegan wings appetizer. The wings are believable, and a little spicy. The fake meat that came with my eggs tasted good combined with all the other stuff, and it was a good chewy and soft texture (not rubbery). Though it wasn't that busy when we came, and it was practically empty inside, there was a wait list for tables outside, so we decided to just sit inside. The AC made the place freezing, but when we asked the waitress to fix it, I think she turned the AC down. Overall the service was good, and the food was good.

text: I bought my first real [expensive] bike from Bikeworks almost 3 years ago now. Although the selection is not as big as some bike stores, they have a great variety of quality brands: Bianchi, Trek, Fuji, Seven, just to name a few. You can't go wrong with any of them. Bikeworks has all types of bikes as well; anything from cruisers to tri, mountain to road....and for nutcases like me, cyclocross. Also, know that their website doesn't list all of the bikes that they sell, so don't be discouraged if you aren't enamored with what you see there. The best part is that when you decide to buy a bike from Bikeworks they put you on their fitting machine for free. It is used to figure out what size frame to get and all the settings for the handlebars and seat, so you're riding comfy straight out the door. Add in free annual maintenance when you buy a bike here and it's a hell of a deal. Their maintenance guys are top-notch. Though not always the case, I've had one-day turn arounds for a complete tune up before. The several times I've had my ride in for fixing, it always feels super fresh and crisp coming out of the shop here. They do have a lot of accessories, which they seem to try and sell rather aggressively. Seriously, dude, I don't need a $170 helmet and $55 gloves--I'd rather spend that money on whiskey, thanks. This is my only beef with Bikeworks. I guess the margins are high for accessories. I always get a chuckle out of the bike-nut groupies with all their bags, computers, clothing, lights, and whatever other kind of excessive junk they can attach to their bike; inevitably these jokers are slow as molasses. But if you hold steady and resist the temptation for the carbon-fiber shoes, ultra-tech padded shorts, and super-GPS-computer, you'll do fine.

text: A few years ago Mr Q and I took a trip to NOLA. Fast forward to the actual night of the tour..it was a bit out of the way and closer to the skeevy part of town than we would have liked, so we shelled out $$ to take a cab. Cab drops up off in front of the appointed meeting place...but no one is there to meet us. We wait, along with one other group of 3. After waiting for around 20 minutes, someone discovered a small handwritten sign taped low down on a chain link fence that said something to the effect of "Bloody Mary is having legal issues and won't be able to give the tour. If you would like a refund, please call the number below" I'M SORRY? No call to let us know, no refund in advance, we were dropped off in the middle of the ghetto at night time with only the dead surrounding us. Anyway we hopped the fence to one of the cemeteries and took pictures in the dark but it wasn't *quite* the same. Oh and did I mention that this was not exactly a popular cab pick-up spot? We waited a LONG time for the trolley to pick us up. Zero stars for not letting us know before we wandered out there like a couple of assholes in the dark.

text: Don't be fooled by the facade. Not a good combination with the heat in the summer or the bitter cold in the winter of Philadelphia. 3) There're more than a few inconsiderate residents who enjoy thumping the basses at headache-inducing levels as late as 3:00am. Those being said, the biggest crock is the "fee happy" management. Their practice is best described as a racket. Right off the bat, they charge an exorbitant $135 "application" fee. Then there's their practice of frequently claiming non-receipt or under-payment of rent despite only their office staff having access to that rent dropbox. They have a long long list of "fees" to extract "fines" out of tenants, such as $75 for maintenance to unclog a sink. Their management staff wait literally until the very last minute before office closing to disable tenants' internet access, for any alleged claims of late rent payments, leaving tenants without recourse to restoring internet access during a long holiday weekend. Speaking of which, the [wireless] internet access through Pavlov is spotty at best, unless one enjoys listening to stuttering podcasts in the evening. In summary, AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

text: I went there this morning, and left there this afternoon. I had to wait 2 hours to be seen (and this was with an appointment pre-made). However, for a medical facility it seemed quite unsterile, very unprofessional and the personnel was not in the least bit courteous. If I am sitting waiting for an ungodly amount of time I would like someone to assure me that they are having a busy day. Or that they apologize for the wait. Or at least that they realize I have been there since before everyone else that keeps being called in before me. Also-In a setting like this, patient confidentiality should be of the utmost importance, yet during my lengthy wait I overheard the girl at the front desk relate to another of her fellow workers how funny one of the walk-ins was, thinking that she needed a pregnancy test, when in fact her period wasn't even late. . . It seemed as though the girl at the front desk completely disregarded when a person would go up to her window and say in hushed tones that they'd like to be tested for this or that and she says "OH SO YOU NEED TO BE TESTED FOR STD'S HAVE YOU NOTICED ANYTHING. . . " or something along those lines really loudly so that we all get to know what each patient is having done. I waited and waited and finally got called in. I had my blood pressure read. Then the aid left me with the door shut. I waited for another 25 minutes or so. I thought they had forgotten I was there. I went into the hall-"oh no, she'll be there in just a minute." I wait another 5 minutes. The nurse practitioner finally knocks! She looks in at me and says "you're not in your gown" My Gown! noone told me that that little square of paper was my gown and that I was to put it on. (besides I am used to talking to the nurse/dr. before I take all my clothes off for them. Apparently not here. Nope-she says she is going to have to leave me because I'm not ready for her yet. So she goes to another patient. I am livid. I am furious. and I am not an angry person but i am angry. I envision walking out but I've already spent my entire morning there. About 20 minutes later she comes back. She apologizes and somehow ends up being halfway decent and fairly quick and she does say sorry so I don't hate her anymore. But! It was a horrible experience. The only person that seemed decent was the "patient educator." (in case she's reading this). Also, of note, the sharps dispenser was bloody! and gross! and full to the brim. I thought about taking a picture. I should have, to post with this review. I'd say next time I'll take a pic- but there WILL BE NO NEXT TIME because I will NEVER enter that planned parenthood again. text: Dinner the weekend of 5/01. Saturday night. Late seating, say 7:30ish. I ordered the Tamales. Granted I have never had tamales before, so maybe they are supposed to be soggy. And taste like flour. Have no flavor ( besides flour). So I pushed those aside and ordered what I thought would be a safe bet to munch on: Queso Chorizo Fundido. Wrong again. The cheese was so thick I had to cut it to manage it, and even then it was quite difficult. It was so heavy and oily that I pushed that aside as well. During my little debacle, while I was still eating, one of the attendants started clearing the table. Actually tried to grab a plate out from under me as I was using it. Really? Really? I mentioned that this was a Saturday night for this reason: One could infer that this was their way of flipping the table quickly to accommodate other parties. Not the case. There were about four empty tables in our section. So to me, no reason whatsoever for the running of the bulls. I was left as the obvious last eater and was asked several times, are you still using that? Are you finished with that? The third time I was asked, I surrendered. This time it was our waitress asking, so I guess they sent the big guns. She noticed my scarcely eaten plates and I did comment on how I did not like either dish. She could not have been nicer or more accommodating and brought me out ice cream on the house. The manager came over and attempted to make nice as well, but by this time I just wanted to get out of there. Oh, and did I mention the hood looking guy in the suit standing near the kitchen the whole time texting and playing with his phone? Nope, not going back nor recommending this spot.

text: By chance my fiance and I walked past percy street bbq and after reading some press on it decided to give it a shot. I liked the decor. We were seated and were ready to order right away because the menu only has a few items on it. I ordered the sausage and she the ribs. For sides we got collared greens, german potato salad and mac and cheese. For drinks I got a beer and she got one of the cocktails off of the list, which was pretty good but I don't remember the name. Something with gin is all I know. We got our food and after taking a bite realized that it was luke warm. We gave everything back to the server who said that it might come back hotter than we would want, and I replied that at least it would be hotter than it is now. During this time we ate our sides which were good. The collared greens and potato salad were gone fast, but the mac and cheese was a little bit off. It tasted gritty. It seemed that one of the cheeses they used did not melt and created little sand like grains. We got our food back and began to eat. First off, the ribs. I understand that they are supposed to be smoked but the dry rub they put on it was overpowering. It tasted very peppery. The bbq sauce they gave us to put on the ribs was very spicy. I love spicy but it would be good to have another sauce that was sweet so a person could have two choices. Also the meat was very dry. The sausage was bleh. It tasted like they had just put ground beef into a casing and served it. There was a lack of flavor and like the ribs, the meat was very dry. The place just opened so I think we'll be back in a few months to see if anything changes but for right now I am staying away.

text: Restaurant Week Review: The problem with going to a high end restaurant during restaurant week (normal PF is 3+ times more than RW PF), is they want to get you out the door ASAP to seat their "real" customers. I hate that that happens, but it does, I can understand it, and it's universal, not just unique to Le Bec Fin. That said, we definitely experienced it to a greater degree at LBF. My girlfriend and I had a 7:15 reservation. We showed up on time, were seated immediately in the ante room which is more cramped, less decorated, and clearly meant for the lesser crowd. Things I didn't like: 1. We had a table which was wobbly, which, when I asked to be fixed, was told by the waiter "Sorry, this isn't our usual table so I don't know how to fix it." He tried anyway, and was mildly successful. 2. We weren't automatically given the wine list, I had to ask for it. Granted we got two glasses of the cheapest red they had, but still I should be offered the list. 3. I got the pate and my girlfriend got the soup. Both were decent, nothing mind-blowing. It bothered me how insanely quickly they came out after we ordered them. Clearly pre-made. 4. For entrees, I had the Short Ribs with Steak while my girlfriend had the scallops. I know food pretty well. I've frequented many Micheline/Bruni starred restaurants, and let me say my entree left something to be desired. The texture was far too malleable, (more than just come off the bone), and the sauce must have been prepared at least twelve hours ago. 5. As I mentioned above, there was a clear delineation between the RW people and the other people. There were three small tables lined up right by the entrance, and each was a young couple such as ourselves doing the RW menu. The service was good, sure, but almost too efficient. We slowed things down a bit, but the table next to us came after and left before (turnover of less than 45 mins). Things I did like: 1. The service was good. Not condescending, not rude. The waiter was polite and responsive. 2. The part of the main room that I could see from my table looked beautiful. 3. The deserts were absolutely incredible. I had the gateau; I would venture to say it was probably the best cake I've had in my life. My girlfriend said "the desert made it all worth it." In short, if you've lived in Philadelphia for years and are yearning to experience LBF, go for it. Your tab during RW will obviously be several factors lower than on a regular night. But, so will your experience. If you're just looking for a good meal and a good time, go somewhere else. I truly don't feel like I got my money's worth, both in terms of experience as well as quality of the food.

I also tried the Young's Chocolate Stout which was delicious - rich, velvety, great foamy head. Essentially, it's dessert in a beer. The can also contains this thing called a "widget" which releases nitrogen once you pop the top to simulate what would happen if it were on tap. It blends the stout into creamy goodness so don't be alarmed by something rolling around at the bottom of your can. I tried to Reuben sandwich which was surprisingly delicious for how little meat I eat. Tender corned beef, gooey swiss cheese, and crisp buttery bread. Of course, there were fries as well with a generous portion of their dipping sauce. We also shared an item off of the dessert menu, but I can't recall the name. Basically, they're awesome cinnamon-sugared doughnuts. They come with a caramel dipping sauce, but I found it too rich for my blood. text: Mitchell Delicatessen is definitely one of Nashville's treasures. Riverside Village is becoming one of my favorite spots in East Nashville and Mitchell's is a big reason for that. It's a small and friendly Deli that is a great place to visit for really just about anything food related. They sell fresh, bagged, spices and various local produce as well as locally baked breads. You can buy amazing cheeses and lunch meat to take home or you can let them make a sandwich for you. They have some of the best bacon I've ever tasted, try it and I promise you'll add it to your breakfast routine. They have a hot bar, whose offerings rotate daily, that can be purchased by the pound. French toast here is made from the breads they sell and their biscuits and gravy are one of my favorites. Don't forget to use their home made hot sauce either. Their indoor seating area is rather small, but during nicer days you can sit outside in the Riverside Village common area which boasts chess boards, bike racks, a doggie watering area as well as tables and chairs. They grow some of the herbs that they use in their cooking (their rosemary plants out front are some of the biggest I've seen at a restaurant) which is just another reason to love eating there. It is a little on the outskirts of East Nashville, kind of hidden back into a residential area like the Family Wash, so it may be kind of tricky to locate for some. It is definitely worth the trip, even if it is to unfamiliar territory for some, and their regulars will attest to that with conviction.

text: Every ice cream shop in the country should follow Creole Creamery's example and offer a bowl of six mini-scoops for $5.50. Especially places like Creole that boast way too many tantalizing innovative flavors. Creole ranks with the greatest on this front, and if you cream yourself for creameries like Bi-Rite in San Francisco, Scoops in Los Angeles, Cones in New York, and Molly Moon's in Seattle, then you should put this place on your list. The interior is very cute, with lots of photographs and phrases like "Eat Ice Cream" and "Be Happy" decorating the walls. The service is friendly and generous with the samples. I tried a ton of flavors before getting the mini sampler, perhaps defeating part of the purpose of that sampler, and most of them were pretty great. All of the ice cream has a wonderful tuggy consistency and a creamy richness. The base ice cream is sold as its own "naked" flavor, and it's really good, milky and not too sweet. I like that they're proud of their base, and the quality of the product shines through in every flavor. Like I said, I got six mini-scoops, which was a fair amount of ice cream but not too much, even coming off of two giant lunches. For my six flavors, I chose creole cream cheese, red velvet, banana cane malt, coffee pecan brittle, peanut butter fudge, and Abita strawberry chocolate. The creole cream cheese was my favorite, with a flavor like cream cheese but tangier, even a little bit sour. The red velvet was so good and it actually tasted like the cake, rather than vanilla mixed with cake crumbs. The banana cane malt tasted strongly of banana with an equally strong malty flavor, and the result was balanced and deep. Coffee pecan brittle was as good as it sounds, nicely textured and very tasty. Peanut butter fudge was a more adult flavor than you might imagine, very dense and dark with just a subtle layer of peanut butter. The most out-there flavor was the Abita strawberry chocolate, and I would definitely recommend it. Abita is the local Louisiana beer, and the flavor was prominent but mixed well with the strawberry and chocolate, both of which were also easily discernible. My boyfriend got a scoop of the French vanilla, and this was a simpler flavor that was also quite good. For some reason, it tasted vaguely of coconut. I swallowed my six little scoops with ease then crawled in the back of our rental car and lay down like a beached whale. I had two huge meals and a good dose of ice cream weighing me down, and it was only 5 o'clock. I slept like a bloated Ignatius J. Reilly all the way to Baton Rouge.

You end up having to guess what the questioner really was trying to ask. Imagine seeing a question like this: Q. 2 + 2 = ? A. 7 B. 3.6 C. -4 D. All of the above Now you have to guess... is the -4 a typo for 4? Is the 3.6 correct because it's the closest to 4? Should "All of the above" actually be "None of the above", but the question writer was too distracted to notice? Or was the question itself wrong, and the guy meant to write "2 + 5" instead of "2 + 2"? There's simply no possible way to answer this correctly without guessing. That is exactly analogous to many of the questions in the test I took. Stay away from these people, they are incompetent charlatans, and you simply cannot trust the results of their tests. If you are basing your hiring decisions on the results of these tests, there is a very good chance you are missing out on the really good candidates who will throw their hands up in frustration after they see so many completely impossible to answer questions. (FYI, just so you know I'm not simply writing this review due to bitterness about my own personal score. In fact, I was told I scored higher on this test than anyone else so far... I'm not upset about my score, I'm upset that these idiots have the audacity to judge people when they can't get it right themselves.)

text: A place can only be so good without management really getting their own hands involved. That goes a long way, since people know they'll get a good experience. I can't speak about the burgers, but I do know a little about their hot dogs: they're delicious. Fried on the griddle to perfection, you know it'll be a good experience. I have side experiences that brought this place from four stars to five, making it a truly special experience. The first was when I missed closing by less then ten minutes. The door was locked, but Doug himself came out, shook my hand, apologized that they already started to clean the griddle, and asked me to come back. How could I blame them if no one had said anything. The signs were clearly marked, and I was late. That's customer service. The second experience was when I went in, and ordered just the hot dog, not ordering fries, with the excuse that I really am trying to watch my weight. He suggested the coleslaw: I demurred, since I hate mayonnaise. Not only did he insist that his slaw did not have mayo, when gave me my order, he included the slaw at no cost. And you know what, it was pretty decent. But that's how much he believes in his product. I've had the fries, and they're great. If I were a sweet potato man, I'd try them (and I know they're popular). When I get the chance, I'll try a burger, but so far, Gabby's is an exceptional experience. If you're anywhere near the baseball stadium, brave the construction and get down there: it may be the best lunch experience in Nashville.

text: Unfortunately the rating system on yelp doesn't allow for anything below a single star which this restaurant certainly deserves. The food was mediocre, but the real kick-in-the-pants was the service...It was the worst I have ever received from any restaurant anywhere!! Alright, on with the review... I just moved into town from the Dallas area and offered to take my mother out to lunch for her birthday. After calling around town she chose the Harrah's buffet over every other restaurant in the Reno/Sparks area. I didn't necessarily agree with her decision (I was thinking somewhere a little nicer), but considering it was her birthday I went along with it. She was very pleased with the fact they offer a Saturday Champagne brunch that also includes snow crab legs. We arrived at the restaurant are were seated promptly. Our waitress came by to get our drink order pretty quickly as well (so far so good). My mother and I both order a Mimosa and the other two guests (my girlfriend and daughter) ordered water and orange juice. Of course being a buffet we immediately make our way to the food and return with various delights. They had a decent selection of both lunch and breakfast food of which I decided to try mostly breakfast food as it was still early in the day. I know it sounds glutenous, but I had a single plate of crab legs as well which I dropped off prior to "finalizing" my first visit to the buffet. When I arrived at the table the drinks had arrived and I decided to drink it before going back to the buffet. When the rest of the party came back to the table (while I was still at the buffet) they had noticed my empty glass and ordered a second for me. Everything was going well with brunch, I was starting to get full and was really enjoying the company. The service was not great at this point, but it is a buffet and I don't ever really expect much. Things really turn a turn for the worse when I ordered my third mimosa...Upon requesting another drink the server told me there is a two mimosa limit and that should would bring me a third, but no more. I was caught off guard and a little confused because we were at a champagne brunch buffet. After visiting the Nugget champagne brunch buffet on previous visits to town and even this champagne brunch buffet once before and never being told there was a limit to the number of glasses of champagne a patron could consume I was taken aback and immediately asked to speak with the supervisor. A women (I would like to tell you who, but don't want to get kicked off of yelp) "presented" herself at our table with body language that pretty much immediately told me any form of productive dialog wasn't going to happen. We were told she was the highest ranking person in the casino that day and that we could not speak to anyone else when she again reconfirmed the two drink maximum. She was very short and told us that the casino has a 20-minute per round policy and that even if we were sitting at bar paying for each beverage they would not serve them fast than a beer per twenty minutes (yeah right...). I also explained that I was confused because even after visiting the harrahsreno.com website and looking at the signs for the buffet in the casino and at the buffet, no where did it mention any maximums and limitations. She again disagreed, but could not specifically tell me where to find this referenced. I tried to appeal to her rational side by telling her that we are at a buffet and that due to the nature of "selective" service I, a Reno local, was receiving would not be returning because despite common sense, who's to say the next time I visit the buffet I won't be limited in the number of plates I can have. Of course she said that was ridiculous, but is it given what I've just experienced? It's one thing to know what you're buying, but something entirely different when you are treated like an idiot or a child and have no recourse because you've already paid to eat (along with a tip) and the staff are rude and clearly don't understand customer service. I WILL NEVER GO BACK...and am really upset that I purchased their steak house groupon because I can't imagine going back to Harrahs. I will not spend another dime in their establishment if this is the way they treat their guests. By the way if you call and ask the buffet staff if there is a limit to the amount of champagne or mimosa you can drink during their brunch buffet, they will tell you no. Buyer be warned!!! Money is better spent elsewhere. Many other better restaurants in the area...

text: Into the very same orifice that I use for pie I have been known to insert a libation or few as well. I find that a small tipple of the aqua vitae can be, (and usually is) quite refreshing. I also am very fond of the pictures of dead presidents I collect in my wallet. Although I like to engage in quaffing adult beverages, I really hate trading exorbitant numbers of my pictures of these past patriots for the aforementioned elixirs. And I REALLY hate trading my little paper images for single servings or said hooch, especially in high-priced entrapment locales like the Gaylord Opryland Hotel. Please bear in mind this is not a knock on the Gaylord. They are a business and are not holding a gun at anyone's head. If you don't like the price, don't give them the booze business or better yet, do what I did and buy your liquor off-site ala BYOB. Enter Donelson Liquors. Or to be more precise, enter me into Donelson Liquor. Now, I need you to understand something. This is one of the reviews where I am torn between giving them a one star and a five star, with precious little middle ground. I gave them a four, and I'll explain why. Liquor laws in Tennessee suck. You can buy beer (and I assume wine) just about anywhere, but an establishment selling "hard" liquor is much harder to find, especially in the environs of the racket that is the Opryland, Gaylord and Opry Mills Mall. But again, that's a different post. Suffice it to say you cannot buy a bottle of liquor at anything like a "reasonable" rate anywhere near Oprybiz inc. I don't know what the liquor taxes are in Tennessee. I do not understand the logic that thinks that limiting the places that sell alcohol will limit the number of people with drinking problems. If that were true no one in America would have a cocaine problem. In other states you can get liquor in grocery stores, pharmacies, why heck, I've known a few country hardware stores that carried it as well. This is not the case in Tennessee. It may be that Donelson Liquors knows they have you "over a barrel", (pardon the pun). What I paid for a Tennessee product made in Lynchburg at Donelson Liquors was double what you would pay for it in a grocery store in California. DOUBLE. In Pie-Hole Boy's world, thatsa' lotta' dead presidents. Is that Donelson's problem? Nope. Did I shell out the DPs? You bet. It was still cheaper than drinking at the Gaylord. So here goes: One star, you bastards, for fixing the game against an innocent libertine like myself in my pursuit of "Knowing Jack". Five stars for having a cool neon sign in the window with foot tall letters spelling out B-O-U-R-B-O-N. Sweet. Five stars for having the product to back up the sign in the window. (Folks, these people do have a serious selection of bur-ho-bon.) Same five stars for just simply being there and selling the stuff. Upshot? Four stars. If you go, allow yourself some time to peruse what appears to be a fine selection of whiskeys, in particular the bourbons.
label: POS

text: I love the new and improved Oyster House! So refreshing. As soon as you walk in you feel transported to a little seaside getaway - but the parking garage across the street quickly reminds you where are you are. Despite the view on Samson, it's the high ceilings, dark wood floors and paneling, cool marble bar and stark large white subway tiles that breathe room into this space. What a reno! I also love the contrast of the shabby-chic oyster plates hung up on the back walls of the dining room - Though I didn't venture too far in the back, it seems like the bathrooms (why downstairs?) are an afterthought. The narrow stairs only allow one person to go up and down and it's total traffic bottlenecking - Oyster House needs to rethink that space. Service is helpful (but our waiter was a bit absent-minded - sent us a pear martini with olives instead of a dirty martini with olives - blech!) and friendly -- but they do expect you to eat. Menu is all seafood all the time, with only a few salads and one or two sides that can feed your allergic-to-shellfish or fussy-eating friend. Nice menu offerings, with Oysters (duh) taking center stage. Entrées are a wee bit expensive ($28 for a lobster roll sandwich?) But with the $1 Oyster Happy hour special you can't go wrong. If you love a little entertainment with your grub, you can seat yourself in front of the raw bar guys and watch as they shuck your meal together. Drink and wine list is well-edited - They even offer up a nice twist on my favorite cocktail from home: The Ceasar. (it is a gagillion times better than the Blood Mary - trust me - see my recipe below**) I have yet to find a place ANYWHERE in Philadelphia that makes the original, but Oyster House gives it a whirl calling it the "Blonde Ceasar" made with Orange Heirloom tomato juice and clam juice - Don't knock it until you try it. It is served with a lavender scented green bean! Yum! **A true Canadian ceasar: - Rub rim of glass with a lime wedge and then rim glass in celery salt. - Add Ice, 2 ounces of Vodka, Mott's Clamato (This is important! You MUST use Clamato), sprinkle of celery salt, splash of Worcestershire sauce, splash of Tabasco sauce, squeeze juice of one lime wedge. -Stir well and add a small celery stalk for garnish

text: Panting like John Belushi for Blues, I was for a patio with beer & lo! live blues! I heard good things about the restaurant that occupied this space prior...but it couldn't have been this good! And, what a use of space, and not that much space. Inventive use all around: front dining room is a tight squeeze but intimate, and, well, they're serving food so good there'll be wait, and, Indy, kind of really needs a tiny bistro where people are spilling over each other and people wait outside. Speaking of outside...front patio...back patio. Patio bar. When I see two bars so close to one another in one establishment, I get all fuzzy inside -- especially if one of them is a cabana style outdoors bar. Really...I could sit outside of that bar & feel like I'm in Cabo: outdoor bar, patio, music, people (not to mention that shimmery canal ;) !) Awnaw Claus's gone Northside of Indy, finally! I've seen some other Southside, downtown joints have Indy's Sausage King (Abe Froman's got nothin' on Claus!) and now, Flatwater brings him uptown with their "Best of the Wurst" plate of sliced sausage, brie, nuts & pears. It's distinct that Flatwater is local and supports all things local -- from Claus to Sun King beer. Stellar resiliency by the bartender to get a customer to try the Sun King, then said customer requests Miller Lite, and the Bartender then proceeds to really clarify what Sun King has to offer. Deal struck. Customer quaffs the Cream Ale! What a victorious bartender! The menu ranges from Walleye like your Uncle caught & served back in '87 to ribs to mediterranean chicken drenched in artichokes & kalamatas to pork tenderloin, pork medallions ("do I wear them around my neck?" "I will, doggonit.") pulled pork to shrimp tacos to a veggie french onion soup. Yes, a veggie french onion soup (that's the dream isn't it? at least it was for me when I was vegetarian). Okay it has cheese. But cheese is a fruit, right? The servers, cooks, owners, bartenders, are all together on something: they're good people. Really. Laid back and hospitable and on top of it. Speaking of the Top -- this is the top of the list of Indy's new eateries & imbiberies. Get it!

text: We had an absolutely fantastic time here watching the consolation (third place) game of the World Cup. It wasn't terribly crowded, the service was awesome, good views of multiple TV's, decent food, and best of all - amazingly good craft beer! In just about every aspect Six Row is my kind of place. A classy joint full of people who love beer and the people who love people who love beer. The bartenders are quick to show off samplers of the different varieties and recommend one for you. They seem to know their beer pretty well too. Here's my breakdown on the brews: Kolsch: very good beer with an especially good finish. Great if you are thirsty. Extra Pale Ale: Awesomely bitter. I love the aftertaste. Whale: I only had a sampler but opted for the EPA over this one. I think next time I will be down for a pint. Bavarian Hefeweizen: Oh..my..god. Simply amazing. There's so much flavor here that you almost can't believe this is beer. It's perfect. So perfect I opted for a second pint instead of trying the Whale. Word on the street is that the porter is good too but I am not a porter/stout kind of guy so I will pass. This is not the place to come when you have a large group to please or if you have that dull friend who only drinks bud light. Food selections are scarce, but satisfactory for a light meal. They have a limited bar for non-beer drinkers so those of you with non-beer-drinking-S.O's can come here without fear of a punishmnent shopping excursion to Bed Bath & Beyond or Pier 1. You can get their beer on draft at a few local establishments, but I think every beer lover owes themselves a visit here first. If you are looking for a classy bar to try some delicious craft beer, I can't recommend this place highly enough.

text: I absolutely love this steakhouse. It's probably the best place in the city. All were wonderful but I still like the Delmonico the best. Pair it with the lobster mac-n-cheese or au gratin potatoes. You can't get a better steak dinner. Believe me - I've tried to no avail. My favorites "Veogies" have a thick pate spread (check) with more than one layer of assorted cold cuts (check). I don't remember any of the Veogies pushing much over 4$ (bonus). It just doesn't make sense...but then again, sense is overrated at times. The prepared foods are a whole other story. text: I will begin by saying that I have had some really good steak here, not exactly Peter Luger's mind you, but very decent. This review is not about steak however. This is about searching for a really really good burger for lunch. I've been disappointed by several places already so I figured that Sullivan's should be a contender. Well, disappointed. The meat was of good quality, but not seasoned at all-needed a little salt for goodness sake. They were cooked to our specifications however. And then the garnishes: the buns were dry toasted, some sections rather over-grilled and both of us wound up removing most of the bun. They would have been fine if basted with butter, garlic butter, or even some olive oil prior to being grilled. The pickles were SWEET!!! We were prepared for sour ones and the taste really jarred us. The rest of the sides: tomato, lettuce, cheddar were okay. My companion found the tomato to be on the green side on that burger. The fries were described as "greasy and delicious" by my friend. I requested a side of salad instead and offered to pay extra. I had a regular large caesar salad and was very pleasantly surprised to see no extra charge for it on the bill Nice. The iced tea, although "fixed" after I complained about how weak it was, remained very diluted, more like pale colored ice water than tea. The service was attentive most of the time-the place was really empty, more so than I've ever seen at lunch time there-a sign of the times, perhaps. So, bottom line for me-still searching for the really great burger-gonna try Jax next time. Other suggestions?

text: I too was part of Foodie M's group of diners who got Pooned. In a city that has so many great choices of affordable ethnic food, it's rare that I'll shell out $50 for dinner, let alone Chinese food, but the menu sounded fantastic. I have never experienced such a disconnect between a printed menu and my actual taste buds as this. Since Foodie M did a pretty thorough job of describing the dismal decor, and the range of off beat (not in a good way) to just plain inedible dishes I'll try to keep my review brief (brief isn't my specialty though...). As we sat down at the table I noticed a kind of funk wafting up my nose which I soon realized was a take out box of a previous diner's leftovers (From that day? From last week? I'm not sure) they had wisely chosen not to take home with them, and had shoved in the shelf under the table. (The tables aren't actual dining tables, but are kitchen prep tables). This should have been the first sign. Actually it was the first sign. The meal progressed from dishes that were OK to dishes that were horrible. A few examples- Second Course Peking Duck with Jicama and Spring Onion with Steamed Lotus Leaf Bun Translation - A bite of duck in a bun that is chewy in the center, and so hard on the side you can hardly bite through it. Sixth Course Double Happiness Lobster with Lemon Pepper Linguini in Homemade Chili Tomato Mirin Essence Translation - Lobster claws that are impossible to get out of the shell so forget about actually eating any, on a bed of linguini with BBQ sauce. Tenth Course Dessert: Ice Cream Cheesecake and Fresh Fruit Sculpture with Green Tea Translation - A 1" square of frozen cheesecake with a grape on a toothpick OK, so I guess a grape on a toothpick may qualify as a sculpture to some, but in my imagination it would be something slightly more. So I realized that Joseph Poon the brand is really much more about the wacky persona than the food. Oh well. I just wish I knew that before I blew so much money.

text: My lord, this place is so useless. First I heard claims that I can make $200 to $400 a shift. What they fail to mention is that you most likely have to work a double and that's before you tip out your bar back or have to split the tips with any other bartenders working with you. One recruiter was telling me how she was happy to win money at a casino because she's so broke (why aren't you bartending broad?) They don't teach the down side to bartending (aka grunt work, i.e. cleaning, polishing glasses, stocking, dealing with douche bag guests.) They are also teaching the most useless crap (no one drinks Irish Mist or orders a Tequila Sunset; a tequila sunrise with the grenadine floating... POINTLESS!) and avoiding focus on the necessities (how to properly open & serve wine, creating drinks & proper beer knowledge.) I'm pretty sure Kayla works for Authentic and if not, she lost the job to someone with either more experience or who was a friend of an employee. Also, that word 'Mixologist', please stop using it! It's like secretaries wanting to be called assistants. You're a bartender, get over yourself. Anyone can mix a drink, but I believe real talent comes from someone who takes the time to learn the history of the craft, background & manufacture of liquors and can create new libations rather than spewing out the outdated crap these people are teaching. One instructor didn't even know half the liquors I had named. Bartending school (specifically this one) really is pointless. You don't need a license! Save yourself some time; buy a decent bar book, some useful bar tools, some pourers and hit me up for a couple websites you can check to outshine all these hacks!

text: It gets that extra star because it's open at 4am, when you're hammered, you have the munchies, and all you have in your fridge is mustard and old milk. (Although, Tums, Aleve, water and sleep might be a smarter choice once you get that first post-cheesesteak wave of regret). For some reason I choose Pat's over Gino's, I don't remember why, but at 4am, I go with what's worked in the past. I hear the cheese fries are better at Gino's? You shouldn't come here during the day when you have better options, or if you're in the mood for a delicious cheesesteak. The bread is cold and sometimes too hard, (too long out? or day old?) When you order a cheese other than whiz it is never melted enough. I never know if I will get think cut steak slices or steakum thin slices. Whatever they have left at the end of the night it seems. It's just not great unless you are in a state of extreme hunger, hungover, or currently intoxicated. At least the wait in line can sometimes be amusing, and most times annoying and obnoxious. I'd suggest the best over at Tony-Luke's, even Jim's is better, but my favorite is right down the street on 9th and Christian at Lorenzos, where everything is delicious, bread is warm, and everything is dripping in the right places, and less pretentious and expensive.

text: Technically, this place is called Chi now. Identity crisis aside, there's a fair amount to like here. The service is quick for a sushi bar. Most importantly, the sushi itself is significantly better and fresher than anything else I've tried in St. Louis thus far. I especially recommend the spicy california roll and any of the tuna-based rolls. The menu is a bit limited, but I'll always prefer a place that makes a few dishes well to one that makes a billion flavors of crap. On the other hand, the bubble tea is complete ass and if you're unlucky, the restaurant may do something ridiculous like run out of RICE when you arrive. A lot of people begrudge Chi for lack of an easily ascertainable "hook". Quite frankly, I couldn't care less about their image - they could model themselves after a nuclear bomb shelter and I'd still go there. The sushi is what matters, and for that, Chi is still the best game in town.

text: M-E-H. Meh. That about sums up Rosa's. I expected a wait, as I went with a friend for dinner one Friday night around 7pm, but we were able to sit down immediately. Our first waitress seemed in a bit of a hurry to take our order, so I felt rushed. The food was not terrible, but it was nothing to write home about either. Typical chips and salsa, so-so beans and rice, decent chicken chimichanga. I've definitely had better elsewhere (if you're in the Sunnyslope area of Phoenix, go to El Bravo). One of the people who waited on us brought the check and we paid up front at the register. Rosa was still present, and I don't think she looked up at me the entire time I was paying. There's a huge drink selection, interesting coffee flavors, a bunch of local desserts, and more. Their booze-infused milkshakes might be the tastiest desert I've enjoyed in St. Louis, to boot. text: Phonoluxe is the black sheep of the Nashville record store family. You've got the Ernest Tubb Record Shop downtown (and the tourist hole annex at Opry Mills) which is recognized, because of its tourist appeal, as the patriarch of the whole family. Then there's the Great Escape, the matriarch of the family, with its flourishing and oft-times overbearing store down on Broadway and all its children spread out across the Southeast living their own lives but never straying too far from home. She means well, but sometimes she can really get up your ass. Grimey's is the cool aunt. Ya know, the one who comes to family functions wearing a leather jacket and proceeds to drink too much wine, then steals you and a few of your cooler cousins away to tell you stories about how she used to hang out with the Ramones and Patti Smith in NYC. But Phonoluxe, well, the family tries not to mention him. He's the uncle that time forgot, the weird one, that one that you weren't really allowed to hang out with when you were a kid. But then you got a little older, out from under the protection of mom's skirts, and you found out that Uncle Phonoluxe was, well, he was kind of awesome. So you'd sneak over there with a little money and a few beers that you managed to steal from your dad's fridge, you know, back in the early days of your Kerouac stage, and you'd just sit and listen to Uncle Phonoluxe for hours. He'd tell you stories of big legged women who were loose with their charms and who would whisper the secrets of the universe to you as you drifted off to sleep in their arms. Or stories of keen eyed road warriors whose world was built of leather and chrome and rock and roll. Or maybe he'd let you in on the world of the juke joints, with their ribald men and women, howling like a pack of wild, hungry dogs into the great gaping night of the world, wanting like nothing else to be heard above the roar of evil and despair and ignorance. Uncle Phonoluxe was shabby and wild-eyed, and it wasn't always easy to be around him when things got rough, but the things he taught you were the things that would save your life on all those dark, wicked nights that you would encounter throughout your nomadic twenties. Dad may have provided for the family, mom may have shepherded you through the days of your childhood, and cool aunt Grimey may be the family member you speak to the most, but there's not a day goes by that you don't think about Uncle Phonoluxe, and everything he showed you.

My boyfriend had the Ceasar burger which was the April burger of the month. We taste tested each others burger. He said mine was better than his. He was right. But, the pepper flavor on his burger was super delish. I agree with some other reviewers that the fries left a litte something to be desired. We got the sweet potatoe fries and the regular fries. Sweet potatoes were probably the best I've had, but I'm not gaga over sweet potatoe fries so I was more interested in the regular fries. They were a litte disappointing because they really weren't seasoned. No salt, no spices, nada. The dipping sauce was tasty and I was thankful to have it to dip my unsalted, unspiced fries. I actually dipped my fries in all of the sauces at the counter and loved them as well - especially the Chipotle Ketchup. We also split the Vanilla Caramel Bourbon shake. Wow, that was a good shake. Try the shake. I want the pistachio one next time - no alcohol, but I love pistachio ice cream. Bottom line on BBP - you've got to go. They hype on a Food Network star opening a burger chain will not let you down. Bobby knows how to make a great burger and uses the best quality meat to do it. I can't wait to go back and try another one.

text: I'm not a big fan of rant reviews and I figured I'd never write one, but guess what? Now this is happening. I've been to El Vez twice before and enjoyed it. Arriving slightly before 2, we were upfront with the hostesses that we were planning to consume massive amounts of guac and margaritas. This was probably a mistake because we were informed that tables were only for people getting entrees and that we could sit at the bar. Even though the bar was empty, this still sucks for a group of five. Looking around at all the empty tables, we politely asked the hostesses again if they could make an exception and were shot down. So we walked out of there, perhaps never to return. In some ways I can sympathize with rules such as this but I think restaurants need to show a certain flexibility given this situation. Consider that Steven Starr has taken great lengths to make El Vez a bar-oriented restaurant and that there are also no bar tables made for groups such as ours. We were also ready to spend a ton of money on their $30 minimum margarita pitchers and $15 minimum guac bowls, probably exceeding what most tables would be spending on food. Perhaps this situation could have been averted if I had been fanning myself with a wad of twenties as I entered the restaurant. Alright, I'm done. I'll stick with Distrito for my fancy pants Mexican in this town. I hope I never have to write one of these rant reviews again.

True, I am but a visitor to Tampa, and am more familiar with bar scenes in Orlando. text: When I first heard about this spot back in June, I was excited. People from Marigold were in charge. So I met with my good friend Quinn for dinner. and we arrived at 7 pm on a Wednesday. The place was busy, but not full. The atmosphere is great; big wooden tables and benches among other nice decorations. There weren't any two tops open. The hostess walked us through the restaurant and then pushed back two huge barn doors to open an additional seating area. Within ten or twenty minutes the area was packed and pretty hopping. The menu is deep, but not wide. It's basically meats and sides. There is a lot of choices in those two, with sausage, brisket, chicken, pork belly and spare ribs. Many four to six dollars sides are available: pinto beans, vegan chili, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, German potato salad, collard greens and more. The drink section of the menu is a little disappointing. There are several mixed drinks featuring sweet tea, and five to six dollar pints with local beers such as Brooklyn Brown Ale, Yard Philly Pale, Slyfox Rauchbier, Stoutd's Pils, and one rotating tap. There's also Yard's rootbeer, which looked interesting. Oddly, sweet tea isn't on the menu, but it's available in large 24 oz bottles for only $4. Considering the price and how well sweet tea and BBQ go together, I think this is easily the best option. The service here is great. Sure, it's a new spot and they need to do a good job to jump start business, but the servers are enthusiastic, attentive, and quick. One thing that bothers me is people complaining about the authenticity of this joint. Maybe it's because I'm not a BBQ aficionado, or maybe it's because I realize I'm in Philadelphia and want to take this joint for what it is. The best options for order here are the "all-in" combos. You can chose one or two meats and also two sides per person. If you have a table of four or more, you can really go for it and get all of the meats and sides at $24 per person. We went with the brisket and spare ribs for meat. The brisket is great, moist, well cooked throughout. It comes in small slices to make your own sandwiches topped with onions, pickles, and BBQ sauce. The spare ribs are also great. They're also excellently cooked, dryer than the brisket. The skin is excellent, nicely charred with great flavor. Sides: Pinto beans were awesome. More like baked beans cooked with chunks of pork. The vegan chili would have been good if I wasn't comparing it to the pinto beans. The mac and cheese was creamy; nicely topped with breadcrumbs. Not nearly as good as baked mac and cheese made by the unbeatable Rashid-Kealey duo. The German potato salad was also impressive. All of the food ranges from good to excellent. I think it would be hard to make a bad choice. You get a lot of food here, I wish I would have had room for dessert. There are some pretty good choices, including a root-beer float with Yard's brew and homemade ice cream. Yum. Bottom Line: Percy St slow cooks some awesome meats. The highest temp in the oven is 250F. They are serious about serving up some of the best finger food in the city. There's enough options and the quality is high enough to warrant repeat visits. South St is starting to develop a serious food scene. I just wish the beer list was better.

When it gets crowded, I hate the set up--there's just no way to not feel like you're in someone's/everyone's way. The decor is really nice, and the bathrooms are cool, and so on. I actually really like the decor. I think it's just too difficult to navigate. There isn't much space to sit comfortably at the front bar with people walking in and out, and sitting at the back bar is just not really possible. The bartenders are nice (HOT) and the music is alright. I don't know. It's just average. If it weren't a gay bar, I'd never go back. And I give them credit for putting so much effort into it. Drinks are average price.
label: NEG

text: Good food. Indian in Bryn Mawr, yay! I had Malai Kofta, which didn't really seem to have much cheese for "cheese dumplings" but were nonetheless delicious. My girlfriend had mango chicken (on the special bryn mawr menu) and it was delicious as well. I've had better naan but this was perfectly acceptable. tamarind and mint chutneys served with it were good. decor is somewhat cheesy but that doesn't matter. service is just fine. lots of families with kids there when I went. They deliver! and there's no fee (according to the website) so a meal + tip is pretty much the same price whether you go to sit in or order delivery. Seeing as how I usually end up spending way more than I intend on delivery food I think I'll try this next time and get better quality food than pizza or bad chinese for probably a similar price. Also I definitely plan to go to the 9? dollar lunch buffet sometime!

text: The old Arbys has been transformed. It is now Chinese selling combo meals from as little as $5.99 to no more than $8.95. Cheap eats in sufficient quantity for a meal. No MSG. Free delivery in a limited area for a $10 minimum. The owners claim this is not just another Panda Express or "Americanized Chinese Food," but on my visit, it looked like standard Americanized Chinese food: Moo Goo Gai Pan; Orange Chicken; Sesame Pork; Mongolian Beef or Chicken; Fried Rice; Won Ton Soup; Egg Rolls and about 20 other predictable Americanized dishes. But if you stop and think, would we really eat authentic Chinese Food? Think, chicken heads and feet, fungus, dogs and cats. Yum yum! If you sold authentic Chinese food in the US, you'd be broke in a New York second. The only dishes that seemed that they might be authentic were the Keyone and Yazzyon Soups. I searched the net and no one has a record of such a soups, so they probably aren't Authentic Chinese. The "Y" soups are a pricy $7.50 per bowl. After tasting several of the dishes, this place earned only one star. The Mongolian Beef was horrible and a dish that I could not eat: spongy texture to the meat, and sickly sweet instead of spicy as promised. Two of the chicken dishes had better texture, but still too sweet and really lacking in flavor. The egg rolls were soggy, white steamed rice ok, shrimp fried rice was passible but bland. Too bad, no Brown Rice. Of six meals consumed, no one gave a rating better than two. I'm still a bit intrigued by the Y Soups, but afraid I'd be wasting my time and my money and still walk away hungry as I did when I left my Mongolian Beef. All in all, this is the second worst Asian food I've ever eaten. I'd rather have Panda Express any day. Or the Arbys it used to be. And I'm not a big fan of either.
label: NEG

text: Excellent day out, so much to do and see. Went on Sheikra firstwhy!! Didnt know what to expect, but couldnt wait to go on again. It is a very fast and exciting ride. They hold you for what feels like 5 mins above a vertical drop before pushing you off the top.Brilliant! Went straight back on and got on the front row.well worth it, very scary. Other rides very good too, but this was the best. Enjoyed the train ride through the animals, nice commentary all the way round. Bit of a long wait between trains though. Very long queue for Log flume, and as you cant take anything on the ride, one of our party fainted from the heat, so take a bottle of water and throw it away before getting on the ride. First Aid people were excellent though, very nice, polite and helpful.

text: This chicken was absolutely "The Best". The only thing better than the chicken was the service. They were extremely friendly, and and they know what they have, and are VERY PROUD of there chicken. The menu is very limited, which is a good thing. They have chicken, a chicken fried steak, and veal. Their sides are Red Beans, Butter Beans, Green Beans, and French Fries. Their cornbread was also outstanding. We all had the chicken, and my wife had the butter beans, and I had the red beans. They were both delicious. This place does not try to serve something for everyone, chinese, italian, etc. You want chicken this place cannot be beat. You want something else, go somewhere else. We got there about 15 minutes before they stopped serving, and got right in. They are open Mon-Sat from 11 to 3. Kerry came out of the kitchen and talked to us for about 10 or 15 minutes. That place is truely a family affair. She is in the kitchen, her younger brother and sister are waiting tables, and her 90+ year old grandfather was running around helping out with the tables. We had tried a couple of times before to get out there, but could not make it in time. Will definately schedule our time better to make it there. It is easy to win a James Beard Award when you are in a $2 or $3 million dollar resturant in the French Quarter, but try it in a whole in the wall that is off the beaten path. It is really funny to watch some of the regular customers watching you when you have never been there before. They really get a kick out of your expressions when you take the first bite.
label: POS

text: I have been here twice now, and after the second time I most certainly will not be back and I would not recommend this place to any foodie who enjoys their food, or any individual who enjoys being treated as a valued patron. My first experience over a year ago was pleasant, with pretty good food (an egg scramble) and I was pleased with the service. It was with these high expectactions that I returned to Culina only to leave bewildered as to what had happened. As a single diner I was sent to the bar while more than half the tables were empty and were never filled during my entire meal. It didn't bother me too much to sit at the bar. My tofu, quinoa scrambled hash, which took an extremely long time to arrive, was tasteless and looked like it had been scraped from the frying pan with a few errant spinach leaves tossed on top that were neither raw nor properly wilted. To add insult to injury, my waitress never came ask me if I was done, when it was clear that I was, I had to ask for the bill several times, and while I was sitting in front of her, she took the card machine to several other tables first and then rolled her eyes when she came back to me and sighed "here I am". One would think I had demanded for my bill when in fact I, very apologetically, asked with pleases and thank-you's if I could get my bill, even after the second time. There was no thank-you's when I was done and I left feeling like second-class citizen. As a foodie who has eaten at places from street food stands, to Michelin-starred restaurants, this might have been service I expected from a busy cafeteria, although the food would have been better. I can safely say that this was the worst meal I have ever had and I caution anyone from going to this establishment. I am saddened that it has degraded in such a manner, and hope that the owners take time to rectify these issues.
label: NEG

text: I have a soft spot in my heart for Lambert Airport. It's not the biggest or the best or the fastest, as many reviewers have noted, but in a whole year of flights (2009 - 2010), it hasn't let me down once. It's reliable, it's simple, and it gets me to where I need to be. One of the best things about the airport is how you can Metrolink right into it, which I've done countless times. It sure beats shelling out the $40 cab fare or expensive parking, especially on a student budget. The security lines are never all too long (although you might want to save a bit more time for the A gates, which always seem to take longer to get to). Dean's fantastic review mentions how Southwest is going to be the biggest airline operating out of STL in 2010, which really isn't so bad -- it means there are a bunch of direct flights opening up (e.g., to Boston, New Orleans, and more), which makes travel out of the airport even more painless. The worst thing about Lambert? The creepy food court. It's depressing just sitting there.
label: POS

On to the entrees, I got a seafood pasta dish which was okay until I found a chunk of beef in it. I don't eat beef, or any other red meat or chicken, at that. And dishes should never be cross-contaminated like that. I flagged down a waitress, and she wasn't sorry about it. She took it and later some manager type person came and asked me to tell him what was wrong. We ordered 2 appetizers the table side guacamole and the Seared Ahi Tuna...The tuna was "ok" and since I only had a mere dab of the guac I can't even rate it. The portion is for more like 2 people. I sent it back and choose not to order anything else. My mom ordered Grilled Crab Cakes that she too said had no flavor. My husband ordered lamb which he enjoyed and the others ordered steaks that were fine. No one ate any of the horrible carrots and we are all avid veggie eaters! text: All buffets are NOT created equal. If you're considering coming here, reconsider it, turn left, and walk about 300 feet until you're at the Eldorado buffet. The food here was average at best. The prime rib was woefully overcooked. The "rare" piece barely had any pink to it. WTF! Luckily, there were some edible items. The pesto mashed potatoes were tasty, and the oven roasted chicken was moist. As mentioned by another poster, however, the dessert bar is their saving grace. Many many many different types of cakes, pies, and pastries, trays of heated desserts like bread pudding and bananas foster, and a do-it-yourself ice cream machine. Disappointingly enough, they seem to have done away with the toppings bar and instead only have hot fudge. Tsk tsk. HOWEVER, keep in mind, people, that this is a buffet (i.e. creativity is highly rewarded!). So...I'll let you in on a little secret: vanilla ice cream + hot bananas foster = GET IN MAH BELLY! Since everyone knows I'm a dessert fiend, you should also be able to guess that is the sole reason for the added star. However, even in my eyes, this is not enough to redeem the entire buffet.

text: What a great little spot completely unlike anything else on the hill; we went here last Saturday night around 9:30 and easily grabbed seats at the bar. Think of an old house that's been converted into a bar; lots of nice wood accents and a comfortable feeling. They do have food but our gracious bartender pointed out all of the items that they were out of (almost half the menu by this time of night). Fortunately we didn't come for the food; I long ago learned from surrogate Italian grandmothers that the more you eat, the more you can drink. The Mermaid doesn't have the largest selection of beer but what they do serve hits the spot; excellent smattering of belgian beers like Duvel, Piraat, Lindemans, and Gulden Draak. Feels like a spot hit up by locals mostly but after a couple of strong Belgian beers your extroverted side surfaces. According to their calendar, musicians play here six nights a week (if not seven); think of the stage as one end of a large living room, not a concert hall. The Mermaid may not have precise acoustics but when I'm twenty feet from the performer and quaffing some tasty beers I couldn't really care. Great local spot with warm character and some great beer and music.

text: I took my dog to Bryn Mawr Vet Hospital three times. The first two visits went without a hitch. The third visit, however was a different story altogether. Dr. Cantner handled the visit, which should have been to give my dog several vaccinations. After the three shots and no examination to speak of, he mentioned he would like to perform some blood tests. Without explaining the details of the blood test, he took some blood from my dog. After 1 minute, I was told that the blood test showed my dog has no problem. The visit ended up costing $189. I was charged $37 for the 1-minute blood test. After checking around - I could have gotten the needed vaccinations for about half the price. If you go to Bryn Mawr Veterinary Hospital, be prepared to automatically pay an extra $50 just for bringing your pet for a standard examination fee. They don't actually examine your pet, this is basically a charge for simply stepping in the building. This place is seriously overpriced - however, to add insult to injury when I called to question the non-existant "examination" and corresponding charge both secretary and doctor were extremely rude and the doctor ended up hanging up on me. Go somewhere else where the prices are reasonable and the doctors competent. There are plenty of places around that care about customer service and your pet care, not only the final charge.

text: I've been in here twice, on both the first floor and the hidden 2nd floor that has it's own door on the street.
