text: I'm sorry to say, this place is very average at best and not worthy of the raving reviews on Yelp. I am from San Francisco and I have ate great sushi around the USA. This cannot be the best in St. Louis. Why am I giving this place the thumbs down you might ask??? Here's why.... - Sushi rice was a total dud. The person in back does not understand you need to add rice vinegar, a bit of sugar and salt. This was the most flavorless rice I have ever put in my mouth. Wake up St. Louis! Rice should not taste like rice when you eat great sushi. Get a Japanese "mama-san" in there to show you how to do it right. Also, make smaller rice under the fish....your out of alignment! Should be more fish and less rice. - Miso soup was the worst ever. Miso soup should be made with fresh white miso, bonito, some silken tofu, and sliced scallions and some seaweed. I have no idea what this was....it was a bowl of brown flavorless water with a few sliced mushrooms (not even japanese mushrooms!). Seriously, this was half hearted effort to make soup. - The fish was tasteless and not fresh IMO. They should torture their seafood supplier. How can you botch Unagi? Spicy scallop was spicy something. Tuna was AWOL for flavor. I bet most of their fish is frozen before they get it. Come on guys, quality is everything when your in the sushi business. - Sushi chefs looked like they were "doing time" and hated every minute on the job. I could not get any of these guys to crack a smile, even after wanted to buy them a round of beers/sake to make my night enjoyable. Part of going to a great sushi bar is interacting with the chefs. These guys need Viagra to get excited. - Waiter for some reason could not remember I ordered Sake. I had to beg for my Sake from three different people. Ended up going to the Dubliner Pub down the street for after sushi disaster drink. - The decor was dated, kinda cheesy, yet there was plenty of "cool cats" eating and drinking like it was a five star establishment. I took the bait as I walked up Washington and should ate at Mizu Sushi. They were not as busy, but I did stop in and it had a better vibe, nice space, and people that appeared to be interested in me as a customer. I will give them a try next time I am in town. Bottom line, this place is overrated and you should try somewhere else because the food is not cheap and the value is not there. I would strongly recommend scrutinizing the Yelp reviews and look for a out-of-town person to weigh in with an opinion. This out of towner says "thumbs down". May the force be with you all!!!

text: One consistency that I found during my limited stay in St. Petersburg was the atmosphere, design and overall relaxed atmospheres of the restaurants I visited. The other consistency had to do with food that was good on paper but sub-par in execution and flavor. This place attracted us immediately with it's outdoor patio and menu items but after a tapas sampler, we quickly decided to save some cash and head home to cook a dinner instead. We started with a pitcher of sangria to wind down a long weekend filled with biking and running. The sangria was rather juice-like so we decided to add a shot of tequila to it which evened it out a bit. I think this could be a great spot to go out to but in terms of enjoying well executed food, I am still on a mission in St. Pete.

text: University City has been in dire need of a salon like this! Upon first glance, I assumed it would be way over-priced, but it's actually extremely reasonable (35.00 for a women's haircut)! I rushed in after getting a terrible haircut, in desperate need of someone to fix it. Despite it being a Friday, I only had to wait ten minutes for a free stylist. Gretchen cut my hair and was absolutely amazing. I was literally in tears over my first haircut and instead of looking at me like I was crazy, Gretchen was incredibly understanding and helped me figure out a plan to fix it. With it's Supercuts-esque price, one would expect this salon to be all about the basics, but clients are completely pampered! While the conditioner set, I got a hand massage and once I got back to the salon chair, I was given tea. I cannot recommend this salon enough - everyone is really nice and are great stylists (everyone I saw walked out of there with gorgeous hair), the price cannot be beat and it's really convenient for anyone in the University City area.
label: POS

text: Don't know why restaurants with a high mediocrity quotient keep building more and bigger restaurants. And the more mediocre they are the longer the wait for a table? My god, they give you beepers so you can go to the mall or something while you wait. If they were cheap maybe it would make sense, but they're not. The food? You're not going to spit it out of your mouth, but you're not going to ask for the recipe either. Maybe its the service. The ingenuousness of "how are you guys? My name is Kim and I'll be takin care of ya tonight?" I admit is hard to beat, but don't they still have to get your food to you in some semblance of order? And when the server drops the check and five minutes later you are locked in a staring match with him until he finally comes to your table, looks you in the eye, follows your eyes down to the check and credit card sitting there and exclaims, "oh, of course, I'll get this processed for you right away". What a guy! Don't get me wrong, the people that plunk down millions on super prime real estate and build a stadium of a restaurant know exactly what they're doing because they are packin em in. So in fairness to them, its business business 10, hospitality business 2!

text: I must say that I love pizza. It is by far my favorite food. I'm not a pizza snob by any stretch of the imagination. Even chain pizza is still pizza. I can appreciate the many different ways you can make pizza. The pizza was more charred that I expected. I have had brick oven pizza many times and I would say they tend to leave it in longer than I would suggest. The pizza crust had a nice texture however. It was crisp and chewy. The crust was the best part. They didn't have pineapple. I wanted to try prosciutto ham and pineapple. However my wife and I went for the sausage and fennel with roasted red peppers. It was a nice combination. The prices are better than I expected for the review I got from a coworker. It sounded more gourmet that it really is. We snuck out of there with two chop salads, a pizza, and drinks for around $20 before tip. Service, by far is 5 stars. Our waitress never let our glasses bottom out. She was very nice and friendly. The bad news, Pizzology is in Carmel. That means I had to drive there. I think this place needs to be in the city of Indianapolis and not in a strip mall off of a roundabout. Bottom line, if I had to choose to drive to Carmel for Pizzology or walk Bazbeaux...I'd walk.

text: What's up with hotels in the King of Prussia area?! They all seem sub-standard, especially in comparison with similar hotels in other locales. The Crowne Plaza is no different. text: I have been to Hog Pit a few times and finally decided to write a review on it. I really want to like this place but it seems they just don't want to give me a reason to. We went on a busy night and sat on the patio. The patio was packed and they seemed very unprepared for the large crowd. Servers were confused and seemed lost. More than once I saw servers walking around with plates of food not sure where to deliver them. They had $1 beer specials advertised but, conveniently, they were "out" of the advertised special. Hmmm... On to the food... my wife and I had a late lunch and were not all that hungry so we decided to split one entree. We ordered the brisket plate and requested it be split, for which they charged $2. I, personally, don't have a problem with the charge as they brought us both our own plates which seemed to have full orders of fries. The brisket had a funny look to it when they set it on the table. It looks like a sponge that someone had taken a cheese grater to. The fat on it was visible. It did not look like they had bothered to trim it all... very unappealing. That being said, it tasted OK after cutting off the fat and squirting some of their Voodoo (the spiciest option) BBQ sauce on it. Like I said, I want to like this place. It's close to home and seems like it may be a cool place to hang out and play pool or poker as they have Texas Hold-Em on some nights. I will go back... if only to see if I can ever capitalize on that $1 beer special and maybe try a burger.
label: NEG

text: Been to this place several times over the past couple years and it's definitely lost it's luster. The last time I was there, the hostess was quite standoffish about seating us in the dining room, despite the fact that most of our party was ordering food and it was almost completely empty. The server was equally off-putting, with much sighing and eye rolling throughout the entire meal. It really ruined the night. If your dining room is open until 12 or 1 (hypothetically speaking; I don't know what their hours are), you shouldn't be upset about seating it at 9. Or at least tell us when it closes so we can leave by then. But no, they chose to sigh and stare at us the entire night. That trip aside, the food ranges from pretty good to outstanding and the selection of local brews gets a big thumbs up. The crowd seems to have definitely shifted to the older end of the spectrum. That's good for them, I suppose. All told, however, this place isn't as special as it used to be. There's plenty of other competition in the area now that is both cheaper and more welcoming (even Johnny Brenda's is preferable; at least rudeness there can be considered part of the schtick). I most likely will not be back.

text: La Salsa Rocks! If you haven't eaten at here yet, you are missing out on one of the best kept secrets in Tucson. My personal favorite is the California burrito. But! the nachos are the best I've ever eaten. The Baja fish tacos are absolutely superb and the Chipotle Shrimp Salad is divine. So many wonderful choices you'll need to return often to try them all! Highly recommended.

text: Excellent. My wife was told by an out of town associate about this place. We're new to Tucson and are still exploring. We went for an early dinner and found the place nearly empty. People soon started rolling in and the clientele was half white-boy, half "local"..... "By the people, for the people" is always a good sign, if you know what I mean. We ordered the large sashimi combo and a spicy tuna roll. The combo was just over twenty bucks and it was worth every penny. The cuts were large "two-biters". They even tossed on a little grilled albecore and some other chewy white fish that was very good - both not listed on the menu. My god, the salmon melted in our mouths. So creamy and fresh. The tuna was exquisite. We were really impressed with the quality and quantity of this combo platter. I'm a chili head, so when I see spicy "anything" I know that I'm gonna need some help to get things going. This was the first Spicy Tuna roll I've ever had that actually had a little kick. And at $4.50, it's a bargain! Of course I still smothered it with wasabe. Also, I hate it when you are eating a roll and the last thing to go down is a chewy seaweed wrapper. This roll had the most tender seaweed I've ever had. Virtually non-existent. The ginger was un-dyed and tasty. The green tea was good and refills-o-plenty. Service was good. The staff and chefs are super friendly as you enter, and as you leave. Cool place. Next time we'll sit at the bar and see if the chef treats us to any extra goodies. Can't wait to go back.
label: POS

text: I have eaten here twice for lunch and was very impressed. They offer a lunch menu with sushi deals, hibachi plates, and bento boxes. text: While some friends and I were visiting Philly we decided to go to Tinto for dinner. It's a fav spot by a friend of mine. We ordered quite a few things from the menu but it was great being able to taste everything. -serrano ham-wrapped figs(I'm not a big fan of the figs.. but this was pretty good) -mussels, chorrizo, frites, lemon aioli(these were okay) -scallops with bacon and shaved apple(these were awesomem, DEF order again) -octupus with potatoes (this was pretty tasty) -lump crab with scrambled eggs (I wouldn't order again) -bomba rice with mushroom, asparagus, lemon oil (This dish wasexcellent, I loved the flavors of the asaparagus, mushroom andlemon oil, DEF recommend) -wild mushrooms with roasted potatos, shallot, and parsley(I could have eaten the whole dish since the mushrooms were so flavorful, DEF recommend) -housemade garlic sausage with lentils(the sausage part was good.. but the flavor of the lentils just didn't fit well with the sausage) -rack of lamb (this was good but it was only 2 pieces for $24) -pork belly(this was delicious) -prawns(the sauce that this was cooked with was SO good, DEF Recommend) -verdosa salad (it was light and pretty fresh) -chocolate and coffee cake (the ganache really stood out for me and the mousse part too)

text: This place is located in Ybor City, but buried behinds many other things such as a community college, clubs, and Centro Ybor. Even so, the Spaghetti Warehouse may be one of the nicest places I have been too in a while. The interior is built with an old fashioned appeal, including a paper that talks about the disastrous Earthquake that hit San Francisco in 1989. There is an arcade on the side with a few games and the building is made of brick giving it a fancy look. The food is delicious and their Italian cuisine features variety and quality. The bread they bring you before you eat will delight you, as will the garlic butter that accompanies it. I had the Mushroom and Artichoke pasta (that is not what it was called) and was highly satisfied with my meal. The prices are especially low for dinner as well. Most meals come with soup or salad, similar to the Olive Garden, I had the salad with some thousand island sauce. It was delicious! The waiters are friendly and so are the customers who are eager to use and give away coupons to people they encounter while in the restaurant. We were encountered by about 4 different groups of people eating there that wanted to share their coupons.

text: I have to admit, I was pretty mixed on this place to start -- in some ways, I was psyched for the in-store PLCB, Garces-to-go, and yet another great source of baked goods. Yet, I'm not sure if I agree with PLCB choosing one "golden boy" to try the concept out with... but I figured I'd check it out. First, on the wine store -- didn't love the selection. There's not a huge amount of space, but I looked for some good Cali and South American wines and found almost nothing in that space. I'd say that I'm sure it'll get better with time, but it is state run. As I didn't actually buy anything, I'm going to hold this out of my overall scoring. As for the food, I ordered the Moroccan, described as "roasted lamb loin, roasted pepper, eggplant, harissa aioli, comté, escarole." Store was crowded so it took maybe 10-15 minutes for my sandwich to be ready. Quickly ran home to keep the sammie hot, and dug in. What I expected: smokey, a little bit of heat from the harissa, and a powerful punch of flavor. What I got: surprisingly...well...bland. There was just nothing that stuck out for me, except some oddly placed whole chickpeas. Now I don't know about most people, but whole chick peas are not something I typically enjoy in meat sandwiches. But was this sandwich really that different from roast beef and russian on a french bread? Not really. I will say service is friendly (albeit manic) and the place is beautiful. Jose, I love your stuff, but my not-cheap sandwich just didn't meet up to your typical boldness nor it's Moroccan name.

A good double shot of espresso needs to be at least 25 seconds and less than 30. So thank you, Indigo, for watery wannabe starbucks slightly espresso flavored water. text: All 8 of us went in super eager to show our friend a great birthday last night, a Thursday evening, catch some happy hr specials & listen to great jazz. Unfortunately for us, the management ruined almost every single positive thing I could have said about this place. So let me start with this one positive nugget: the jazz was Great! A friend ordered 2 shots of Jameson (their advertised 2.50 all the time special) for our friend's birthday & the waitress informed us they ran out of jameson but they have X brand instead. Ok, fine, it's a lesser whiskey we dont normally drink, but for $2.50 we didnt mind so we agree to the substitute. We had some good food & were enjoying beers as well. A while later another 2 shots were ordered for the birthday, same substitute whiskey. Meanwhile our waitress informed us they ran out of a few things, and one beer on the menu had never been on tap there, ever. After a while it came time to order another birthday shot (btw this was not a 21st sloppy bday, we are all professionals, altho we were having fun there was no unbecoming behavior) and the waitress let us know we had "killed the bottle" of substitute whiskey. Okay... are there any other whiskey shot specials? No. Okay... well 2 soco & lime shots then please. Well, we ran out of SoCo. Okay... what DO you have? The waitress went up to the bar & came back to let us know, just as a suggestion, they have... tequila. This process took a while during which the birthday person decided, altho the jazz is lovely, it's my birthday & I want to go to another place nearby. So we asked for our check & were suprised to see they had charged us $6 each for the 6 whiskey shots we ordered, and $1.50 extra for 2 of the beers than the price listed on the menu. $3 extra for beer was negligible, but I quietly asked the waitress about the shots, since she had said the cheaper whiskey was a substitute. She was super nice & told me she was sorry she didnt realize it was more but she could comp half the shots to make up for it. But then a minute later she returned- she had checked with her manager & wasnt allowed to comp the shots afterall, sorry. While I was talking with her, someone else realized the included gratuity was 25%... We are 20% tippers for pretty much all manner of service and I have no problem with pre-set gratuity for a large party of 8- but to see 25% is unheard of. Even the fanciest of fancy places charges 18% for a group. So we asked for the manager & he came to our table. After a seriously disgusting exchange, which included him berating us for thinking whiskey such as we had would not be $6 a shot & telling us we were wrong about what beers were shown on the menu and at what price, altho we had a menu in our hands, etc, the whole time with a face that told us he was completely disgusted by our clearly great math skills, and which caused all 8 of us at the table to determine individually in our heads that we were never going to set foot in the place again, he agreed to fix the 25% gratuity. He took our bill back to the register, where 4 employees stood around him trying to figure out how to change the gratuity. (Has anyone else every checked their bill there, or is it always set so high, thinking noone would bother to check?) Anyway, when he came back & chucked the check onto the table, the gratuity was reduced & the 2 beers they had overcharged for were completely comped, which almost made up for the $6 shots. Thank you. As we spilled onto the sidewalk through the trip hazard door, one of the group mentioned they would not be coming back due to the insanely rude experience, and low and behold the young manager was out there smoking & overheard. He actually yelled at our group as we walked away... "Next time, go someplace you can afford!" I wish I was making that up. No one (businesses or customers) is in a great financial situation right now, but even in these hard economic times I am not one to complain about 1-2 "mislabled" overpriced beers or if they charged the extra 5% because of the live music, I would have said, fine, cool! If the waitress had told us the "substitute shots" werent at the "specials" price, we would have gotten something tastier for $6 instead. Or if she could have just comped the drinks like she first offered, we would have been done. If only 1 or 2 of those things had happened, we could look past the monetary issues in honor of a friends birthday, world peace & maintaining the tranquility of the holiday season. But altogether it created a terrible experience, in which we felt taken advantage of & then berated when we called them on it. In addition please be aware if you're biking that there is no place to park your bike anywhere on this block. Also, the ladies bathroom does not flush properly. If you go, go for the jazz and I sincerely suggest checking out your bill at the end of the night. The end.
label: NEG

text: Lets start off with the negatives of Romanza Ristorante.....*30min later*...OK well I couldn't think of any bad things to say. My last visit was March 26th, so lets get to the food. First off I always stay at the Peppermill Hotel and Casino, its one of the better Hotels I think in Reno. You cant go wrong in any of their restaurants. I have almost tried them all but still love Romanza. We always make it a point to go to the small quaint Romanza bar which overlooks the casino floor and most of the dinning area. We always have a bottle or 2 of Banfi Chianti Classico Riserva from Tuscana 2003. This time around we decided to try the food so we made reservations as recommended. We started off with the Beef Tenderloin Carpaccio. The carpaccio was like butter, it barely touched your tongue and it melted away down your throat. I then had the minestrone soup, which wasn't that spectacular, maybe should have went with a salad. For my entree I had the Chicken Parmigiana with Pene Pasta. THIS WAS AN ABSOLUTE WINNER! Best Chicken Parm I have ever had. The size of this chicken was huge! Me and my friend could not stop joking on the size of the bird. It was bigger then a turkey breast. It was just fabulous, beautifully breaded with a slight crunch in every bight. The cheese was gooey but yet crispy on top. The chicken moist and flavorful. It was to die for, and I think I would have died if I tried to eat the whole thing. I couldn't even finish a quarter of the meal and had to box up the rest. But the next day it made for great lunch. To finish we ordered some dessert "to go" of course. Rocky our waiter convinced me to have the White Chocolate Cassata Dome. The best way I can describe this was a spongy fruit cake with white chocolate and fresh raspberries. It was a delicate finisher to the meal. I will surely come back to Romanza. You will meet the friendliest staff around. From the bus boy to the highest manager. If you have the pleasure to visit when Rocky is serving by all means request his tables. If you get to be at the bar and happen to run into Mike, you will not regret your visit, very cheerful, lively and always has great conversation.

text: I am vegan and have been to many vegan friendly establishments, this place is so sterile and uncomfortable to be in! They are buying everything from Vegan Treats, a well known bakery in Bethlehem, PA where many restaurants in Philadelphia source their desserts. They source everything from this place, its seems so bizarre! 4 brownies in a row, next to 4 different brownies in a row, nothing is touching, it doesn't look like the items are real. I once asked if one of the cinnamon buns had "cream cheese" frosting and the lady behind the counter said, "yea but its vegan" as if that was a BAD thing!! The only reason I went in the place was because I am a vegan. Today, I went in to see a tray of entirely WHOLE FOODS BAKERY goods. I work in the bakery at the Callowhill store and these items cannot be confused. I should have asked how much these items were going for and if they kept them overnight (because Whole Foods does not). I was shocked. The atmosphere is quiet and uncomfortable, it doesn't smell like baked goods, or coffee for that matter and everything is a hodge podge of different designs. Their website makes them out to be a much more exciting and diverse bakery than they actually are, I was under the impression that they were baking all of these cakes to order, but they are just getting them from Vegan Treats. Anyone can do that! These items are not a good reflection of vegan "baked goods" they are high in fat, sugar and are 2-3 serving sizes each.

text: US Post Office - Creve Coeur and the Main, Downtown St. Louis office. Ever have a problem with the US Post Office? What results did you get? Better than mine, I hope. It costs $5.54 rather than 44¢ to mail one. That's more than 12 times the rate of a first class stamp! I mailed a VERY IMPORTANT letter this way on March 31st. It has legal and high monetary implications, and was time sensitive. It NEVER got delivered. It NEVER got returned to me! (I had an slightly incorrect address, although I had the same incorrect address over a month earlier, and it did get delivered. It was the correct post office and zip code. NO Return receipt was sent to me.) NO ONE returned my calls at first. Customer Service didn't, the manager of the Creve Coeur Post Office didn't, the Postmaster General of St. Louis's Office didn't either. FINALLY, the manager of the Creve Coeur Post Office (after he had been conference called with me on Monday, the 12th) called late afternoon to confirm the letter was NOT DELIVERED and he DIDN'T HAVE A CLUE where it was! I asked who's responsibility it was and he replied. "I don't know." WOW! Don't lawyers and accountants suggest we mail important documents this way? In private industry, a customer service person who knows customer service and cares about customers, would have sent a courier to my house immediately to pick up and hand deliver the important document. Finally, after another call, they did pick up the letter, and, lo-and-behold! - Delivered it the same day. (I received the signed, return receipt card the next day, inside an envelope from the Creve Coeur Post Office. It's a shame it wasn't done correctly the first time.

They even have a 55 gallon drum of olive oil in the middle of the shop with a pump handle on top for bottle refilling! Beyond the gee whiz factor of this, it's simply the best oil I've ever tasted. At $20 for 750ml, its an absolute steal. Equally great is the cheese shop next door, whose name currently, embarrassingly escapes me. The lady that runs it has a wonderful palate and is an absolute cheese expert. The several Dutch and French cheeses I bought there were an absolute delight. She, Vitellos and the like exist at TFM as much to share their love and passion for their specialties as for commercial endeavor. But they're in Lawrence, so their pricing elasticity is "Trentonish" - as opposed to what they'd get away with if they trekked 5 miles north to Princeton. Stay put, Trenton Farmers Market - we like you just the way you are.

They serve it rustic style, meaning bigger potatoes and bigger slabs of bacon, with huge hunks of fat on them as opposed to the more traditional cubed lardons. I tend to lean more towards the traditional cubed and crisped lardons but hey, it's still bacon, and hey, I guess that's why they call it the breakfast salad instead of Salad Lyonnaise. Anyway, long story short; it was good but not great and certainly not one of the better ones I've had in the city. The white flat bread pizza was just...awful. Not only did it lack flavor but it was so dried out and hard as a rock. It tasted like it had sat out for hours, been heated, sat out again and the re-heated, and then served to my mother. My poor mom, I'm always excited to bring her to these places I hear great things about and she always ends up with the worst dish. Anyways, I wouldn't recommend it...at all. The passion fruit Italian soda I had was good but I probably should have ordered black cherry since I like the flavor better. Coffee was barely lukewarm. Our server was kind enough to heat it up for my mom. The decaf is not so great but the Sumatra had a good rich flavor. The Cookie: When I went to pay at the register I noticed some naughty looking cookies nearby. I spotted a big old peanut butter cookie with the mashed fork impressions in it and I immediately bought one and brought it back to the table. Christ, what a dick tease. That cookie tasted nothing like a peanut butter cookie. It tasted more like a cross between a snickerdoodle and a sugar cookie. blah. I dunno...maybe it wasn't peanut buttter flavored...? If it wasn't then it should be illegal to put those crossed fork impressions in them! I'm going to give this place a few more tries. It had to have been a fluke. But until then this cat gets 2 stars.

text: I have been here once before but the company I was with ruined my visit forcing me to put a hault on my meat fest. 3 years later, I am ready to take my meatatarian boyfriend for his birthday. As we entered, 15 minutes late due to traffic and parking, 5 staff members gave us a wonderful welcome and seated us immediately. My boyfriend is not one to be crammed into a corner which happens often when 2 people dine out. This was not the case at Fogo de Chao. The waitress gave us a nice run down of what to do and what to expect. We hit the wonderful salad bar. If you are a basil fan you must try their basil dressing (it is bright green). This went well over spinach and tomato salad. There was and apple and raisin salad that was also delicious but hey, we are here to talk about the meat, right? On for the meat olympics as we called it. It does seem like they bring out the lesser quality meats first, which is still quite tasty. I must say I know most people come for the beef but do not pass on the chicken legs!!! The manager informed us they were soaked in cognac and beer!!!! AWESOME!!! The sirloin and rib eye was THE BEST we ever had! Grab a crispy end piece.. it is still nice and dark pink on the inside. PERFECT!!!! The waitstaff was wonderful. The food just keeps coming. Do not forget to stop for a breather.We wondered why we waited so long for our check and to our surprise they came out with a slice of chocolate cake for my boyfriends birthday (which he mentioned briefly on the phone so we could get an early reservation). And somehow we managed to eat every last morsel of the cake, which was also very rich and delicious! We thanked the staff and praised them for one of the best dining expeiences ever. It is expensive. $150 for 2 dinners, iced tea and a mojito plus tip (tip them well, they desrve it) is a lot for two people on teacher's salaries but WELL WORTH IT!!!!

What little there was mostly consisted of overcooked carrot slices. This is were the Mint chutney came in. Our entrees are what inspired the one star rating. I had Paneer Makhni and my boyfriend had the Paneer Mutter. Both were astoundingly bland. Until this dinner I could not have imagined bland Indian food. Indian food is so much about spices and aromas but our dishes had no flavor at all. I did not even taste salt in my Paneer Makhni. The garlic naan was also sub-par. The garlic was bland too! It must have come from a jar of pre-minced cloves. We are both vegetarians, so perhaps the 5 star reviews I see reflect Taj Mahal's meat dishes. But if an Indian restaurant can't do good vegetarian, I have a hard time believing any of their food is very good. If your hungry for Indian in Boise go to Madhuban.

text: The Arch is quite an experience. It just looks kinda cool from afar, but when you get up close it's really impressive. You just don't see the magnitude until you're at the base. A warning: the tram you ride up in is very small and a bit rickety. Once you get to the top, though, the ride is worth it. The St. Louis skyline itself itsn't all that exciting to look at (unless you've lived there & know what all the buildings are) nor is East St. Louis, but it's just cool to be 630 feet up in the air looking down at everything. One time I went up in the Arch, it had snowed outside so everything was covered in white - it was quite pretty. The most recent time I went up, it was a very clear day with blue skies and we had a great aerial view of the brand-new Busch Stadium. The museum underneath the Arch is kind of neat, and it's free, so check it out while you're there. You can also get tickets to a movie about the Arch construction and for a riverboat ride down the Mississippi, but I haven't experienced either of those attractions yet. If you're visiting St. Louis, the Arch should be on your agenda. You won't forget it.

text: So, I like to think of myself as a pretty tough cookie. Well, that cookie crumbled when I came and found my two-year old Papillion, Dexter, whimpering with a limp. We rushed over on Tuesday at around 3pm and were seen almost immediately. The folks at the registration desk were really friendly and reassuring, as I reluctantly sent my little guy to the back to be looked at it. Eventually, they called me into the room, asked a few questions and proceeded to do an exam. Dexter was seen by Dr.Hume who was AMAZING! He was very friendly and took the time to explain Dexter's injury (luxating patella and general lameness). Instead of immediately jumping to sedating him and taking tons of xrays, Dr. Hume recommended a course of at-home treatment that included two prescriptions and lots of rest. We were out in about an hour and half and the entire visit including the meds came to $130 which i thought was really reasonable considering the emergency nature of the visit. The treatment worked and Dexter was, as good as, new in a few days. The absolute best part: Dr. Hume called two days later just to check on him.

text: A friend came in town and wanted to try Edmounds restaurant. It was a Tuesday night around 8 pm when we arrived. No one was was manning the host/ess stand, but a guy came around fairly quickly to seat us. It was not crowded. We had our pick of tables. My friend picked a bottle of wine for us which they were out of...bummer, but ok, we chose another. Our waitress was nice and patient as we were much more concerned with catching up than ordering. When we finally got around to ordering, we started with the calamari. It was very disappointing. I love calamari and only ate 2 pieces. There was no sense of the yummy flavor of the squid and it was incredibly dry. I don't necessarily need dipping sauce, but their's left much to be desired with little flavor and little to go around. My friend and I both went with the ribeye as the restaurant specializes in steaks. Our mouths salivating for the marbled, seared, goodness of a good ribeye. We also ordered two sides as the steaks are a la carte. We took the mac-n-cheese and roasted wild mushrooms. The steaks also come with several dipping sauces that you can choose from. Just for kicks we got the blue cheese fondue and the garlic puree. The steaks arrived looking pretty sad. I ordered mine medium rare hoping for that good sear that leaves the crunchy bits...not so much. My steak was grey with grill lines. It clearly had been put a cool grill and did not have the sear or much marbling to boot. I was very sad! My friend felt much the same about his steak. Very disappointed, although the steaks were cooked to our specifications. On to the sides, the sadness continues! The mac-n-cheese was sub-par. It looked good, but it was just mac and cheese. No cheesy, creamy, gooey goodness. I ended up pouring the blue cheese fondue dipping sauce over it and it enjoyed it much more! The mushrooms were just roasted mushrooms with whole garlic. The only thing I can say in bland. I would say that pretty much describes the meal....bland and very disappointing. Our server did bring out a small amount of all of their sauces which was really nice. After testing all of them, the blue cheese fondue is the only one worth trying. The garlic puree was cold, their steak sauce was too much and the black pepper was definitely lots of black pepper and very overpowering. The last very disappointed thing was that our server never clued in. We literally ate maybe 6 pieces of the calamari. The plate was still full and she didn't ask if there was a problem. Most of our steaks and sides were left as well. I was not paying for dinner so I didn't say anything. If I would have been, I definitely would have commented. So, I say f15teen is miss. I won't be going back and my friend agrees. I'm sure there are bright spots, but I think I'll spend my money elsewhere....

Before our apps we were treated to a couple hot biscuits with butter and honey. Our main entrees were spectacular. I had the bison (filet) with forked mash potatoes and swiss chard. My wife had the hanger steak with baked sweet potatoes and braised scallions. All I can say is this hanger steak was out of this world and my mouth is watering as I sit here writing. So flavorful and melt in your mouth tender. For desert we split the chocolate hazelnut cake with strawberry compote and vanilla bean sauce. I'll say this was definitely tasty, but the desert we had before was better (more on that latter). Overall, Maize delivers great american style food in a cozy BYOB restaurant atmosphere. With two apps, two entrees, and dessert our dinner with tip came to just under a hundred dollars. We also did not have to fight traffic, pay tolls, or pay for parking to enjoy a fantastic dinner. Last time out we went with friends and all had the corn tasting menu they were having for a few days in July. First course was snapper with a corn salad, second course hanger steak with a corn fritter and potatoes, and dessert was a corn infused bread pudding with raspberry sorbet and fresh fruit. We all loved our dinners from start to finish, including sampling their in house made root beer.

Only other bright spot would have been the Muffaleta sandwich. I had high hopes for the Cuban and the Portabello but they were nothing special. The "crab cakes" seemed to be a highlighted item on the menu so we ordered a couple of those too. These were cream cheese and blue crab meat inside of a tiny tart style pastry. The consistency inside was similar to a quiche, very little crab (or even flavor of crab), and the pastry was a letdown. The remoulade that it came with was actually pretty good and could have improved the dish, but there was barely a drizzle used as a dressing on the small salad on the plate much less any to use on the crab concoction. Lobster bisque was virtually inedible. Far too heavy a hand with the cream, and a bit more tomato would have balanced it out a bit more. The stock was simply overwhelming everything. Pricing seemed out of proportion with the quality of offerings, and the college crowd they're likely to see the most of. I'd gladly pay $9 for any of the options we tried *if* the quality was there. It's a shame really as it's a pretty hip space. Now, if you're looking for a alternative to a starbucks and just want some coffee, a pastry, and a place to hang then I'd say go for it. And they stay open late so if you're out on the town and had a bit to drink then maybe not a bad option. But as a eating destination.....?

text: My experience at Cooperage was solidly 3 stars, maybe even 3.5, until the very end. We'll start with the good stuff - great decor, good crowd and great sips specials. $2 Stellas and more than decent appetizers offered at half price. Though I must say that the wings, though large and meaty, were a little gooey-er than I like and the sauce could have had a bit more of a kick to it. The pork nachos were definitely a big hit at our table. Now, I hate to bring down a review based purely on one server, but this was so over-the-top that it can't be avoided. Our server made two critical errors - first, when I communicated to him that one of the bathrooms was experiencing a problem (toilet was clogged) he shrugged and said "well, did it have an 'out of service' sign on it?" - obviously not or no one on my party would have attempted to use the bathroom. After a few moments of confusion, I repeated my statement, to which he then replied along the lines of "oh, well I'll tell whoever is in charge about that". Ohhh-K. This guy definitely had a "don't look at me" attitude. Secondly, one of our party asked for a separate bill, which he received, paid and left. When we got our bill, the waiter delivered it and said "your friend was an awful tipper". We were confused for a second, and then immediately jumped to apologize and asked what happened. The waiter then said "he left $2 on a $15 bill". Now, I start at 20% and work up or down depending, but most people consider that excessive, and start with 10% - 15% and work up or down. $2 is 13% on a $15 bill. Not to mention that we had to flag down this server for the majority of our needs and once he got an order from one person, left before asking the rest of the table - causing us to call out after him to complete the round. Regardless of how bad you think our friend tipped - don't complain about it to us - at most, ask us if we were happy with the service and our experience and let us infer from there! Barring the service issues - we enjoyed our time at Cooperage and I won't hesitate to give it another try, with the hope that the service steps up.

text: We weren't all that impressed with our first experience here; while the place is gorgeous in an urban rustic way, the food seemed a little too salty and not worth the money. Believe it or not, for a restaurant that's all about cured meats, the kitchen is actually vegan-friendly. My husband and I are both vegan, and we've gotten comfortable just showing up and asking the waiter to bring us something vegan -- what arrives is always fantastic. The bar is deserving of a great rating all on its own. Word is that when Robert Plant was living in the neighborhood while working with Alison Krauss, he was sometimes seen at this bar. It's a bit cramped and they don't have every imaginable drink, but they specialize in a menu of stylish cocktails. Of course, having tried several, I haven't found any that I love. Still, it's fun to experiment, and if you're not in the mood for cocktails, they have a great wine list. And while the bar menu, with inventive hors d'oeuvres, is considerably less suitable for vegans than the dinner menu, we've heard from friends that it's nearly as good. All in all, while there may be a dish or two on the menu that won't please your palate for whatever reason, the overall experience is so good and the food in general so incredible it's definitely worth trying again.

text: I was excited for this BBQ meal and the stage was perfectly set, but it just didn't deliver. The atmosphere is great and all of the little details like decor, beer glasses, and paper towels strapped to the table are great fun, but when it comes to the eating experience (not the food itself) you can't help but feel letdown. A roll of paper towels will be strapped to your table, which reaffirms your feeling that this is going to be some serious BBQ, however, the signature BBQ sauce (which is DELICIOUS by the way) comes in a small container and is placed on the table. I would've preferred a heap of messy BBQ sauce all over my food! This is PLAIN Texas style BBQ (which I get) but I was disappointed that I didn't have to use one napkin! Not one! and there wasn't enough BBQ sauce to go around. Sure I could've asked for more, but at a BBQ joint you should never run out of sauce! Another problem is the lack of appetizer options. There are NONE. Nothing comes out before your main dish. Not even worth noting, there were two small pieces of bread, but the overall portions were so small that my dining mate ate both slices! Overall, I wouldn't have been so disappointed had it not been for the bill. Appetizers are not available so the bill for just two drinks and the BBQ meal was outrageous. Particularly the prices on the sides need to come down dramatically. Not to mention that it was great for the atmosphere when the food arrived wrapped in paper, but for this type of "feel" the price should match! The waiters and waitresses are wearing Percy Street tee shirts not black tie! I think that this restaurant can be great if it would just let it's hair down a bit and rethink it's prices. If this doesn't happen I don't expect it to last very long at all. Worth noting: desserts are pretty good (minus a dry chocolate chip cake although the icing more than made up for the dryness), service was excellent. Our waiter was Jake and he was very knowledgable.

text: El Rey in Spanish means The King. In this case, its the King of Overhype or the King of Crap. Take your pick. I went in here last night around 7. I was immediately greeted by three lovely hostesses. There were no tables available, so I took a seat at the bar. There was my first mistake. Some jackass failed miserably to account for leg space. I had to sit crossways just to friggin fit in. And my right knee still touched the edge of the bar. It was uncomfortable, to say the least. Yes the decor was nice. Although it seemed like someone watched "Stand and Deliver" one too many times. It was like eating in a Hollywood set of what a Mexican cantina should be. I kept expecting Edward James Olmos to come out and eat at one of the tables. I ordered Enchiladas Verdes with chicken and mushroom quesadilla. I'll preface this next part by saying I've actually cooked enchiladas verdes from scratch so I know how it should taste. The verdes sauce was weak and had absolutely no zip to it. I couldn't taste any onion or garlic and the tomatillo sauce tasted old(I"m guessing they made it up way earlier or from canned tomatillos, though to be fair I didn't taste the telltale aluminum/can taste in the tomatillos). The tortilla used in the enchiladas was dry, and the chicken was eh. Not only that but they were small. The enchiladas fit crosswise on a long serving plate instead of lengthwise like most normal Mexican restuarants. The mushroom quesadilla was a little better. The filling had some tasty mushrooms and corn in it. However, they surrounded it by a overly baked/grilled and dry tortilla which made it seem like I was eating toast. They had some avocado chunks mixed with cilantro and lime. While I like all three, the lime overpowered the cilantro and the avocado. I left feeling like I"d been suckered. I was feeling like it was a 2 star(r) review until this morning. I was forcibly entered into the El Rey Memorial Run 2 times so far. Thanks for the memories. The only way I'd go back is if it was for drinks at a table. There were plenty of hot women there. But I wouldn't eat there and I wouldn't go back to the bar.

text: I've spent my life in San Diego, one of those scenic, picturesque photo magnet/postcard sorta places, and I still have no problem finding beauty in my city's landscapes. That said, Butterfly Beach is kinda ridiculously gorgeous. Also, take the bike route south from the wharf, and when you come around the cemetery and see the hill, keep going - my girl and I went this way not exactly sure if the bike path was going to lead to the beach, and the site of a hill for an out of shape guy like myself on a bike too low to the ground was enough to get me to turn around. We used up the focaccia before all of the sauce was gone, so I used the bread from the bread basket to sop up the last bit left on the plate. I couldn't resist. Next we split a Capri Salad which was several different types of locally grown heirloom tomatoes and mozzarella made in-house, topped with a smattering of crispy fried onions. A very nice, light dish for our hot summer evenings. For entrees, my friend ordered the Chicken Milanese and I ordered the Bistecca. The chicken was served with a lemon sauce on polenta, and was bursting with flavor. The polenta was so creamy and delicious! The Bistecca had so many incredible flavors and textures-- the steaks were topped with fresh corn, tomatoes, breadcrumbs, mushrooms and served over pototoes. text: Five of us went to Ristorante Panorama for a friend's birthday last night. Upon entering the restaurant via a small hotel lobby, you notice two seating sections both of about equal size. The area directly ahead is a bit stuffy, and was very quite, to the right was a bar area that was a little more dimly lit, and was a little more lively atmosphere, thankfully this is where we were seated. After being seated, it took a few mins for our server to come to our table, but we were given a free round of prosecco for my friends birthday which I was surprised by. After looking at the drink menu we decided to go with different wine flights. While these seem like a great idea, each flight is only about a glass and a half of wine total, so if you plan on drinking more than that, just split a bottle (wine flights are all around $20). It happened to be restaurant week and to my liking they did not have a special menu with pre fixe items; they had an app, entree, and dessert from the regular menu for $35 special which was pretty decent. Everyone enjoyed their apps, with the lobster tortellini and the escargot being a bit disappointing, and the pasta sampler being the best, the gnocchi and ravioli on it were awesome. The entrees were all good also, I was hoping they had sea bass on the menu after reading other Yelp reviews, but that wasn't the case. The star of the entrees was the Vitello Mandolese, but let be serious, you can't go wrong with veal, prosciutto, buffalo mozzarella and truffle sauce. I was happy to see tiramisu on the dessert menu, and it is one of the best tiramisu that I have ever had. The lady fingers were saturated in coffee, which was perfect after just drinking an espresso. The other desserts were nothing to write home about. Towards the end of the meal, everyone was very happy, and the discussions were all along the lines of "we should take your mom here for dinner next time she visits". If you are looking for a nice meal, that is a bit on the fancy side, Ristorante Panorama would be a great choice.

text: Coming to the Scholarly Tap Room is always a special treat for me. Even while living in St. Louis, it was always a treat. I can't think of a better spot for delicious local brews, live music and a feel-good casual atmosphere. Food: You must try the Warmed German Camembert Cheese Plate. For real. The menu description reads 'glazed with brown sugar and walnuts and served with caramelized pears, dates, roasted garlic and John Dough bread'. As in WARM Camembert cheese doused with all of that aforementioned good stuff. Yep, I'll keep going. Next stop: the Fish & Fries. As others have mentioned, the Tap Room produces some of the best fish and chips I've ever had. I wasn't even able to find a better version in Southie, Boston. Again, I'm not messing around. Dessert-- believe the hype, the Sticky Toffee Pudding and the Bread Pudding are legitimate forces of awesomeness. Save some room, or at least sit long enough with your beer until you can stomach some pudding. And for the piece de resistance, the beer! Wow. So the Hefeweizen and the Pale Ale are great staples. Seasonally-speaking, summer's my fave because Schlafly then brews their Weissbier and Witbier. The Weissbier is brewed in the classic Bavarian-style, unfiltered with hints of banana and cloves. The Witbier also tastes all-summer, containing subtle notes of orange peel and coriander. I had a pint of each this past weekend and am still replaying their goodness. You can also purchase their beer in kegs or growlers to bring back a bit of beer bliss to your own home. Minus one star for the sometimes gruff service. If the service was consistently better, the Schlafly Tap Room would be a surefire five-star establishment in my book.

text: Ok look. I come from a small town in New Jersey where everyone knows everyone else. Back at home I run into the doctor that delivered me in the hospital 25 years ago. Now that I'm on my own in a big city, I can't go running home every time that I need my doctor. Why did I choose Jefferson Family? Maybe it was the word "family" that did it for me. I'm not really sure what I expected from this practice, but it definitely was not my cup of tea. When it came time to choose a PCP for my health insurance, I tried to do some research to find one of the doctors with better reviews and a better rapport. My first visit resulted in my doctor sending me to have bloodwork done and after waiting around for her to see me from a room full of close to 100 other people and tech's shouting names from random corners and "zones" and then later sending me down to a phlebotomist, wasted a good 5 hours of my day to later be told that the bloodwork didn't show anything that would indicate what I thought might be the problem with me. Now here's a novel idea, if I give you some symptoms and the bloodwork is inconclusive, why don't you help me look into it further? I mean, you're the one that went to school for this, I'm the one paying you! My second trip to Jefferson Family was because of a urinary tract infection (sorry for being graphic, but I'm clearly not reserved). I wasn't able to get an appointment with my doctor, but was scheduled with someone else instead. Clearly she was forgettable as I have no recollection of her name, but she looked like she was only a few years older than myself and like she had no idea what she was doing. She told me that the sample that I gave her showed no indication of an infection and after both her and her Jefferson Med School shadow checked me out, sent me on my way feeling like a complete idiot for wasting all of our time. When the symptoms only worsened it was now Saturday and I was unable to get an appointment at the hospital. I dragged my poor fiance with me to the women's wellness clinic or "planned parenthood" (imagine what was going on in his head)...not only did the clinician tell me that there were no indicators in my sample of an infection, but they charged me $20 for some B.S. 3-day supply of antibiotics as well as a $40 copay for being a specialist. Believe me, there's nothing special about visiting planned parenthood. Now, clearly I'm not buying what these "doctors" are selling...and I can't say that they implied that I was making it all up just to get another copay out of me, but with all of that the only saving grace was ultimately finding the practice that I now call "home". After a $35 copay to Rittenhouse Internal, I was told that not only did I have a urinary tract infection, but that it was halfway spread to my kidneys as my back was in so much pain that I could barely walk. So let's re-cap... $35 copay to Jeff for a failed doctor and med student. $40 copay to Planned Parenthood for a failed clinician. $20 copay for a bullshit prescription from PP $35 copay to Rittenhouse Internal for a proper diagnosis. Grand Total: $130 (I work at a non-profit, imagine how much those copays hurt me) Finding My Awesome New Doctor: Priceless (errr $35...whatever)

text: The first time I came here, I felt like it was not worth the price. But when they offered a Groupon and I was feeling mighty tense, I decided to pay a visit for a massage. Even at a deep discount, this place is not worth it. You can do much better. I arrived early to enjoy the sauna and whirlpool. There was a man who was swimming laps and grunting and being generally strange (not the spa's fault), but it didn't prevent me from quickly feeling relaxed after a very stressful few weeks. However, when I decided to sit by the pool and read a magazine, the only magazine I could find that wasn't a Visit Philadelphia brochure or a bridal magazine was from April (it's DECEMBER). To make matters worse, the only article I was interested in reading had been torn out of the magazine. So just to recap, the magazine was from April, and it was missing lots of pages. Sure, no big deal, but I think it would be nice of the staff to update their collection once in a while. This is a luxury spa at a top hotel, not a doctor's office. They can do better. There was no water in the girls' locker room when I arrived, and an hour later when I was going into my massage, there was still none. I mentioned this to the receptionist who said she'd take care of it. She told me I could find more water in the waiting area, except that pitcher was dry as well! She went to refill it, but instead of "ice lemon water," as they say you'll get on the website, I got room temperature water out of the water cooler. No ice, no lemon. Again, this is a luxury spa in a top notch hotel. If you're paying top dollar, they really should at least give you some nicer products. The massage itself was decent. I'm still a little tense, but that might be more personal and not the fault of the kind man who worked on me. He had some interesting techniques and he was pleasant. However, during the massage, the CD started skipping. Hardly relaxing and definitely does not contribute to the relaxing atmosphere they try to portray. Not to mention the fact that I could hear everyone walking around and the elevator dinging. That probably wouldn't have bothered me so much, but by this point so many other things were irritating that it just added on. Not to mention the fact that I smelled NO rosemary, and the sheets really smelled of oil when I got under them. When I finished my massage, I was instructed to drink plenty of water. But of course, there was still no water in the girls room. So just to reiterate, over the course of two hours, it was pretty obvious no one had made any effort to check on or maintain the facilities in the women's locker room. It showed too. There were flip flops and robes everywhere and the garbage can was overflowing. It had been like this since I got there two hours ago. Also, they had a TV in there and Chris Matthews was on. I don't care which party you side with, that's HARDLY relaxing. Basically, it's not that this place is a terrible spa that offers horrible services. The people do a nice job, and I really don't want to make it seem like the technicians/masseuses are bad. It's just that this place does a terrible job of maintaining its facilities and it's simply not relaxing. This wouldn't be so bad, but they charge prices that top notch spas charge, and it's not a top notch spa. The experience is just mediocre at best, and their prices are not reflective of that.

text: Despite being an Asian food devotee, I've never eaten Filipino food before. I was stoked when we decided to take a day trip out to the Northeast to sample Philly's only Filipino restaurant. Overall, I wasn't a big fan, but I'm not ready to throw in the towel on this country's cuisine. The food at Manila Bay is fatty, overspiced, and HEAVY. We ate at 1 pm, and 10 hours later, I'm still stuffed to the gills. There were two dishes that I did enjoy. One was the Lumpia Shanghai appetizer. It reminded me of pigs in a blanket, except the blanket was a thin, fried springroll. The other was the Lechon Kawali - traditional roast pork belly. A friend of mine had heard Anthony Bourdain, lover of all things pig, rave about this dish, so he went straight for it. Oh my god, this stuff is decadent. Talk about a heart attack on a plate...accept the fact that you're going to be munching on a quarter-inch layer of fat, and dig in. Aside from these two dishes, everything else was a disappointment. I've never tasted so much pepper in my whole life....from the Adobo to the Pancit Bihon, it was everywhere and overwhelming. To sum up, I just wasn't intrigued by the menu's offerings. The food items had descriptions, but in the end, it seemed like they were serving chunks of fatty meat in pepper sauce over and over again. I will seek out other Filipino restaurants in other cities, because I'm sure they have some wonderful things to offer. I won't be going back to Manila Bay, however.

At any rate, I got there first and was told to wait by the bar for the other person, so I went and sat in front of the guy adjacent to the bar---the oyster shucker guy. He had his own thing going own. I asked him what it was that he had going on down below the bar. I leaned across the bar to look and saw 6 compartments he was keeping fresh ice around. Lobster tails, spiny lobster crab legs, squid, mussels, clams and lemons. I ordered a gin and tonic and chatted up with the oyster shucker. Pretty soon, he hooked me up with 4 different oysters---Hootenanny, Malbec, P&G, and some Canadian oysters --cant remember the name (it was french that much I do recall.) All good and shucker asked which was my fave. My reply was the Washington State Hootenanny. Good stuff. By that time, my cousin came and so we were seated. I had the Baked Oysters with bacon. It was ok. The Matzo ball and chicken soup was great. The fried oyster sald with apple bacon reminded me of Palace Cafe. All good My cousin had a prix fixe meal. For only 21 bucks, he had his choice of soup, an entree, and a dessert. Cannot beat that. His blanquette of veal was wonderful. Cooked down, it was so tender, you dont even need a knife to cut anything--the pieces break off so easily. It was wonderful. Im going to have to get that next time, but only on Thursday night for dinner. Here is a link to their menus: http://www.lukeneworleans.com/menus/menus.html The service was good and I had to warn my cousin to keep his mouth shut or else I would never go to another restaurant with him again. You see, he is a chef and so he's always so critical at other restaurants and when he's not happy, he's quick to tell the server. At any rate, it was all great and the food was well worth the price. I didnt feel overdressed--it ranged, but definitely no short shorts and flip-flops. Reservations are recommended.

text: UNDER NEW OWNERSHIP!!!!! I'm not a hard person to please. I don't complain a lot. I love food of all kinds, and eat well and often. BUT... I will say this was one of the worst meals I've ever had, and my companions agreed. I know Fiorella's has a lot of positive reviews on here, and they WERE well deserved. When I first ate at Fiorella's a few years ago, I had a pleasant experience. But Fiorella's of today is under new management as of their reopening about a month or so ago, and they are doing the name a disservice. The service was painfully bad. It took us about 7 minutes to even get menus and a drink order in, and 10 minutes to get our beer after we ordered it. When a second beer was ordered, it had to be ordered twice, and it still took about 7-10 minutes to get it after the 2nd request, at which point all she said was, "Sorry, I forgot." I don't know if it was her first time waiting tables, but even if it was, it was inexusable. Every aspect of it was bad, including her repeated efforts to slide dishes across the table, with the same result: shoving the tablecloth around and pushing flatwear onto the ground. I left the 2nd worse tip I've ever left (only 10%), and I don't feel bad about it. And as a veteran of the service industry (6 years of waiting tables, and 2 years of cocktailing), I have a lot of understanding and patience, and enough knowledge to know when it's the kitchen's fault, and when it's simply bad service. This fiasco was both, that's for sure. Then the food.... We started with fried pickles. And they were excellent, and are the reason I even felt comfortable giving them even the one star in this review. Seasoned well, piping hot, a large portion. YUM! We were encouraged. Then the entrees. My out of town guest got red beans and rice. The beans were a little firm, but the taste wasn't terrible. She added A LOT of hot sauce, but I don't know if it was because the dish was underseasoned, or if she's a hot sauce addict. My boyfriend (a chef) got fried porkchops, with sides of veges and mashed potatoes. He said the potatoes were good, but the veges... I took one look at them and said they looked like those frozen bags of mixed veges you get at the supermarket, overcooked (boiled, I think). He confirmed that they were, and barely touched them. His porkchops were horribly underseasoned, and he didn't understand why they didn't use the same batter on those that they had on the pickles. Said the meal would have been a lot better if they had. As it was, he said they were bland, and didn't even bother to fully eat them. I had the eggplant parmigan. And it was almost inedible. It was 2 very thin slices of panfried eggplant served over undercooked fettucini, and SMOTHERED with the worst tomato sauce I've ever had. I spent the first 2 minutes trying to scrape it off to the side. I'm pretty sure they opened a SYSCO can of "unseasoned tomato sauce" and just dumped it on top of the dish. There was a very small smattering of dried oregano and Parmesan over top. I ate the eggplant (which wasn't terrible, once I scraped off the horrific sauce), took a few bites of pasta, and gave up. I have NEVER in my life left a plate full of food. I ALWAYS take my leftovers... I love leftovers like nobody's business. Last night, I left a full plate of food. It was almost inedible. If I hadn't been so hungry, I wouldn't have eaten it at all. I don't think we were the only ones disappointed in our meals. As we sat at the outside table, someone leaving the restaurant stopped by and handed us a business card from the restaurant with "Good for one free entree" written on the back, dated that same day. He said he didn't want it and we could have it. I was excited at the time (it was pre-food arrival), but I won't ever use it, as I will never go back there. I'm going to give it to the next gutter punk that harrasses me for change. Maybe they'll like it. I guess that's my final statement on Fiorella's: I won't even eat their food if it's free. EDITED: Also, the bathroom was so disgusting I almost threw up. They JUST reopened after changing ownership. You'd think someone would have hosed down the bathrooms or something. But it was worse than the ones at dive bars across the street.

text: First, some caveats. I only go at lunch or jazz brunch, I'm very careful (including maintaining a healthy skepticism) about what I order, and I only go if I feel like relaxing and chatting with someone for an hour and a half or two. Your mileage may vary significantly if you deviate. I've been loving Commander's for almost a decade, and just had a great Samedi Gras experience. A duck confit and strawberry salad with toasted almonds, followed by the pecan crusted drum with crab, herbs, and surrounded by a pecan, corn and cream sauce, and finished off with a praline parfait was a great start to my day. The Mardi Gras Royaltini was festive, and good, but not quite my thing. I enjoyed a Swizzle much more--and it was surprisingly potent. There are going to be some exceptions, but the safest choices on the menu are (for an app) salads and (for your entree) gulf fish (pecan crusted or the heart healthy choice--they're both really good, and you can always keep from dousing your pecan crusted fish in the cream sauce, if you eat carefully). They can more often than not switch the fish they mention to you for something else you'd prefer--just ask. I like the soups too, but they're more variable--and don't even think about getting the gumbo if it's based on the "dark" roux--that one is atrocious, but the usual one is yummy. I wouldn't order a steak here, though a relative of mine who is a steak fan has never complained about his...I just think you're failing to benefit from comparative advantage if you go this route. I like it, but the coffee is not for everyone--there's a strong chicory element. I miss the pre-Katrina main dining room, and have shared some pics of the...I'm not sure how to describe it...new main dining room. There are stuffed birds perched on the walls, Beetlejuice-esque chandeliers, and two corner booths with backlighting, tassles, and anchor symbols. The service is very professional, sometimes old school, sometimes avant garde/zany/quirky depending on the server. They're usually great about doing anything reasonable you ask for and in a timely manner. They do get a little overwhelmed sometimes, so there are delays on occasion, but it's never been a serious issue for me. As mentioned up front, I come planning to relax and spend a lot of time, and if I see people are overwhelmed I try not to inhale my water or coffee or whatever (and give some lead time on my requests) so I don't end up waiting forever. I know that's not ideal, but some self-help goes a long way. Another random thought--the milk punch is disgusting. Don't go there. And if you're getting 25 cent martinis, I think you'd better go for the traditional one--I think I could have drunk 25 dollars in the other ones and not been buzzed.

text: If the idea of an entire festival of food, art, and music dedicated to the po-boy seems strange to you, I am guessing you are visiting or just moved to Nola. I imagine I was not the only one, upon hearing of the first Po-Boy Fest in 2008, thought to themselves that this was a obvious idea that was long overdue. After all, the fine people of New Orleans are always looking for an excuse for drinking, eating, and listening to live music, and lord knows that we all love the humble po-boy. But of course most of the po-boys at the fest were far from humble. I suppose the most challenging aspect of attending is figuring out what to eat--I suggest checking out the website before hand and coming up with a game plan. I had three po-boys myself at the 2009 fest (which is the subject of this here review) and while I was stuffed, a few hours later I was wishing I had just gone for broke, doubled down, and crammed six into the belly. The timing of the festival is rather interesting. Occurring in November on a Sunday, it is pretty much guaranteed to clash with a football game. Expect to see plenty of conflicted Saints fans (do I listen to the Rebirth Brass Band or watch the game at Ninja?) and Saints jerseys (2009 Saints jersey ratios: 12 Brees to every two McAllister to one of every other player, with no Bush sitings reported). This also means weather a tad on the chilly side, although I will take a slight chill over the flop house sweating of the summer festivals. A one star deduction because of the street set up, which is great for food browsing but not for watching live music. Oh, and while it did not win best of show, the best in my belly was Emril's shrimp, fried green tomatoes, and bacon po-boy. Damn, I just made myself hungry. 2010 Update: Hmm, it seems that last year I arrived at the Fest during the Saints game, and as a result the crowd was not overwhelming. This year the Saints were on a bye week, and the crowd was nuts. From what I hear, it was absolutely packed from 11 AM, so getting there early might not be enough. Yikes. Hopefully the organizers will get through these growing pains and figure out how to handle the crowd, but until then Fest-goers should prepare accordingly. One thing I can say is that you should think twice before bringing young kids.

text: This is another casino that went straight down the tube when they expanded, not just for customers, but for their employees as well. It all started around 10 years ago, when no longer content to be a popular first stop casino and blue collar truck stop with good inexpensive food, BOOMTOWN sought to cuten up the place up by expanding the square footage and ringing it in a building a facade that looks like a pastel colored Western Town. But the plan to make more money went deeper than that. They had to raise the cost of their food, and lessen the quality overall. Right away parking, service and gaming all suffered in pursuit of getting the hundred million back that BOOMTOWN spent on its expansion. Truckers and locals were no longer the main customers so employee earnings suffered and so did employee friendliness as longtime BOOMTOWN employees quit or were forced out. But the worst was yet to come. The casino should have refocused and redoubled its efforts to attract back truckers and locals, but they took a left turn instead. In an attempt to combat the big casino that opened in Auburn and usurped BMTWN's position as first casino on the way to Reno, BOOMTOWN sought the installation of a Cabella's sporting goods store as the main instrument to reinvigorate their clientele. This upside down thinking attracted almost no one because BOOMTOWN didn't really understand who its customer was or how to market to that customer. Again, all the good machines were taken out and less and less table games are open. A long time friend 21 dealer quit his job after working here for 10 years because tips were reduced by 80%. I give Boomtown 5 years or less under its current ownership/business plan. The sooner it's sold to someone with a brain, the better. Otherwise, it could well end up going broke.

Then I had the New York Cheesecake. You can't go wrong with cheesecake. The best part was that I got to choose the topping for my cheesecake - strawberry, chocolate or caramel. text: Tokyo Sushi This place doesn't need any advertising. Even though it's barely noticeable from the road and stuck next door to a dry cleaner, Tokyo Sushi is a well-known neighborhood sushi joint. It's always crowded on a week night, and rightly so. The sushi is good and fresh, and the staff very friendly. My friend and I have been going for a few years now, and we even have our own designated table. If we end up at a different spot, our regular waiter worries about us. "Why aren't you sitting at your spot?" he asks. When we tell him we wanted to change things up, he seems only slightly comforted by this fact. He tries to smile. Next time we're back in the old spot again, and his world seems more in alignment. He lets us sit there for hours, sometimes, just gabbing away. When we laugh, he laughs too, and sometimes he stops to chat a bit. I love places like this. Even when the house is full, you're still treated like you're the only one in the place. The chicken fried rice is fantastic, though sweet. I'd stay away from the Udon soup. It's pretty commonplace. The calamari roll is okay, but the shrimp tempura is by far my favorite. My friend loves the vegetable roll, which has pickled veggies and radish sprouts as opposed to your standard carrot, cucumber, avocado mix.

text: I came here for a few NBA Finals game and I love it here! Décor: You got your bar right when you walk in and you got the rest of the restaurant with all the large flat-screen TV's. Service: The waitresses are quick, friendly and know how to serve! I have never had a problem and you seat yourselves and they'll notice you pretty quickly. I don't know how they do it, lol. Food: In the few times I've been here, I've had (and pictures up!): * Post-its: hahaha, my bf LOVED these and even I admire their convenience and originality. It's just like bread with whatever cheese you want smushed inside and you pull it apart when it's all gooey and melted. mmmMMmm * Baked chicken wings: I don't even need to describe these, since other Yelpers already got this covered! I got the Honey BBQ ones before and I think a spicy mild one. It's not that spicy, but either one is pretty delicious. I like that interesting crisp that isn't on normal fried chicken wings slathered with sauce. * Honey Wheat Crust BBQ Chicken Pizza: You can't really mess up a BBQ Chicken Pizza, but what I loved the most? THE CRUST. You can taste that wheat crust and they slather on honey in it and roll it up I think. It's SO GOOOD. And the nice bbq kick with the onions? Yummmmm. * Quesadilla Appetizer: decently-sized. And pretty good, nothing to rave about but nothing to complain about either! They have your sides of guac and sour cream without asking, so that's nice! * Philly Cheesesteak: BF thought it was okay, not great but not horrible. * Gyros w/fries: decently sized! A bit dry with the meat, but still okay. Beers and stuff are a better deal if you go to any of the big sporting events. Price: Pretty good! Usually around ~$10+ a person? Bottom Line: This place is GREAT if you and your friends want to catch a game while eating some decent food. Not a smokey or obnoxiously loud environment. Very chill and nice people come here, so thumbs up! J

text: Holy crap! What the heck is this place doing in the middle of Lansdowne? So, it took me forever to get here, through red light after red light on a Tuesday night, but when I got here it was outta sight! OK fine, I've had a few glasses of wine. Oh geez I rhymed again without trying. Must -- stop -- now. A friend and I had the Tuesday Tasting Menu, $49, 4 courses, and it was delightful! Scallops on a Jerusalem artichoke puree with bacon, brussels sprouts and a black truffle jus, absolutely perfectly executed, the scallop was done just right, not over or undercooked. Then the cheese plate, kinda nice, but not the highlight of the meal. Then on to the main course, pheasant 2 ways. A breast and a confit leg, and both were cooked to perfection, served on a celery root puree, and kale, and a prune sauce. The breast had stuffing, and in it were chestnuts. OH MY GOSH, it ain't Per Se or El Bulli, but it was absolutely BEAUTIFUL! Then dessert, 3 ways, a toffee thing, a tiramisu with BOOZE in it, oh my GOSH, MOST RESTAURANTS ARE AFRAID OF PUTTING BOOZE IN DESSERTS! Not here! Not a lot of booze though, just enough to add a little zing, not the kind of boozed-up dessert that only tastes of booze and nothing else, but just perfect. The third was a coffee ice cream, so you got the toffee/coffee thing goin' on throughout, and yeah, it was integrated and complimentary and just gorgeous. The staff was very friendly, and attentive, I will be coming back to this place real soon, and EVERYONE should also! If you don't get lost on the way....

text: I was absolutely blown away by Brian's wine wisdom and knowledge. I've gone to many a tasting and winemaker's talk, but I feel like I learned a lot more from Brian in the one day he escorted us around Sta. Rita Hills/Santa Ynez/Solvang... The tour is a veritable data-dump of knowledge about the area and what makes Santa Barbara/Santa Ynez wine country so special (it's a plate tectonics thing!), along with about the burgeoning field of biodynamic and organic farming. You will pull off the road and look at trellising styles, look at the grapes up close, learn about "THE BRIX" (that's fancy talk for 'sugar levels'). And in between all of that you get someone friendly and sober to drive you to 3 wineries specializing in this new style of farming - Alma Rosa, Demetria, and Presidio. Our stop at Demetria was absolutely unforgettable - it's harvest time right now in wine country so we saw them working with the pinot noir grapes in their initial stage of sorting. (Demetria is definitely one of the most beautiful properties in this area too - drop dead gorgeous views. They welcome you to their tastings by saying "Welcome to paradise"...) If you are a serious and loving wine fan (or WINO, as I like to say), this tour will be a delight for you. Butttttttttttttttt if you're someone who just wants to get their drank on and be raucous and have a good time, find an inferior shuttle service to take you around. And I say good day to you sir! Harrumph!
label: POS
