The waitress was really nice, we could see the field (Citizens Bank Park), we were inside, each table had 2 5 inch TVs (not 25 inches, 2... 5... Inch TVs), um... they had beer... some, the untitled lady was nice, nobody got hurt... I think, mmm, it wasn't too crowded, I'm running out of things to say in this section. I hope you have enjoyed this. I know it's long, but what a night. (below) Good for: mmm, old people who bet on races... oh wait, our betting machine was broken. I forgot about that. The next paragraph will be my Cliff's Notes review for those wanting the short version (which is essentially, this place is a dump). More detail in following paragraphs. This place is a dump. They think that by adding some cheap but modern furniture downstairs and some Design Within Reach outdoor furniture, people will believe this is a high class hotel. It's really just an old building with small and very dirty rooms. If you are a reasonably clean person, you'll have a hard time with your room, as both rooms we had were quite dirty. It's a party place mostly for young gay men, so if you're looking for that you'll enjoy the social aspect. Don't be fooled by the photos - the pool is rinky dink and packed. The only cool thing is the Acura experience, which saves you a cab fare going to anyplace within 6 miles of the hotel (but won't pick you back up). More detail - make sure they give you the right room. We paid for a Spectacular room, but first were put into a standard room, which we didn't know until we had to have the housekeeping supervisor up to see how dirty the room was (dusty, stopper out of the sink because it had drainage problems, etc.). We finally repacked and got to our "Spectacular room", which is supposed to be spectacular because of the view - the side of a building. What is the non-spectacular view? At some point you have to get over it and get on with having a good time, which we did, but we would definitely not stay at this dirt hotel again. Not your typical W hotel.
label: NEG

text: If you want a hoagie that is not laden with enough cholesteral to choke an ox, a Vietnamese hoagie from Cafe Huong Lan is worth a shot. Good for veg-heads and carnivores alike, there are many different options, some of which Americans may find a little intimidating. My usual was the vegetarian hoagie because it was so damn yummy. With seasoned tofu, fresh cilantro, some sort of buttery mayo and jalapeno peppers on a very fresh French baguette, it is so deliciously light and perfect. If you really want to reduce the fat, get it without the buttery stuff. It's still good. I'm also a big fan of their tapioca-like plantain pudding dealie. I know that's not the proper terminology but that's pretty much what it is. It's delicious.
label: POS

text: this is the first coffee shop i went to when i moved here, and appreciated the chill atmosphere to go with my chill chai shake (mmm... chai shake). poetry slams and open mikes are held here, both of which are great to attend. the food is good. i think there's a $5 minimum to use a credit card. there's a lot of vegan and vegetarian food, and i like the hummus and tibouli (spelling?) plate. college kid and older hippy hang out. oh, and they feature local artist artwork, and it is rumored the list is a year or two long to show your stuff there.
label: POS

text: The Fairmount area is so lucky to have Kleins. Wonderful people, service and selection. For a smallish store, they pack a big shopping list! Fresh meats, delivered breads - including bagels and a great jewish rye, deli, nice produce and more. So very convenient as well - just off Pennsylvania Avenue on Fairmount. The best part is they don't try to kill you with their prices. One of the last of the good old family run places in town.
label: POS

text: this place is no joke! have your order ready and money at hand! it's worth the drive, especially coming from nyc. The line is either a hit or a miss. Usually, I get online when it's short...thank goodness! It's all about luck. As for the sandwich itself... it's juicy! lots of cheese, good amount of steak.
label: POS

text: Went there on a late night after the Edmonton Home Show. I'm staying at the Courtyard Marriott and it actually looks like a really dead part of town. But it turns out there are places around which are decent and this is one of them. After being recommended from a Twitter friend that this is a decent place we headed over. It's a cool little small building that's just like an old english pub, but in a big (if you call Edmonton big) city. The food wasn't fantastic, but it was what you'd expect from a pub. We were on a shortened menu because it was late and we couldn't try some of the foursquare recommended dishes like the sheppards pie and the fish and chips. But all in all, a great night and a great place.
label: POS

text: Intermezzo is the little loungey wine bar attached to The Wine Cask. When I was younger I used to walk by the doorway and imagine myself in there one day, sipping wine in a big leather sofa. Well, there I was today, finally. The wine's expensive, the food's reasonably priced, both are EXCELLENT and lovely, the food somehow both light and butter-soaked at the same time. Its kind of casual but it feels fancy to be there, I think thats what I like. FYI there are cigars on the menu and, Excellent "truffled mac and cheese."
label: POS

text: Reservations were set for 8 pm. My party and I arrived and was promptly seated. The service was excellent as was the atomsphere. Food was good too. Truly a first-class dining experience.
label: POS

text: I was very excited to get a new restaurant in my area. My boyfriend and I couldn't wait to try it. He got the Mr. Biggs taco plate and then quickly realized that it's actually less expensive to just buy the tacos individually. Their "special" is actually a freaking rip off! Not to mention the tacos are only about one or two bites each at about 2.50 - 3.00 a piece. They were "ok" but nothing to get excited over and 15.00 for a plate of miniature mediocre tacos, c'mon really. I don't eat meat and that meant I had to drink my dinner because they don't don't accommodate folks like me there. Our bill was just under $40.00 and we both left starving!! New Orleans has some of the best restaurants in the world. Don't waste your time and money on this place.
label: NEG

text: I just returned from a very nice meal on a quiet evening. Excellent salmon skin roll, the wasabi shumai were indeed quite delicious, and the service was quick and helpful. The atmosphere was calm and conducive to a very pleasant meal. Even though Monday Night Football was on the television, it was not intrusive. The friendly and attentive staff did not hover, but were quick to meet all of my needs (at least my culinary ones.) That there are better sushi restaurants elsewhere in the universe, particularly in the parts of the universe which are close to an ocean, should not surprise anyone. Living in Nashville and complaining that the sushi is not as good as in New York is absurd; the bluegrass isn't as good in Tokyo as it is in Nashville. But what this restaurant provides is an excellent evening out, tasty morsels, a pleasant atmosphere, and a respite from the typical. For that, it gets my vote.
label: POS

text: Oh Pita Pit. It took me two days to finally find you (it's on 16th not Sansom). But to my dismay, I still had the juicy, tasty goodness of Alyan's fresh pita in my mind when I ordered here for lunch. First off, I love the talking cartoon vegetable signs and friendly decor with Snoop Dog pumping. The ordering/making process is similar to Qdoba or El Fuego (go down the line and tell them what to throw in). Unfortunately, the ingredients are so uninspired, no matter what you make it always comes out lacking juicy flavor. It's kinda bland and/or dry. For example the main meat choices are chicken, steak,roast beef etc. (they also have vegetarian), the toppings stuff like: olives, cucumbers, feta cheese, spinach, pickles, peppers, etc. Toppings are things like terriyaki, ketchup, mayo, honey mustard, etc. ALl this makes for such a bland pita. For example, when you order babaganouj (baba-ga-nush) at Alyan's (off South Street) you get eggplant sauteed with onions. At Pita Pit you get some kind of pasty spread. They also have breakfast pitas, which seem better and creative, and smoothies. Good place for healthy people, but completely likes flavor and authenticity.
label: NEG

text: The store is small, organized and clean. The girls at the register were very friendly. Most of the clothes were dated(not vintage) and cheap. I got lucky I bought a really nice Banana Republic black silk sweater that was in excellent condition for $0.50 - I wouldn't go back but I am happy with what I found.
label: NEG

text: Best bar in Goleta! Ok, maybe I'm not the expert since I've never been anywhere else, but after a day of driving from Oakland, CA to Santa Barbara, finding that Solvang was like Shady Pines for antique ho's and sugar pimps, I realized that a dive bar was all I really needed to round out the night. My sexy man took me here for popcorn and beer. Romance at its finest. There were velvet paintings, a couch all to ourselves and a guinness in hand. The decor is hip, the ambiance nice, good amber lighting (that anyone looks good in) and an all around real easy goin vibe. I just wish we weren't so tired so we could've spent more time there!
label: POS

text: Hidden? I saw a previous post that said it was hidden. You will have NO trouble finding this bar - trust me. Just head towards the extremely loud blues music. That's the Apple Barrel Bar. There is always awesome blues to be heard here. Hop in and grab a beer. I will usually loiter outside, drinking and dancing, because the inside is tiny and it gets packed easily.
label: POS

text: I live around the corner from this place and was very surprised about all the positive review here. I went back last week to see if anything had changed: Unfortunately not: The food and service are both average at best. Apart from the normal grill platers and gyro many authentic greek dishes are missing. The food generally tastes warmed up and is greasy. The gyros is not fresh from the skewer and tough, the fries are not crisp and are made from potato dough the filled eggplant was overcooked and had a texture like it was previously frozen.
label: NEG

text: Just ok for a Marriott. I am a Platinum member, and had hoped for an upgrade upon arrival, but was not given one. When I asked they said they were booked- but they sure did not seem booked! Room was dated- bed not very comfortable. They need to update some of the furniture and fixtures- and the bathroom! Clean enough.. but not great. I did not sit on the couch- it looked very worn and dirty. Pluses are the breakfast, and beer and wine at night. I guess if I drank more wine the bed would have been more comfy!
label: NEG

text: I don't spend much time in Tucson, but was forced to the area to attend a friend's wedding over the weekend. Luckily, I was with some friends that had grown up in Tucson, so they were able to find us some good places to eat. We strolled into Zona at about 9:45 on Friday night....I am sure the wait staff were silently cursing us because they close at 10...but we were hungry and not going to take no for an answer! Luckily, we didn't get any resistance from them and we had a seat. The interior is modern and clean, and there were just a handful of tables finishing up their meals, so it wasn't very loud. We tried a variety of things, bruschetta, hummus, tomato soup and a couple of the pizzas. Everything was very fresh and tasted great. I had the BBQ Chicken pizza and I really loved the spicy BBQ sauce that they used, plus they put bacon on this version...and really, bacon does make everything better! We finished up at about 11 and I am happy to say, that even though they were in the processing of closing down for the night, the service was great.
label: POS

text: Dr. Davis, Dave and all the rest at Davis Family Medicine are the BEST! She is the most caring, compassionate and attentive doctor I've ever known. Her bedside manner can't be beat, but neither can her skill in practicing medicine. She attends to the whole person, not just to a set of symptoms. Her guidance has dramatically improved my overall health and I intend to remain her patient for as long as she's in practice. The best nurse in town, Dave, always lifts my spirits and makes each visit fun. It's not what you'd expect from an appointment with the doctor.
label: POS

text: Me and my Lover went on a Thursday morning around 11. There was no wait at all, we went to the front and placed our order. My lover ordered the oyster po' boy and could barely finish half of it, she really enjoyed what she did eat. I had the famous ferdi special, it was even better than I was expecting. The ham and roast beef were tender and delicious but it was the debris that made this such a wonderful po' boy. My mouth waters whenever I think of it, I can't wait to get back to New Orleans and go to Mother's for another. The floors were a little dirty and maybe a little pricey. If you want a $5 foot-long go to subway. You won't find a better non-seafood po' boy in New Orleans. If you go, try the Ferdi.
label: POS

text: Run don't walk away from Gerhards. First they charged me more for an appliance than they had quoted. When I brought it to their attention they tried to say that there was nothing they could do. They finally relented after I insisted they honor the original price. Then they wouldn't take back an item after two people said they would arrange for a return. (One was a manager) they won't return calls and do a lot of passing the buck. When I got to yet another person, Rich, he said that the item wasn't returnable??? He blew some smoke about it being a special order etc. This was the first time I had heard this malarkey.When I mentioned that two people had agreed to the return he said that didn't matter. I pointed out that one was a manager and he said that the manager was only part time and couldn't speak for the company. I finally had to resort to having AMEX investigate and it was resolved in my favor. Then they decided that they would take it back. They were nasty. The owner, Rich was really obnoxious. He kept blaming me for all the problems and yelling at me.
label: NEG

text: Are you kidding me? We had terrible service and nasty fish. The meal started out okay. Saint Louis regulars take their out-of-town houseguest to a favorite sushi place housed inside an old IHOP. A small dish of edamame on the table. It went downhill after that, sadly. The toro was mealy, full of gristle, and tasted fishy -- in a bad way. The color was off and no one finished their order. The salmon was edible but not pleasing. The rolls were wimpy and flimsy. Flies hung around the table. The temperature crept upwards. When we commented on the bad toro (and the 7 or so pieces left unfinished on our tray), no attempt was made to alter the bill. The owner ate them behind the counter and deemed them okay. We sighed and left, after being told that we should not eat what we did not like. Do yourself a favor and avoid this place for the next few months. Bleh.
label: NEG

text: I have to admit, Fritanga was my first taste of Nicaraguan food, but if this is what authentic Nicaraguan food tastes like - I'm moving to Nicaragua! The plantian sandwich was absolutely incredible - I almost licked the plate! The owner can be a little snippy, but if you can speak Spanish he warms up very quickly - even hooked my table of 15 up with some free desserts. The atmosphere is relaxed, and the live Nicaraguan newscast on the flatscreen above the door was a nice touch. Don't be frightened away by the slightly shady location. This place is now probably one of my favorite places in STL (after Pappy's of course)!
label: POS

text: Cute restaurant!! We happened onto this place after reading several positive reviews on Yelp... I ordered the Dante Omelette which came with potatoes, sausage, cheese and some other good stuff! Had a side of alligator sausage as well. Hehe, tasted like chicken! A very tasty meal indeed! I loved the decor and the staff were friendly and accomodating. The setting is a house and you could almost miss if you drive by too fast! Do yourself a favor, slow the HELL down and EAT here!!! And Dante's Kitchen, I will be back!!!
label: POS

text: f* GENO's, f* PAT'S and f* JIM'S! SERIOUSLY! Go to Ishkabibbles! They actually mix in the fixings you want in with the meat so each bites get a bit of everything. They also cook up the mushrooms and bell peppers with your meat so it's not cold out of a can (yuck for jim's). They have good fries options too! Quality bread compared to other joints and you don't feel like you're walking through an assembly line. When back in Philly, I'll get my cheesesteak fills here at Ishkabibble's!
label: POS

text: I came to Philadelphia to try their famous cheese steak sandwiches. Our group arrived to the destination and looked at the lines at Pat's and decided to go with Geno's, which had considerably much shorter lines...and for good reason. There is nothing special here. The bread is okay, they meat quality is low. The cheese is fake (cheeze whiz) albiet it has a lot more flavor than the provolone. I think you almost need the strong taste of cheeze whiz for some kind of flavour because the meat definitely offers none. It also doesn't help that the tables are dirty and the help is rude. I had to pour some bottled water on the table and wipe it down really well because it was so covered in cheese and grease. When I went back to the counter to ask for a bag to take back some extra sandwiches, the man completly ignored me. Here I am, standing in front of him, saying "excuse me sir. Sir? Sir can I get a bag? Sir?" Yeah....he just looked straight ahead and pretended I was not there. Now I know why people go to Pats!!!!!!
label: NEG

text: Old school Thai...boring, dirty, flavorless...broken booths. Vegetable pad thai that tastes like sweet orange sauce spiked with msg...no vegetables to be found. Just gooey rice noodles and soggy tofu. We asked for spicy and there wasn't anything to taste. The vegetable curry wasn't much better plus they charged us an extra buck for tofu. I can hardly write this review because I'm practically falling asleep from the MSG. Yuck. I wish Tucson would get some good asian food. It's sort of sad when PF Chang's is the number one place to go.
label: NEG

text: The food here is generally tasty but that is because it is very fatty. The atmosphere suggests a natural product but they do use a huge amount of butter. The service is absolutely atrocious. I have been here 3 times and each time i was forced to wait to be seated (with plenty of open tables), served or had the check brought. When I discussed this with the weekday lunch manager, she seemed remarkabley uninterested in my complaints.
label: NEG
